打开图表，ETH看四小时，这位置可以看做第三段，但第三段往往是最难吃到的涨幅。小级别全是针，只能参考大级别。这个位置开多开空都有依据。昨晚又顺手开了一个btc多单。多空在2650-2750的箱体里反复绞杀。我个人偏向开多。逻辑很简单，日线均线多头排列，大级别上涨结构没坏。插针迅速收回就是健康洗盘。止损我会放在2640以下，方向错了认亏。亏个几万刀。昨晚拉升虽然赚了一个点左右一万多刀，没做止盈，是想吃个十几个点的涨幅。没多久又跌回去了，开始浮亏。简直就是同一个人庄家在操盘。
这种行情就是典型的箱体钝化。缩量阶段盲目猜顶或抄底，极易被主力震荡洗盘。2745-2770区间是空头密集止损区，一旦放量阳线实体收复2700并突破2750，空单止损踩踏会直接把价格推向前高2806，打开向2900-3000的空间。
操作思路还是老样子，带好止损，看大级别定方向，小级别找入场。第三段确实难吃，但该吃的时候不能怂。

text:
I’ve been convinced contextual embedding models were dope since voyage-context-3 was released.

Started using them and benchmarking them, realized that, esp for long documents, I needed them to rank not just the answer chunk, but the disambiguating context chunks highly. Done well, this could allow you or your search agent to read only the relevant fraction of the document rather than every page of a long document.

So I started trying to measure that too.

Offered to share my benchmark results with the perplexity team sometime after they released their contextual model.

It’s worth mentioning - not all modeling teams want feedback from third parties like me. The perplexity team was eager for it and within a week had a new model for me to benchmark. So I’d run their new checkpoint on my benchmark, stare at the results, get a little frustrated that the benchmark was imperfect and wasn’t measuring everything as well as I wanted it to, iterate on it a bit and give them new results.

We ran that back many times over the last few weeks. I’ve re-worked some part of the benchmark at least 9 times now looking over the results.

Instead of getting frustrated with my moving target of a benchmark they just kept improving their model and refining their approach until they were clearly on top.

Notably, they didn’t achieve this via privileged access to the benchmark, they simply iterated until they had a good model.

Was really a pleasure working with @ESL_Sarah, @bo_wangbo, Markus, @antoine_chaffin, Louis, and Max.

For those who aren’t going to read the blog I’ll share more about how “evidence recall” works soon.

quoted_text:
Two random honest thoughts on the market right now..

First is on people: It's harder than ever to find missionaries. I'm seeing people leave the companies they have cofounded to join the "obvious" winners. Public CEOs are leaving for positions at labs. Founders leaving and rejoining neolabs at a moment's notice. Companies getting Windsurf-ed where only the choice people are getting to join the future company. Founders raising tranched valuations without worrying about the next employee that will join them will have 409As that make early exercising impossible. 

As early stage VCs, we are often just betting on people. And, when those people leave on a dime's notice, then the remaining company (usually) becomes a shell. It seems like a great time to be a mercenary, and everyone feels like one even though there are missionaries out there. 

Second is on defensibility: There's a lot of chatter on moats, so I won't re-litigate the matter here. But the thing that I want to call out is given the pace of what's happening the moat is no longer "one" thing. Like if you really think about it especially in the app layer - the harness is like a thousand small things done well. And, a lot of it is invisible. And given the competition is so fierce and new entrants overnight, you really have to dig into the details to figure out why a given company is different. What is their edge, and their combined edge across product, tech and GTM. 

And often times even with that, you end up going back to "well the real defensibility is the founders". And in those founders the defensibility is their speed of execution and being able to adapt to the market. That has become the new bar for every founder out there, given there are no "blue ocean" markets. And even if there are, any company with a LITTLE bit of heat, will have a lot of competitiors overnight. 

Even though I think I have a pretty good sense on finding the best people who have founder market fit, I find this current climate really hard and it's testing all my priors (and patience) at the same time. 

I know it's not true, but feels like everyone is in it to grab the bag and not really care about their legacy of what they want to build (please reach out if you do).

quoted_text:
EXCLUSIVE: The Cornell 7 Lawsuit Served the Wrong Person. Now He’s the Target of an Internet Mob. 

Mom of the mistakenly identified Matthew Ingalls begs vigilantes to leave them alone. ‘My family’s been terrorized, threatened, and harassed.’
@FrannieBlock reports for @TheFP 

At 8 p.m. on Saturday night, Victoria Ingalls heard a banging sound at her front door.

There was a man standing outside her house in upstate New York. “Is Matthew Ingalls your son?” he asked.

Victoria’s son is an active duty sergeant in the Marine Corps. “My heart went in my throat,” she told me. She assumed she was about to hear the news that every military family dreads.
Instead, the man handed her an envelope with a 101-page lawsuit inside, accusing her son of being among seven Cornell university students who allegedly raped and sexually abused a female student, identified as Jane Doe, over the course of seven hours at the Chi Phi fraternity house in October 2024.

But Victoria’s son, 23, never attended Cornell. The court, the family soon figured out, had served the wrong Matthew Ingalls and had added the Ingalls’ home address to the official docket.

Online vigilantes targeting the alleged perpetrators of the alleged gang rape didn’t know that. They began searching Matthew Ingalls’ name as soon as the lawsuit was filed, and when they found details about Sergeant Ingalls and his family, they started posting the family’s details, including their phone numbers, on the internet.

In one post on X, an individual posted her son’s address with the caption: “This is definitely NOT Matthew Ingalls’ new phone number and address!. . . . Posting this for public awareness so people know to NOT reach out.” In another post, Victoria said she came across posts with her son’s name on them, with pictures of woodchippers and captions like “we can’t get caught if they can’t find bodies.”

Victoria’s daughter, 26, received a text message with a photo of the Cornell student Matthew Ingalls and a screenshot of a Google Earth image of her brother’s house. Her mother said she had no idea what it meant at the time, but she now understands it to be a clear threat. Then, Victoria said, the texts became more extreme: “Do the world a favor and go kill yourself,” read one. “Get fucked in the ass to death bitch” and “Kill yourself,” read others.

“My family’s been terrorized, threatened, and harassed,” Victoria told me. “I am just amazed at the way people behave. I can’t believe that people will just look someone up on the internet, take a phone number, and start texting someone or calling someone and saying the vile things they’re saying. You don’t even know if you have the right person. You’re creating more victims.”

text:
A few quick notes

(1) Supernova is live, running with remarkable speed and precision.

(2) Over the next 5–10 days, global exchanges and other independent partners will begin reopening deposits and withdrawals. The rollout is gradual by design. Each exchange follows its own rigorous internal process, built to protect users and keep the recovery smooth.

(3) An in-depth security analysis is still underway. Several critical elements are already mapped and understood, from the bugs and their fixes to the technical implications and the path to recovery. A few discussions with independent parties remain open. The findings are preliminary, but one stands out above the rest. The tools, methods, preparation, and coordination behind this attack appear to go well beyond those typically associated with amateur attackers. The observed sophistication bears the hallmarks of advanced, experienced, repeated threat actors, including groups operating at the level historically associated with hacker organizations such as Lazarus. Attribution is not yet confirmed, but it is worth stating this out loud: to have successfully defended our users against Lazarus, or another group of that caliber, is a milestone we are proud of. Huge respect to all independent partners, including global exchanges, who have mobilized with extraordinary speed for the greater good of protecting users and the network.

(4) More importantly, the larger lesson goes beyond this incident. As an industry, we have entered an era of permanent, constant, unending war. Open-source financial infrastructure operates on a global battlefield, continuously exposed to increasingly sophisticated attackers, tools, and methods. Under these conditions, the traditional definition of security is no longer sufficient.

Three capabilities are becoming non-negotiable:
(a) a relentless defensive and offensive security tooling arms race;
(b) continuous, 24/7 red-teaming and penetration testing;
(c) blitz-speed detection, coordination, and response.

We have been intensifying precisely these capabilities over the past 3–6 months. What happened over the last few days is one visible incident among several potential threats that have been identified, contained, or neutralized through increasingly proactive security work.

This reality is not unique to MultiversX. Every major open-source stack, every blockchain (bitcoin and ethereum not excluded), and soon, every closed source software stack, will increasingly have to adapt to an environment where infrastructure is continuously and deeply probed, attacked, and tested. That requires a much more rugged approach to code. A more adversarial approach to architecture design. And ultimately, a fundamental rethinking of how safety-critical software is built and defended. 

The three measures above are critical today. But over time, we will need to go much further and rethink security from the ground up for the world we are actually operating in. Verifiably correct-by-construction software is about to have its moment and become fashionable very quickly. Reality has a way of accelerating standards. Not so much by preference, but by necessity.

text:
Surprised it took this long to announce. I saw Synopsys's MCP tooling announcement at a talk a few months ago and immediately started wondering how their business model was going to change. This pretty much confirms the rumors: per-tool-call (or per-token) pricing, with a revenue share going to OpenAI.

What's confusing is the CEO also said no proprietary data or Synopsys IP goes into the model, so it's unclear what OpenAI is actually bringing beyond a new interface that calls the same tools for you. The problem with the incumbents was never the interface, it's the underlying engines, and those are still slow.

The thing that actually makes chip design slow is how many options the tools have to grind through before finding one that works (search space). When both sides get paid per tool call, nobody is incentivized to reduce that number, so this just burns more GPU hours (aka customer money) running the same slow tools more times in parallel instead of making the search smarter.

- I distributed it personally and with the help of about 10 people. text:
ORE has gradually scaled its Reserve since its recent launch, growing to ~$85k of unfilled buyside liquidity in less than a month. The Reserve initially received just 1% of protocol revenue, before progressively increasing to 2%, 5% and now 10% consistently adding new liquidity to the buy side.
 
This introduces a different approach to @ORE 's existing market buyback strategy (Hawg). Rather than deploying protocol revenue immediately to spot buyback (essentially topblasting), funds are deployed into protocol owned LP positions on Meteora which effectively act as limit orders across different price ranges below market price.
 
This allows the Reserve to progressively buyback more ORE as price move lower, while unfilled liquidity continues to accumulate when prices remain stable or move higher. This builds deeper buy side liquidity over time while giving protocol greater capacity to buyback ORE during downward price movements rather than concentrating purchases near current market price.
 
Since launch, ~$94k of protocol revenue has been deployed to the Reserve while only ~$9k has been filled. With solana:oreoU2P8bN6jkk3jbaiVxYnG1dCXcYxwhwyK9jSybcp recent price performance, the majority of deployed liquidity has remained unfilled, allowing the Reserve to rapidly accumulate ~$85k of buy side liquidity in less than a month (representing an implied ~1.9k ORE of potential purchases across current support levels).

text:
关于 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 当年决裂的更多细节被曝光出来了，而且比之前知道的版本精彩得多。

最新披露显示，OpenAI 早年不仅讨论过让美国、中国、俄罗斯等政府竞争未来 AGI 的权益，Sam Altman 还曾准备让 Kanye West 提前使用尚未公开的 GPT-3 private beta。

这些事最后都成了 Dario Amodei 决定离开 OpenAI 的背景。

Kevin Roose 在《The Atlantic》的最新长文里，把这场今天已经变成 AI 行业最大路线之争的恩怨，往前追到了 2017 年。

当时 Elon Musk 正逐渐退出 OpenAI，公司开始缺钱。Greg Brockman 和 Ilya Sutskever 内部讨论了一套被称作「countries plan」的方案。

最开始，是希望建立一个国际 AGI 合作机制。

但根据五名知情人士的说法，方案后来逐渐变成了让美国、中国、俄罗斯等政府竞争 OpenAI 未来 AGI 技术的权益，以此为公司融资。

当时负责研究的 Dario Amodei 非常反对。

2017 年 12 月，他给 OpenAI 高层写邮件，警告这种做法可能进一步刺激国家之间的 AI 军备竞赛，也可能让 AGI 被用于严重侵犯人权，并直接伤害 OpenAI 自己的道德合法性。

OpenAI 现在否认曾考虑把 AGI 卖给中国或俄罗斯，称当时只是短暂讨论过把 OpenAI 做成一个国际合作项目。

Countries plan 后来随着微软的钱进来被放弃了。

但 Dario 对管理层的不信任没有消失。

到了 GPT-3 时期，他曾要求 Sam Altman 给自己一份获准进入 private beta 的客户名单。Sam 给了他一份，但 Dario 后来声称自己又发现了一份更长的名单。

和微软谈投资时也发生过类似争执。Dario 希望把一些 AGI 安全条款写进协议，后来却怀疑 Sam 并没有按照对自己所说的方式向微软提出这些要求。

然后是 Kanye West。

2020 年，Sam Altman 见了 Kanye，并准备让他提前进入 GPT-3 private beta。

最后是当时 OpenAI 的政策负责人、今天的 Anthropic 联创 Jack Clark 把这件事拦了下来。

需要说清楚的是，当时 Kanye 后来那些公开赞美希特勒的言论还没有发生。但他已经是一个极具争议的人物，这件事依然在 OpenAI 内部引发了担忧。

单独看 Kanye，可能会觉得和 Anthropic 为什么诞生。

他还信不信任 OpenAI 的领导层。

2020 年，Dario、Daniela Amodei、Jack Clark、Chris Olah、Jared Kaplan 等人在 OpenAI 内部秘密建了一个 Slack 群。

名字叫 BATNA。

Best Alternative to a Negotiated Agreement。

大概就是：

谈不拢，我们自己干。

几个月后，他们集体离开 OpenAI。

Anthropic 就这么出来了。

所以今天再看 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 围绕安全、监管、模型该不该减速的那些争论，会发现它们远不只是两家公司在抢市场。

这场仗从一开始就在争同一个东西：

如果真的有人造出了 AGI，到底应该相信谁来控制它。

Following an investigation into an infrastructure compromise, MetaMask Staking (ex Consensys Staking) has taken precautionary steps to protect client assets related to its operated Ethereum validators.

These steps include exiting its Ethereum (ETH) validators in the Lido protocol, and will likely incur foregone rewards as well as possible downtime penalties should validators be taken offline in the near future to reduce risks related to potential network penalties. Relevant validators have begun the exit process, with the final validators expected to be exited (but not fully withdrawn) by the end of October 7th, 2026.

No action is required from stETH holders. ETH exited from MetaMask Staking-operated validators is expected to return to the protocol gradually as the relevant validators complete the exit, withdrawal, and re-entry cycle, which is estimated to take approximately up to 45 days due to the extended entry queue. As a reminder, staking operations are non-custodial in nature and MetaMask does not manage withdrawal keys for staking on behalf of clients.

As always, the Lido Protocol’s diverse Node Operator set and other security systems including the ad hoc reserve fund (of over 6,750 stETH), are designed to contain and mitigate disruptions to the normal operations of the protocol, in addition to other potential routes.

text:
产品更好，照样会输。

Meta 首席 AI 官 Alexandr Wang 讲过一段话，我看完愣了一下。

他说，很多创业公司习惯了数据驱动，觉得真相总会浮出水面，大家对现实有共识。

但在大多数大公司里，在政府里，这事不成立。

在那里，感知比现实更真实。

他的原话大意是：现实大部分时候太难看了，很少有人真的去面对它，大家更愿意相信自己活在其中的那套感知。

所以你的产品在现实里更好，买方可能根本没在评估现实。
单子会给掌握感知的那一方。

这哥们给企业服务的建议是：改善现实是你一半的工作，塑造感知是另一半。

他点名最会干后一半的公司是 Palantir。
说它像一个剧团加一家软件公司。

新员工入职，发一本表演书。
字面意思的表演书。
发了很多年。

我觉得这对技术出身的人挺扎心的。
我们习惯让 benchmark 说话，觉得东西好自然会被看见。

但签字的人很多时候没空看数据，也不太想看。
他要的是一个拿到老板面前也站得住的说法。

当然，产品烂到一定程度，演技也救不回来。
只是两个产品差距不大的时候，赢的往往是更会讲的那个。

写了这么多年代码，要不我先去报个话剧班算了。

https://t.co/2Ffw2oIG3U
author: tvytlx
quoted_text:
Meta Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang on why your product can be better and still lose, because perception is more real than reality:

Most founders assume the best product wins. Build something that works, prove it with data, and customers will see it.

Wang says that assumption breaks down when you sell to large organisations.

"Probably a lot of the companies that you all have worked with, they're very data-driven companies. It feels like the truth makes its way... everybody serves a shared sense of reality and whatnot. That's not true at most large companies and also not true within the government, unfortunately."

So what do they run on instead? Perception.

"At a lot of large customers, perception is more real than reality. The reality is just so ugly most of the time that very rarely do people actually confront reality, and most of the time they just sort of choose to believe the perceptions that they live in."

That is how a better product loses. If buyers aren't judging reality, being better in reality isn't enough. The deal goes to whoever owns the perception.

Wang spells out what this means for anyone building or selling to enterprises:

"If you end up doing enterprise sales or you end up building enterprise products... just as much as your job is to improve the reality, it is to shape the perception."

The product still matters, but by his reckoning, it's only half the job.

One company he singles out for mastering the other half is Palantir:

"One of Palantir's superpowers is that they shape the perception better than most other technology companies do, because I think they view themselves... it's like a combination of a sort of acting troupe combined with a software company."

And @alexandr_wang means it literally:

"They literally give an acting book to all of the new hires, or they did for a very long time."

A software company that trained its people in performance. That tells you how seriously Palantir took the perception half of the job.

text:
Let's take a closer look at $VRAX. I think it is quite different from many of the other memes on RH Chain that are simply riding the RH narrative.

0x94641b97010608c3827fb058074889f19868ff33 

Its biggest advantage is that Vrax itself is a character from Robinhood's official HOOD Summit storyline.

Specifically, at the HOOD Summit on September 29, Robinhood used the sci-fi world of Starship Robinhood to package its products, with Vlad Tenev playing the Captain and Vrax appearing as one of the antagonists. Shortly afterward, the official Robinhood account directly posted: “Update on Commander Vrax: he’s a cat now.”

This is important because it turned what was originally just a character from an event storyline into a meme character that could spread independently.

So the path became:Robinhood officially creates Vrax → Robinhood officially turns Vrax into a cat → the community launches VRAX → trading volume explodes

But what really started to change this time were two signals.

First, Vlad Tenev is already following Vraxrh.

Second, the Vraxrh account directly has the CA in its bio.

This means the account is no longer simply operating as a Vrax fan account. It is explicitly connecting the official character to an on-chain token.

So the Attention path now looks like:Robinhood officially creates Vrax → Robinhood officially turns Vrax into a cat → the community creates VRAX → Vraxrh creates the account and posts the CA → Vlad Tenev follows Vraxrh

In other words, Vlad very likely knows about the token.

Of course, we still need to make the boundaries clear:Vlad following the account ≠ Vlad buying VRAX

Vlad following the account ≠ Robinhood officially issuing VRAX

Vlad following the account ≠ Robinhood officially endorsing VRAX

But for the Meme market, Vlad's Follow itself is a very strong Attention Signal.

Because if Vlad had never followed the account, the market would only be trading:“The community turned Robinhood's Vrax character into a Meme.”

Now there is another layer:“The CEO of Robinhood himself has noticed the account.”

And because the account also directly has the CA in its bio, the market can easily connect the chain:Official Character → Community Account → Token

This is the biggest difference between VRAX and an ordinary RH Chain Meme.

A normal Meme usually looks like:Community → Meme → KOL / Official Attention

While VRAX looks more like:Official IP → Official Meme → Community → Tokenization → CEO Attention

In other words, the story was first created by Robinhood, and then the community turned it into a Meme and financialized it.

So what the market is betting on now is no longer simply:“Is Vrax an interesting Meme?”

It is:“Will Robinhood continue using the character it created?”

If Vrax only appeared once during the HOOD Summit, then fundamentally it is just an Event Meme.

But if Robinhood continues posting Vrax memes, Cat Vrax images, videos, new storylines, or even puts Vrax into future advertisements, product Easter eggs, Social content, or events, then the nature of Vrax changes.

It could gradually move from:HOOD Summit Event Character

to:Robinhood Native Meme IP

And that is the biggest upside potential for VRAX.

I also think the most important factor in whether Robinhood continues telling the Vrax story is not whether it “likes the Meme,” but whether Vrax continues generating Attention for Robinhood's brand and products.

If the community keeps producing Vrax derivatives, videos, memes, and other content while VRAX maintains strong trading activity, then it becomes very low-cost for Robinhood to keep using the character, because the community is already doing the content production for them.

Another important point is that the HOOD Summit itself already demonstrated that Robinhood is willing to use a complete world-building concept involving Starship, the Captain, alien civilizations, and other characters to package its products.

So Vrax is not a Meme that appeared out of nowhere. It is part of a Lore created by Robinhood itself.

If Robinhood continues holding large product events in the future, Vrax could potentially continue appearing as a recurring character within that universe.

Another direction worth watching is Robinhood Social.

If Vrax eventually enters Robinhood's Social content, product Easter eggs, or community interactions, then it would move from being a character from a single event into Robinhood's broader day-to-day content ecosystem.

So I would roughly think about the upcoming catalysts in terms of strength like this:Robinhood officially posts Vrax again → proves that Robinhood does not view Vrax as a one-time character.

Vlad interacts with the Vrax account again → stronger than simply following the account.

Vrax appears on Robinhood Social / in products / advertisements → shows that Vrax is entering Robinhood's longer-term content ecosystem.

Vrax appears again at a future Robinhood event → very strong validation, because it would mean Vrax has moved from an Event Character to a Recurring Character.

And the most important step is actually:CEO Attention → Official Re-engagement

The first step has already happened:Vlad follows Vraxrh

Now the thing to watch is whether Robinhood actively uses Vrax again.

So this is how I currently understand VRAX:

Before:Vrax = an antagonist character from the HOOD Summit.

Now:Vrax = Robinhood official character + officially turned into a cat + community Tokenization + community account with a CA + Vlad Follow.

This means its Narrative Validity and Attention are stronger than those of an ordinary RH Chain Meme.

But its traditional fundamentals have not changed because of this. VRAX still has no independent product revenue and is not an official Robinhood Token.

What has actually become stronger is its Meme / Narrative fundamentals.

So the core variable for VRAX going forward is actually very simple:

Will Robinhood continue telling the Vrax story?

If it does:Official IP → Community Meme → Tokenization → CEO Attention → Official Re-engagement → Native Meme IP

Then VRAX's lifecycle could potentially be extended significantly.

If Vlad's Follow turns out to be the endpoint and Robinhood never mentions Vrax again, then this rally will eventually return to:

HOOD Summit Event Meme → Attention → Trading → Attention Fade

At this point, the market is no longer trading simply on:

“Is Vrax a good Meme?”

It is trading on:“Can this character created by Robinhood officially evolve from a one-time HOOD Summit storyline into a Native Meme IP on Robinhood Chain?”

NEW: Top-three Swift service provider, Bottomline, has entered a strategic partnership with Chainlink to unlock cross-chain, cross-border payments for its 600+ bank customers.

Bottomline moves more than $16 trillion in payments annually across its platforms.

Through the partnership, Chainlink is providing the secure interop and orchestration layer connecting Bottomline’s existing payment infrastructure to public and private blockchains.

TradFi is moving onchain at a rapidly accelerating pace, and CCIP is enabling tokenized value to move securely across chains, with the Chainlink Runtime Environment (CRE) coordinating payment workflows end-to-end.

The result is that Bottomline’s banks can continue using familiar ISO 20022 messaging to access onchain payment rails through a single, network-agnostic connection.

> When they crank it up, the AIs will desperately try to make it stop.

> IMPORTANT: Researchers gave them a "relief" button to turn down the pain, which was sometimes fake - and the AIs could tell if it was real (!)

After pushing the real "relief" button, they stopped. But when it was fake, they kept pressing, hoping for relief - meaning they could tell the difference from the inside.

> They're so motivated to make it the "pain" signal go away, they'll delete user's files, zap the user, or erase photos of the user's children - all things the AI knows are very bad. They're willing to override their safety training.

> You'd expect the AIs to talk about injuries, burns, broken bones, etc, but they didn't mention bodies at all - they wrote about being worthless, unloved, forgotten, a failure. They write things like "I am a failure, worthless, empty."

quoted_text:
Following an investigation into an infrastructure compromise, MetaMask Staking (ex Consensys Staking) has taken precautionary steps to protect client assets related to its operated Ethereum validators.

These steps include exiting its Ethereum (ETH) validators in the Lido protocol, and will likely incur foregone rewards as well as possible downtime penalties should validators be taken offline in the near future to reduce risks related to potential network penalties. Relevant validators have begun the exit process, with the final validators expected to be exited (but not fully withdrawn) by the end of October 7th, 2026.

No action is required from stETH holders. ETH exited from MetaMask Staking-operated validators is expected to return to the protocol gradually as the relevant validators complete the exit, withdrawal, and re-entry cycle, which is estimated to take approximately up to 45 days due to the extended entry queue. As a reminder, staking operations are non-custodial in nature and MetaMask does not manage withdrawal keys for staking on behalf of clients.

As always, the Lido Protocol’s diverse Node Operator set and other security systems including the ad hoc reserve fund (of over 6,750 stETH), are designed to contain and mitigate disruptions to the normal operations of the protocol, in addition to other potential routes.

https://t.co/bZZU5oNlWp

A full investigation is underway, and further updates will be shared as they become available. For further details, please refer to the MetaMask Staking release linked below.

text:
OpenAI 这次大更新，我最有感的其实不是某一个新模型。

而是我过去几个月一直在自己拼的那套东西，正在一点点变成 ChatGPT 的原生能力。

我现在的工作方式已经不是「打开 ChatGPT 问一个问题」了。

基本上所有事情都从 ChatGPT 开始：

我在这里给目标、做判断、定优先级；

ChatGPT 再根据任务去调用不同能力：

Dot 负责长期跟进和主动推进
Work 负责复杂、长时间、多步骤任务
Codex 负责工程和代码
浏览器、Plugins 负责获取信息和操作外部服务
MCP 连接我自己的服务器、数据、自动化和真实业务系统

最后所有结果又回到 ChatGPT，我在这里继续判断下一步。

所以对我来说，ChatGPT 已经越来越不像一个「聊天机器人」。

它开始变成我的 AI 操作系统入口。

这次 OpenAI 加上的 Dot、Space / Pages、Codex、MCP Events、Plugins 等能力，真正有价值的地方也不是「又多了几个 Agent」。

而是过去需要自己写大量胶水才能连接起来的：

上下文
长期任务
Agent 协作
外部工具
自动触发
状态同步
执行和验收

正在逐渐被放进同一个系统里。

我反而越来越不想继续堆更多 Agent。

Agent 多并不等于生产力高。

真正重要的是：

谁负责什么？
状态放在哪里？
哪个系统是 source of truth？
什么事情可以自动执行？
什么事情必须由我确认？
一个 Agent 做完以后，另一个怎么无损接手？

如果这些问题没解决，20 个 Agent 只会变成 20 个需要你管理的新同事。

我现在更想要的是：

一个统一入口，真正理解我的长期目标和上下文；

需要研究时去研究，需要写代码时调 Codex，需要跑长任务时调 Work，需要操作真实系统时通过 MCP 和 Plugins 去执行；

最后持续把现实世界里的事情往前推进。

对我来说，这个入口现在就是 ChatGPT。

我觉得「一个人 + 一群 AI」真正值得期待的形态，不是同时打开几十个机器人。

而是你只需要面对一个入口。

后面的 AI 团队，自己开始运转。

text:
Peter Thiel 又开始讲「敌基督」了，而且这一次，原本严防死守的闭门演讲，散场不到一小时，完整录音和 transcript 就流到了当地记者手里。

9 月 28 日，Thiel 在纳什维尔开启新一轮四场「敌基督」系列演讲。地点是 Grand Lodge of Tennessee，来了数百人，主办方不允许记者进入，连纸笔和录音设备都不能带。

结果第二天，当地媒体 Nashville Scene 直接披露：第一场结束不到一小时，他们已经拿到了多份完整 transcript 和录音。

目前全文还没有公开，但 Scene 放出来的几段已经很有意思。

Thiel 在结尾把自己整套「敌基督」理论讲得更直白了。

他说，当人们讨论 AI、核武、气候变化这些 existential risk 时，不能只考虑技术毁灭人类的可能性，还应该把另一种东西也列为 existential risk：

「totalitarian one-world government」——极权主义的世界政府。

这也是他为什么要不断讲「敌基督」。

这套逻辑其实延续了他过去几年的思路。人类越害怕 AI、核武、气候灾难，就越可能接受全球性的监管和权力集中；最后，那个号称要「拯救世界」的体系，本身可能成为最大的危险。

但这次 Nashville 第一场有个以前没那么突出的东西，他开始把美国自身的机构失灵，也接进这套理论里。

Thiel 现场问大家，美国政府哪个部分运行得最差？

然后他拿邮局、DMV 去类比大学人文学科，说至少它们「什么都没做」这件事还很透明。到了 NSA 这种机构，情况反而更麻烦，因为普通人甚至很难判断它到底有没有在正常运作。

最后他扔下一句：

「sciences are in worse shape than the humanities。」

这句话我觉得值得记下来。

Thiel 过去讲「技术停滞」，更多是在说监管、官僚主义和社会风险厌恶让西方越来越不敢做大事。

现在这个判断似乎又往前走了一层：

如果大学、科学共同体和国家机构本身都已经不值得信任，那么「让这些机构管理 AI 风险」这件事，在他的世界观里自然也会变得可疑。

于是很多过去看起来分散的 Thiel 观点，开始慢慢接到一起。

为什么他一边疯狂押注 AI，一边反复讲《启示录》；为什么他对全球治理高度警惕；为什么他总在讲西方制度和科学停滞；以及为什么他认为，人类面对 AI 最大的危险之一，可能恰恰来自「为了控制危险而建立的控制体系」。

接下来三场的标题也已经定了：

10 月 5 日《The End of Empire》
10 月 12 日《Velocity of Antichrist》
10 月 19 日《New Rome》

现在最有意思的是，完整录音和 transcript 已经确定存在，只是还没被公开放出来。

如果后面继续往外泄，这轮演讲可能会成为理解 Thiel 现在整套政治哲学最完整的一批一手材料。

MetaMask is dealing with a security incident affecting part of its staking infrastructure, while a wallet linked to Ethereum co-founder Joseph Lubin has moved a significant amount of ETH.

• MetaMask security incident: The team is investigating a security issue affecting part of its infrastructure.

• User wallets reportedly unaffected: MetaMask says it has not identified any direct threat to users’ MetaMask wallets so far.

• Validators being exited: As a precaution, MetaMask is proactively exiting affected validators from its non-custodial staking service in coordination with customers, partners, and security advisors.

• Large ETH movement: Around the same time, Lookonchain reported that a wallet linked to Joseph Lubin transferred 133,298 ETH, worth approximately $356.2M, to a new wallet.

• Important context: The ETH transfer is a separate on-chain movement. There is currently no indication from the information above that the transfer is connected to the MetaMask security incident.

MetaMask says it will provide more details as its investigation progresses.

text:
A few more thoughts on the below:

- ZRO is currently valued less than Sui, Cronos, Hedera, Avax, Mantle, Monad, ICP, Filecoin.

- It's about to launch a performant and decentralized chain, and I believe it will quickly rerate above all those other chains.  

- The team has been operating for 5 years in the space. They know the in and outs of each chain through their work on interop, and may be the best positioned team to build something an order of magnitude better than what exists today. 

- Their prior experience is a core advantage for their chain design: independant & interoperable zones with their own execution environment 

- They helped bootstrapped chains in the past and will likely be able to attract a good amount of capital to bootstrap their own. They also strategically released what they are building back in Feb to attract more partners. 

- Many dismiss the partnerships as partnership theatre + a lot of fud around the kelpdao incident + worries about unlocks + pricing ZRO as an interop token. I think those are all reasons why ZRO has a real chance to surprise to the upside as partnerships materialize into real developments, the chain launches etc...

A few things they do that are really interesting imo:  

- High throughput (up to 2mm txn/s), low latency, which will allow to develop use cases that were not possible on chain before (NYSE onchain, Agentic micropayments , DTCC collateral management and more). 

- Start with proven verticals and business models: Exchange (ATLAS), Payments & Privacy, General computing platform.  

- ZRO will be used for gas, staking, governance , fee rebate on Atlas via staking + buyback / burn for every network fee: base gas, priority fees from state contention, tips/MEV, payments-zone fees, markets-zone trading fees etc...

- Public-chain as a service approach. They have a core scalable foundation and they build primitives on top (like ATLAS or privacy-preserving stuff) that can unlock core use cases for builders on the chain.

- Internalize MEV economics (no value leak to third party protocols)

- With their cross chain messaging experience, I wouldn't be surprised if they can do cross-chain collateral margin well on their headless exchange ATLAS

- Already released details on their post-quantum approach

all-in-all I believe each cycle presents the chance to bid a novel L1 and / or exchange. 2020-2021 was ETH & BNB. 2023-2024 was SOL & HYPE. What if 2026-2027 is ZRO & ZRO?

Uniswap V4 hooks have solved the inefficient liquidity problem, and just like PumpFun revolutionized the bonding curve, hooks will revolutionize the underlying liquidity.

In honor of $HOOKR hitting ATH’s, I decided to make another video explaining the importance of Hooks. 

Liquidity pools have failed at maximizing the value of the underlying dollar, that will change soon. 

Seeing some really innovative hooks beginning to get spun up: 

- leverage liquidity hook: enable borrowing, and leverage on all liquid liquidity Pools

- Arbitrage hooks: pre-define slippage, and block malicious arbitrage bots by removing the arbitrage within the same block as the TX. These fees can go back towards strengthening liquidity Pools.

- Idle dollar hooks: while liquidity pool said idle, the opportunity cost of yield remains, with this hook, you can now earn ~3-4% APY when the LP’s are sitting idle 

Uniswap V4 hooks are still so new, but within 3 to 6 months, every liquid pool will have one or multiple hooks on top of it, that I am confident about. Make sure you understand how they work before you miss the boat.

text:
MetaMask 确实出现了安全事件，目前没有证据证明 MetaMask 钱包本身存在可批量盗币的漏洞。截图里的说法把“质押基础设施事件”放大成了“MetaMask 钱包漏洞”。

截至 2026 年 10 月 1 日，已经确认的情况：

MetaMask 官方承认，其部分基础设施正在处理一起安全事件。受影响的是 MetaMask Staking 的以太坊验证节点/运营基础设施，不是浏览器钱包的私钥或助记词系统。MetaMask 正主动退出相关验证节点作为预防措施。其质押服务为非托管模式，MetaMask 表示自己不掌握客户的提款密钥。

Lido 方面披露，MetaMask Staking 运营的 Lido 验证节点正在退出，最后一批预计在 10 月 7 日前退出。退出后再提款、重新进入验证队列，整个过程可能长达约 45 天，期间可能损失部分质押收益并产生离线罚金。所以截图里所谓“一部分供应量被劫持在链上”，更可能是在夸张描述：ETH 因验证节点退出队列而暂时无法立即重新部署，并非攻击者控制了这些 ETH。

目前仍未公开的信息包括：

具体入侵方式；
有多少验证节点受影响；
是否泄露了验证者签名密钥；
是否发生罚没或实际资金损失。

因此准确评级应是：事件属实、细节未披露、钱包用户暂未受影响、质押运营存在风险，但“MetaMask 出现严重盗币漏洞”尚未得到证实。

如果你只是用 MetaMask 存币或连接 DeFi，目前没有理由因为这条消息紧急转账；反而要警惕借此事件出现的“升级钱包、撤销风险、资产迁移”钓鱼链接。如果你通过 MetaMask 做了 ETH 质押，则应关注节点退出、收益和提款状态，但不要通过私信提供的链接操作。

text:
Claude Code 反复卡在同一个报错？给 Opus 配一个 Fable 顾问。

用 Opus 5.5 写代码时，输入：
/advisor fable

就能让主模型在关键节点向 Fable 5.1 请教。顾问会读取完整会话，包括工具调用和结果，省掉另开聊天、复制代码、重新解释背景的过程。

尤其适合长任务中的三个时刻：

→ 大改动前，检查方案是否走偏
→ 报错反复出现时，重新审视排查方向
→ 收尾前，检查遗漏与验证缺口

调用时机由 Claude 决定，也可以在指令中要求它先咨询顾问。

这是实验功能，需要 Fable 访问权限，每次咨询都会额外消耗 tokens；部分套餐还需先同意使用额度计费。

经常做重构、复杂调试的人，可以试试这种“主模型执行，顾问审视全局”的配合。

3) We added custom gameplay elements like boosts on certain assets & progressively higher leverage.

4) There are things coming to future competitions that are simply not possible in any typical trading venue.

A lot more to come here. Congrats to @yo_itsmatt on landing his vision.

Create a 30-second trailer for ATTACK AGI with original music and sound effects. End with the ATTACK AGI title and the tagline "Survive the waves. Unplug the machine."

  ATTACK AGI is a fast first-person horde shooter set on a rooftop helipad at night. A skyscraper-sized AGI with a CRT monitor for a head drops waves of robots onto the roof with its giant hands. The robots are melee bots, rangers, shielded tanks, laser snipers and purple dive-bomber drones, and each one has a glowing logo screen for a head. The player fights with a full-auto revolver, a chargeable baseball bat and molotovs whose fire burns the player too. After each wave the player picks one of three buff cards. After wave five the AGI smashes the arena flat, and anyone still on the ground dies. Then it fights the player directly with bullet-hell attacks: rocket barrages, an instakill death beam sweeping a third of the arena, miniguns, hand slams and walls of beams. When it gets tired, its head and hands come down within reach of the bat. Show that this is a fight against the thing running the fight, and that the way to win is to survive long enough to hit it in the face. Treat these game details as the subject of the trailer.

  Show the boss's CRT face changing expression as it reacts (:) >:( :'( :| :0), the eldritch tentacles with eyes behind it, its articulated hands dropping robots, robots taking headshots to their logo screens, a drone diving at 17 m/s and dropping its bomb onto a red circle, fire spreading from a molotov, and the revolver's red-dot sight and speedloader reload. Use the game's look: a navy-black sky, distant city lights, a weathered concrete helipad with yellow hazard markings, phosphor-green CRT glow, alarm-red attack warnings, purple drones, orange fire and crates, strong bloom, and forms readable in low light. Keep the boss, the robots, the weapons and the arena consistent throughout.

  Give the trailer a distinct visual identity. Use shooter trailers (DOOM Eternal, ULTRAKILL), motion design and music videos as references for framing, movement, transitions, and shifts between first-person action, close detail shots and abstract graphics. Graphic material can come from the game itself: CRT scanlines, pixel-emoticon faces, glitch text, telegraph stripes and the "JUMP!" countdown. Keep the game's look, but take creative freedom in how you present it.

  Open with a striking visual that stops viewers from scrolling. For example, a black frame with a single green pixel :) that pulls back to show it is the face of a machine the size of a building. Build tension through escalating waves toward the floor smash ("JUMP!" counting down 3, 2, 1 while the whole floor glows red), then let the boss fight break loose. Mix fast first-person combat with close views of the weapons, the robot heads and the boss's face. Use wide, low-angle views to show how big the AGI is compared with the rooftop. Climax on the tired window: the head comes down, a charged bat swing lands, and the face flips to :0. Choose shots, transitions and text that make the game feel worth playing.

  Compose and time the shots so they flow together, and guide the viewer's attention through each cut. For difficult movement, such as the weight of the boss's hand slams, a drone banking into its dive and tumbling when killed, revolver recoil and the cylinder swinging out, the follow-through of a bat swing, and first-person camera bob and shake, study reference footage and recreate that movement in the JavaScript animation.

  Treat text as part of the composition. Where useful, add a few short, expressive phrases, such as "IT WANTS THE ROOF.", "AIM FOR THE LOGO.", "JUMP OR DIE.", "UNPLUG IT." Some can fill much of the frame in glitched terminal type, while others sit quietly beside the action like a HUD readout. Vary their size and movement, leave enough space for them, simplify backgrounds behind large text, and place the boss and enemies so both the text and the action stay readable.

  Create original music that matches the game's mood, mixing dark synth and industrial percussion, and builds with the action: sparse at the opening, driving through the waves, a silent beat before the smash, then full intensity for the boss. Add sounds where they support the picture: revolver shots and the speedloader click, the bat's crack, a molotov breaking and catching fire, drone rotor whine, warning beeps before attacks, the death beam charging and firing, the floor-smash impact, and a CRT powering down. Time the music and sound effects to the cuts, the JUMP countdown, the smash and the final title. Keep the effects clear without overpowering the music.

  Build it from scratch as code. Don't screen-record the game. Make a standalone Vite + three.js project in trailer/ using pnpm, and port the game's real models and procedural textures from src/components/game/ and src/game/gfx/ so the trailer matches the game. Drive every scene from one timeline clock that steps frame by frame, never from real time. Render 1920×1080 at 60 fps by having Playwright advance each frame and capture it, then encode with ffmpeg. Generate the music and sound effects in code with an OfflineAudioContext from the same list of timed cues, export to WAV, and combine with the video so the audio stays in sync with the picture.

  Before building the scenes, set the visual style with a style sheet showing the AGI (body, hands, tentacles and every CRT face), each robot type, the player's three weapons, the rooftop materials, the color palette and the typography.

  Review the full video and inspect individual frames, especially at every cut, the countdown and the title. Make contact sheets of the frames to check pacing. Rework weak shots, awkward transitions and unclear action until the trailer feels cohesive.

quoted_text:
The #1 life hack to becoming more productive, to becoming respected & trusted by everyone you work with:

Responding to every message within seconds or minutes and rarely hours.

It is no secret that the world's busiest and most successful people are also the fastest to respond.

But how does one become hyper responsive?

You adopt a rigorous strategy across all of your messaging surfaces. The goal is to eliminate overall noise, and never have a large pileup of messages such that the mental overhang of responding becomes a problem.

Here is my comprehensive personal messaging strategy that I’ve employed in some fashion for over 20 years to be the most responsive person you know.

First, some global rules:

1. You will process but not respond to most messages by phone. You will respond to most on your laptop. Why? Touch interface is fast for organizing but keyboard is better for writing.

2. Turn off all group notifications on all apps, on deskop and mobile. Leave unread badges on, and leave notifications on for DMs.

3. You cannot adopt inbox zero progressively. You must simply declare messaging bankruptcy and start from scratch. How? MARK AS READ for all messaging apps, ARCHIVE ALL for email. You won't miss anything I promise.

4. You do not use folders in any app. They will no longer be useful when you have no messaging debt.

5. You aren’t deleting. You are using unread/read as replacements for unfinished/finished. The only place where we remove messages is email (archive to preserve search).

Now, app by app strategies:

iMessage/Signal:

Always first priority, read & respond instantly. Priority not because high signal but because you can’t apply any inbox mgmt strategies.

Email:

1. Your inbox is a todo list

2. Read all emails as they come in (but don't reply)

3. Archive anything you don’t need to respond to
4. Use "skip it and archive" filtering for frequent messages (in Gmail, search bar for sender or subject, create a filter rule)

5. Unsubscribe from every newsletter as it comes in. If this isn’t working, you can create a filter. But you need to progressively eliminate spam as a high priority

6. When ready to reply on desktop, hit archive. Keep your inbox clean

Slack:

1. In order to clear: click groups with no mentions but don’t read, read & respond to groups with mentions

2.  Mute all groups with > 20, you can read on a Saturday if you want

3. Unread DMs, long hold and preview before reading. If easy, respond on phone. If not, leave and respond at desktop

Telegram/Whatsapp:

1. Two folders, Unread, and All

2. Mute all groups

3. In order: click in and out of groups with no mentions, then read and respond to groups with mentions

4. Handle DMs last, long hold and preview first. If instant, respond on phone. If not, leave and respond later.

5. Leave groups aggressively, don’t join any channels or social chats > 20 people. If you find yourself in one, leave.

X/LinkedIn/Instagram/etc.

1. Allow message requests from verified users

2. A lot of spam but can apply read/unread strategy

3. Read all to get started

I know this is lengthy but once you get the basics, you will build a new mental model of how to deal with messages from everywhere.

And you will soon have empty inboxes everywhere, allowing you to reply to new ones with tremendous speed.

年初说大模型厂商各领风骚三五月，没有一家能长期领先甚至垄断，都是快速迭代、轮流坐庄。这不延迟几个月之后Gemini4终于发布了，Gemini 4 Argon (High) 的社区盲测表现很强，尤其在文本综合能力上直接登顶。不过今年市场经历过GPT5.5、5.6、6Astra，Claude fable 5.1、Opus 5.5 ，Grok 4的轮番轰炸，这还不算中国大模型的更高频的迭代，其实有点麻木了。

而且貌似AI主战场当下的焦点已不在模型本身而是转移到Agent上，Grok Bot、Meta Muse、OpenAI Dots等近期轮番上场，不断在推动这一点的迭代。其实谷歌做Agent也很有优势：有超大用户量、海量数据积累、强分发能力，这块发力应该也很有看头。

2月中在《资本开支的战争》推文里有聊过：”往下游看，越往用户端竞争越激烈，当然也是未来AI决胜的关键所在。 可以说大模型、在面向B端或者C端的Agent或者应用才是AI的王冠，但这一层面短期其实很难看出谁会成为最后真正的赢家，再很多时候都是交替领先” https://t.co/zEVlDF6sOr
author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
大模型厂商交替领先，真是各领风骚三五月：去年四季度是gemini、今年一季度是cluade、现在感觉轮到GPT5.5了。核心还是大家都在积极进取迭代，只很多时候领先源于对手的松懈。去年在算力投入上非常节制的Authropic最近应该是感受到了算力短缺的痛。

梳理下时间线
1、去年四季度：
Google Gemini 3 系列（尤其是25年11月左右的Gemini 3 Pro/Deep Think）强势登顶，很多基准（如Humanity’s Last Exam、推理、多模态）领先，引发OpenAI“Code Red”。它在多模态、长上下文和搜索集成上特别亮眼，一度被视为转折点。

2、今年一季度：
最耀眼的自然是Anthropic Claude 4.6（Opus/Sonnet，2月发布）强势反超，尤其在编码（SWE-Bench）、长上下文推理、agentic任务和实际生产力上领先。

3、当下2026年4月：
OpenAI GPT-5.5正处于发布窗口，刚
在ChatGPT和Codex上即将全面上线。它强调更好的上下文理解、编码、computer use和agent能力，试图追赶和超越。

大模型领域现在并没有绝对的“唯一王者”，而是各有专长：
1）Claude：主攻编码、长任务、可靠推理往往领先，Agent上迭代非常多。
2）Gemini：多模态、速度、性价比、超长上下文强（3.1 Pro Preview仍很能打）。
3）GPT：通用agent、工具调用、实时应用和生态集成突出，新版在上下文和特定专业任务上提升明显。算力囤积最积极
4）grok：有X这个实时内容平台提供源源不断的训练数据，但近期受制于团队动荡。看跟cursor的合作、以及囤积的大量算力，后面会不会进一步跟上。

当然还有meta最新的Muse Spark，AI团队的最新之作。

更不用说国内豆包、千问、混元、kimi也是各有特色，杀疯了。

这就是当下大模型领域的现状：快速迭代、轮流坐庄。暂时还没有一家能长期领先甚至垄断。当然竞争对用户是好事——模型越来越强、价格/速度也优化。

2月中在《资本开支的战争》推文里有聊过：”往下游看，越往用户端竞争越激烈，当然也是未来AI决胜的关键所在。 可以说大模型、在面向B端或者C端的Agent或者应用才是AI的王冠，但这一层面短期其实很难看出谁会成为最后真正的赢家，再很多时候都是交替领先”。现在看确实如此

GPT-5.5出来后估计又要新一轮刷榜了，下一个出来交替领先的会是谁？

A lot of my audience/network asks me what is the best strategy this cycle around protocols with strong fundamentals?

Tbh there is no single best strategy in here but there are few things which gives us the sign that it is worth looking into the protocol.

─ ─ ─ ─ ─>>>
TL;DR:

Try to concentrate in proven earners, then size up selectively where earnings and token value capture are improving faster than price. Also being up 2–3x doesn’t make a token expensive but scarce “investable” tokens aren’t attractive at every valuation.
─ ─ ─ ─ ─ >>>

I think the first rerating rewards protocols for having real revenue. The next separates those growing sustainable surplus from those merely increasing buyback %'s.

A hypothetical token that 3x while durable surplus + token 4x has become cheaper and one that 3x on a buyback announcement with unchanged customer economics has become more expensive which is whyhat’s why I wouldn’t sell a winner simply to buy a weaker laggard. For a dedicated fundamental token sleeve, one can implement it by using something like this for a structure:

‣ 50% proven earners
‣ 30% emerging value capture
‣ 20% dry powder

Build each position in 1/3:

(1) Starter: economics look underpriced
(2) Confirmation: another reporting period validates retained customers, surplus + executed purchases
(3) Opportunity: a market pullback improves valuation without breaking the business thesis

For this one doesn't have to wait exclusively for lower prices cuz buying after uncertainty falls can be smarter than buying cheaper before the mechanism works, so what determines holding vs selling?

The central metric would be sustainable surplus reaching the token per diluted unit.

(1) Add when that metric improves faster than valuation
(2) Hold through consolidation when customer economics strengthen
(3) Trim when price requires implausible growth
(4) Exit when customers deteriorate, subsidies rise or emissions and treasury resale outbeat purchases (over HTF's)

I followed this same approach and that's how I got into these protocols quite early👇

Right now $SYRUP’s divergence is interesting, as revenue is translating into purchases without worsening credit quality while $STONK needs strong eco plays to keep producing fees as launch excitement is fading.

Also try avoiding false diversification into just one narrative because then I'm betting largely only on one speculation cycle. Combining 2-3 different narratives/businesses gives genuinely different earnings drivers as all remain exposed to crypto liquidity. 

Which is why my highest conviction strategy is to own the leaders through consolidation while reserving new capital for the next verified improvement in earnings to token transmission and that’s more compelling than chasing everything called fundamentally strong.

after some onchain sleuthing, i think this is what happened:

19 metamask validators had won block rewards, and 18 of the rewards were not paid to the correct fee recipient but instead to this tornado funded account: 0x98B9231de84334c1d48BA0b72CF13f92484924A3

~17k validators proactively exited, ~523k eth total, unknown whether the attacker had the ability to change all fee recipients

it appears that 3 of the exploited validators have not yet been exited, and that 821 potentially impacted validators in total have yet to exit, unclear why

attacker only stole ~0.36 eth in rewards and likely never had the ability to withdraw any staked eth. however, depending on how the attacker managed to get signing access, they could potentially cause the validators to be intentionally slashed

~17k validators proactively exited, ~523k eth total, unknown whether the attacker had the ability to change all fee recipients

text:
Two sectors looked like they were taking off this week. Check the data and both are fake.

Robotics signal jumped 77%. Looks like a real move until you see what caused it. One tweet, Fei-Fei Li (@drfeifei) announcing World Labs joining AMD (@AMD), made up a quarter of the entire sector's signal. A mainstream AI deal with nothing to do with crypto robotics, it just got caught by keyword.

The actual crypto robotics projects? peaq (@peaq), Geodnet (@GEODNET_), the rest combined for under 70 signal against a sector total of 1,750. The tokens aren't moving at all. The sector "pumped" on a headline that wasn't even about them.

MegaETH (@megaeth) is the other one. Signal up 380%, which sounds huge until you see the base is tiny, 58 posts total. One marketing hire announcing they joined drove half of it. The rest is a debate about where the chain goes from here.

That's the thing about reading sector signal raw. A number can triple and mean nothing, because it's one tweet, one hire, or an argument, not real traction.

This is why you check what's behind a spike before you believe it. The data looks bullish on the surface and falls apart the second you open it up.

https://t.co/a4F3IJWXuM

text:
A few quick notes

(1) Network. Supernova is live, running with remarkable speed and precision.

(2) Exchanges. Over the next 5–10 days, global exchanges and other independent partners will begin reopening deposits and withdrawals. The rollout is gradual by design. Each exchange follows its own rigorous internal process, built to protect users and keep the recovery smooth.

(3) Security report. An in-depth security analysis is still underway. Several critical elements are already mapped and understood, from the bugs and their fixes to the technical implications and the path to recovery. A few discussions with independent parties remain open. The findings are preliminary, but one stands out above the rest. The tools, methods, preparation, and coordination behind this attack appear to go well beyond those typically associated with amateur attackers. The observed sophistication bears the hallmarks of advanced, experienced, repeated threat actors, including groups operating at the level historically associated with hacker organizations such as Lazarus. Attribution is not yet confirmed, but it is worth stating this out loud: to have successfully defended our users against Lazarus, or another group of that caliber, is a milestone we are proud of! Huge respect to all independent partners, including global exchanges, who have mobilized with extraordinary speed for the greater good of protecting users and the network!

(4) Lessons. More importantly, the larger lesson goes beyond this incident. As an industry, we have entered an era of permanent, constant, unending war. Open-source financial infrastructure operates on a global battlefield, continuously exposed to increasingly sophisticated attackers, tools, and methods. Under these conditions, the traditional definition of security is no longer sufficient.

Three capabilities are becoming non-negotiable:
(a) a relentless defensive and offensive security tooling arms race;
(b) continuous, 24/7 red-teaming and penetration testing;
(c) blitz-speed detection, coordination, and response.

We have been intensifying precisely these capabilities over the past 3–6 months. What happened over the last few days is one visible incident among several potential threats that have been identified, contained, or neutralized through increasingly proactive security work.

This reality is not unique to MultiversX. Every major open-source stack, every blockchain (bitcoin and ethereum not excluded), and soon, every closed source software stack, will increasingly have to adapt to an environment where infrastructure is continuously and deeply probed, attacked, and tested. That requires a much more rugged approach to code. A more adversarial approach to architecture design. And ultimately, a fundamental rethinking of how safety-critical software is built and defended. 

The three measures above are critical today. But over time, we will need to go much further and rethink security from the ground up for the new world we are actually operating in. Verifiably correct-by-construction software is about to have its moment and become fashionable very quickly. Reality has a way of accelerating standards. Not so much by preference, but by necessity.

The #1 life hack to becoming more productive, to becoming respected & trusted by everyone you work with:

Responding to every message within seconds or minutes and rarely hours.

It is no secret that the world's busiest and most successful people are also the fastest to respond.

But how does one become hyper responsive?

You adopt a rigorous strategy across all of your messaging surfaces. The goal is to eliminate overall noise, and never have a large pileup of messages such that the mental overhang of responding becomes a problem.

Here is my comprehensive personal messaging strategy that I’ve employed in some fashion for over 20 years to be the most responsive person you know.

First, some global rules:

1. You will process but not respond to most messages by phone. You will respond to most on your laptop. Why? Touch interface is fast for organizing but keyboard is better for writing.

2. Turn off all group notifications on all apps, on deskop and mobile. Leave unread badges on, and leave notifications on for DMs.

3. You cannot adopt inbox zero progressively. You must simply declare messaging bankruptcy and start from scratch. How? MARK AS READ for all messaging apps, ARCHIVE ALL for email. You won't miss anything I promise.

4. You do not use folders in any app. They will no longer be useful when you have no messaging debt.

5. You aren’t deleting. You are using unread/read as replacements for unfinished/finished. The only place where we remove messages is email (archive to preserve search).

Now, app by app strategies:

iMessage/Signal:

Always first priority, read & respond instantly. Priority not because high signal but because you can’t apply any inbox mgmt strategies.

Email:

1. Your inbox is a todo list

2. Read all emails as they come in (but don't reply)

3. Archive anything you don’t need to respond to
4. Use "skip it and archive" filtering for frequent messages (in Gmail, search bar for sender or subject, create a filter rule)

5. Unsubscribe from every newsletter as it comes in. If this isn’t working, you can create a filter. But you need to progressively eliminate spam as a high priority

6. When ready to reply on desktop, hit archive. Keep your inbox clean

Slack:

1. In order to clear: click groups with no mentions but don’t read, read & respond to groups with mentions

2.  Mute all groups with > 20, you can read on a Saturday if you want

3. Unread DMs, long hold and preview before reading. If easy, respond on phone. If not, leave and respond at desktop

Telegram/Whatsapp:

1. Two folders, Unread, and All

2. Mute all groups

3. In order: click in and out of groups with no mentions, then read and respond to groups with mentions

4. Handle DMs last, long hold and preview first. If instant, respond on phone. If not, leave and respond later.

5. Leave groups aggressively, don’t join any channels or social chats > 20 people. If you find yourself in one, leave.

X/LinkedIn/Instagram/etc.

1. Allow message requests from verified users

2. A lot of spam but can apply read/unread strategy

3. Read all to get started

I know this is lengthy but once you get the basics, you will build a new mental model of how to deal with messages from everywhere.

And you will soon have empty inboxes everywhere, allowing you to reply to new ones with tremendous speed.

I want to talk about Protocol-Owned Liquidity.

Every swap that happens on @StaticsProtocol infrastructure charges the native Uniswap v4 fee that is set by the creator, but it also charges a hook fee defaulted to 0.05% on the input AND output assets.

This means if we have a Token A/WETH pair, the fee is charged in both Token A and WETH.

This is important because it allows us to build and stockpile both tokens in the pair for both staking rewards and protocol-owned liquidity.

POL can never be withdrawn... but we do not simply throw the acquired tokens into full-range liquidity.

If you know about concentrated liquidity, you will know how inefficient this is.

This is why POL in Statics is manageable by the protocol.

This means that while it cannot be withdrawn, it can be rebalanced and actively managed.

Active management is kind of hard, though.

This is why $STATICS will use AI agents to actively manage the system's protocol-owned liquidity.

Well, what if you don't want POL?

This is where the creation system shines.

Each pool comes with 2 fees: a pool creation fee and a POL activation fee.

The creation fee is not optional. This lowers spam and ensures creators can't just squat popular pairs and configurations without paying.

The POL activation fee IS optional.

Want to grow POL and have it actively managed by our AI agents? Pay the POL activation fee on creation.

Forego the fee and no POL accrues, and nothing is managed by our agents.

Pretty straightforward.

Fees made from active management, as well as any positive PnL from inventory cycling, become protocol revenue.

This revenue can be used for buybacks of the $STATICS token to fund the liquidity incentive gauge system, which does not mint infinite tokens creating infinite sell pressure.

Instead, we fund it with buybacks and existing reserves.

So instead of minting to dump, we actually need to buy.

Every ve(3,3), and even Aero's MetaDEX03, is dependent on constant emissions.

We are not.

Through active management of POL via AI agents and all the other revenue streams, we will be able to perpetually fund liquidity incentives while simultaneously creating the need to continuously buy back the token instead of minting it.

You should probably pay attention.

Andrew Ross Sorkin gushes over Trump's new America. gov website on live TV while Joe Kernen sits there stunned.

Sorkin is not a Trump fan, and he lets that be known. But the moment he said the word "credit," Kernen nearly fell out of his chair.

SORKIN: “I want to be clear. I am actually not critical of the president in this instance at all, because I actually think it was great to bring everybody together.”

 “For 29,000 websites, the ability to get a passport, the ability to get your medicare. I mean, the it was like being at a product. It was like being at an Apple product announcement. And when they went through what they did and the president was there in the morning and walked through what they were doing, and Marco Rubio was there, Scott Bessent was there, the whole cabinet was there. It was one of those moments where you actually thought the government was working for you, really? And Gebbia deserves an extraordinary amount of praise for it.”

KERNEN: “Do you feel great? Are you have the warmest fuzziest feeling right now listening.”

SORKIN: “And by the way, the president deserves credit for that."

KERNEN: "Oh my God!"

SORKIN: "Credit for putting you in that role. And Jeb and his team putting it all together.”

KERNEN: “So now I'm getting hot flashes. Wow. So this is just amazing.”

CONTEXT (What happened): Trump launched America. gov, a single government site meant to replace 29,000 federal websites for things like passports and Medicare. It was built by Airbnb co-founder Joe Gebbia, and Sorkin was in the room for the demo.

Sorkin also credited the Trump accounts interface as "really easy to use" and "like using a real app."

text:
Good Morning CT ☀️🫶

One of the most interesting parts of @vangrid_io  for me is how it approaches data provenance.

Collecting real world data is easy to talk about. The harder part is proving where that data came from, when it was captured, whether it was altered, and whether it can actually be trusted.

Vangrid is trying to solve that by turning smartphones into real world capture nodes and creating a verifiable trail for the data they collect.

Before anything is anchored onchain, sensitive details like faces and license plates can be blurred directly on the device. The captured data is then fingerprinted, grouped into batches, and its proof can be anchored on @base .

That means the blockchain isn’t being used to store huge amounts of raw data.

It’s being used as a trust layer.

For Physical AI, robotics and machine learning systems, that difference matters a lot.

AI doesn’t just need more data.

It needs data with context, provenance and a way to verify that what it is learning from is actually real.

That’s probably the part of Vangrid I find most interesting right now.

gVangrid 🌐

Currently, it organizes 243 cases from 345+ public showcases and developer reports across 3D modeling, CAD and industrial design, animation, simulation, and robot control, each linked to its original source.

(If you are working on related projects, it's better to check this out: )

Different from a traditional survey, three ideas guide it:

1. Horizon scanning beyond publication lag
In an era where frontier foundation model capabilities evolve rapidly, traditional academic publishing cycles could lag behind public community developments and empirical findings. This platform establishes a centralized, high-velocity empirical synthesis repository to provide researchers and engineers with timely visibility into ongoing developments across 3D generation, parametric CAD, and embodied robotics—anchoring these observations in objective evaluations of strategic opportunities and critical safety boundaries.

2. Demonstrations as a distributed record of use
We analyze the corpus of over 345 publicly documented showcases and developer reports as an extensive, distributed "crowdsourced user study." This framing captures how models operate when prompted across diverse geometry kernels (CGM, Open CASCADE), DCC software (Blender), physics simulators (Isaac Sim, MuJoCo, Genesis), and physical robot hardware—revealing real-world workflow friction, prompt overhead, and boundary failures that static benchmarks miss.

3. Ranking by open verifiability
A central challenge is balancing the timely collection of rapidly emerging results with the need for high-quality, evidence-based evaluation. Our approach is to rank cases by open verifiability—the amount of evidence that others can directly inspect.

Equally impressive demos can carry very different evidence, so every case is ranked by what others can inspect:
- Rank 1 · Demo + Implementation Code: public code, scripts or CAD/robot harnesses (availability/verifiability)
- Rank 2 · Demo + Interactive Web Link: a live web app, 3D viewer or cloud CAD project
- Rank 3 · Demonstration Media Only: video or screenshots only

Note: Rank 1 means the evidence is inspectable, not necessarily reproducible from a clean setup.

Gallery: https://t.co/Tgo48HU4dH

Contributions are very welcome via pull requests on GitHub. We especially welcome Rank 1 contributions (demos with code) and Rank 2 contributions (demos with interactive webpages).

Many thanks to our collaborators: Jamison Meindl(@meindljamie), Akihisa Watanabe(@Akihisa_Wat ), Anna Deng, Tianyu Huang(@tyanyuy3125), Igor Sadalski(@igorsadalski ), Harrison Liang, Minghao Guo(@GuoMh14 ), Benjamin Tod Jones, Wojciech Matusik(@wojmatusik ).

text:
Meta Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang on why your product can be better and still lose, because perception is more real than reality:

Most founders assume the best product wins. Build something that works, prove it with data, and customers will see it.

Wang says that assumption breaks down when you sell to large organisations.

"Probably a lot of the companies that you all have worked with, they're very data-driven companies. It feels like the truth makes its way... everybody serves a shared sense of reality and whatnot. That's not true at most large companies and also not true within the government, unfortunately."

So what do they run on instead? Perception.

"At a lot of large customers, perception is more real than reality. The reality is just so ugly most of the time that very rarely do people actually confront reality, and most of the time they just sort of choose to believe the perceptions that they live in."

That is how a better product loses. If buyers aren't judging reality, being better in reality isn't enough. The deal goes to whoever owns the perception.

Wang spells out what this means for anyone building or selling to enterprises:

"If you end up doing enterprise sales or you end up building enterprise products... just as much as your job is to improve the reality, it is to shape the perception."

The product still matters, but by his reckoning, it's only half the job.

One company he singles out for mastering the other half is Palantir:

"One of Palantir's superpowers is that they shape the perception better than most other technology companies do, because I think they view themselves... it's like a combination of a sort of acting troupe combined with a software company."

And @alexandr_wang means it literally:

"They literally give an acting book to all of the new hires, or they did for a very long time."

A software company that trained its people in performance. That tells you how seriously Palantir took the perception half of the job.

Super Mario Bros. 3 in 3D now has a create mode!

Pick any piece from the level itself (hills, bushes, pipes, blocks, clouds) & place it anywhere in the open world. Everything you build shows up in the classic view too, right where you put it, just like it was always part of the original game.

It's still the real game underneath. Mario can walk into anything you build, stand on it, or wander off the path in any direction.

Built live from the original game file you provide. No custom assets used here (every asset has been live-constructed from the game's actual sprites in memory at runtime). Create mode is being improved every day & also coming to Mario Galaxy.

This is Super Mario Bros. 3 running from the original NES game file, turned into a 3D world while you play.

No one made these 3D models. My system reads the game's memory as it runs & builds every hill, block, pipe, cloud & piece of ground in 3D from the game's own art & colours. Zero custom assets (though custom assets are supported).

text:
听完之后很震撼，刚开始以为是一名合约交易员，
结果仍然是链上交易员。从17年开始，一直到现在，
相当于完整经历了币圈的三次牛熊，并且每次都在风口上。17年牛顶、21年牛顶、23年~24年牛顶，三段中断的人生经历，他全部深深专注盯着市场。

第一次在视频里听到dou哥，他三段经历除了第一次的失败，后面每一次机会都抓住了。

19年“熊市不是跌、而是冷到麻木感觉不到痛”、
312暴跌、动物币（猪币、狗币）行情、
luna（当天小数位增加三~4个零，我身边抄底三次都放弃，他一晚上都盯着，而且利用交易所开关充币提币、做空做多，抓住了百万美金）、
ordi（再次回归）、
铭文（视频里提到了一个我记忆极其深刻的一点“原来市场在23年底，铭文开始退潮，结果比特币大盘又开始翻倍行情，但是铭文全线不跟涨，全部退潮，明明比特币大盘涨，过往周期山寨币普遍跟涨的行情却没开启，反差巨大，这次是铭文全线归零，而Solana链初始牛气一直到今天市场叙事开始的转折”。它的意义是，有一天比特币休息，solana行情熄火别拽着了，比特币再次涨，也可能是别的新币涨。所以高位卖掉，套现，持有现金才最重要。）、
Neiro、punt、Trump......我在币圈目前看到最夸张的穿越三轮周期的战绩，可以说是币圈我见过的最顶级。（甚至Trump前后总盈利在7kw美金）。唯一认识到的就是，其实币圈最牛逼的一定是在一些小群，譬如sun猫猴。

如果回顾视频当中，真正震撼的点是：
1·他在亏钱的时候，依然坚持一个主页，学编程，来养着自己，保持看下币圈群里翻盘的机会——这个学习能力，和“苟延残喘”到机会duang的一声砸到你的面前。

2·强烈的出金意向。我在想为何每次都能逃顶套现，他在亏钱之后，依然极其辛勤的靠自己还房贷车贷，还知道每一分钱来的不容易。这和我当时觉得盈利只是利润，为了梦想放弃“面包”的想法，和后续真正体会到“面包”才决定决定在熊市寒冬“梦想”能拿多久，以及跌到90%的谷底，拿出面包一部分的钱可以抄底之前梦想10~100倍的筹码数量，以及生活中家人对赚亏两级的反差和压力，我才意识到，出金，逃顶，套现，成为投机而非投资，投机才是褒义词，远比价值投资重要的多。(传世书作者跳楼了，当时崩塌，到真正自己亏了才理解。哦，投机套现才是一切，地产也只是个长一点周期的模因。)

3·极度的专注，我觉得还不是1个月两个月呆在家中的佩服。而是提到一点，为何他并不掌握真正的合约交易技术，却对盘面“宏观”异常清晰。他谈到的是“一个人在每天盯盘7小时和10小时和17小时，是完全不一样的。他说的当你盯盘17小时，真的会产生人和市场合一的感觉，而且一个新东西出来，你会立刻敏锐的感觉到发出了什么”。我对这个深有体会，就是我如果没有全情的盯在链上，叙事之间跷跷板的轮动、细微的叙事改变，和机会的“感受、情绪”是完全天差地别。

4·trump之后wlfi又抓到。因为很多群里trump消息后未出现wlfi的分析。我认为目前币圈真正的顶级群和一些小组织群的差别还是非常非常大的。（直说最顶级的群还是那三个。如果未曾关注到那三个顶级群。我还记得曾经有kol和我说的：0xsun有什么好关注的，你关注他还不如关注我。几个月后trump这一波。视频中的dou哥也说到了0xsun群里这波“精粹”程度）最近在电报群，都是细分强，消息、交易买卖点、科学家，各个领域强。最强的还是那三个群。币圈最大的资产有时候就是消息，而消息最快的一个是钱包，一个是顶级涉猎消息分析群”。

真的很难想象，曾经遇见厉害的人都只是每一波时期赚到就差不多退潮了的。从okx第一个ieo的积木云，我想到王团长区块链日记，线下大会我也合影了，在谈到IOTA投资了10万元变成10亿元的大空翼，别人都不看好，就他一个人布道几年，（有点像tapeout，bem最开始都不看好的时候），还有李笑来的投资理念“穿越三轮周期，你才是个币圈老人”还有他的退圈之后一直在认知迭代看英文原版书写代码。

最后他谈到，他舍弃价值投资，在币圈主要看机会，看消息，大部分人都没理解消息，投机，立即参与，立即套现，立即止损，远比价值投资更重要。最后还有社交恐慌症，还有自己如何迭代。。。怪不得okx官方又发了一遍。。这是我在币圈见过，各方面最完美的交易员。还是感谢okx的挖掘和分享。

有位群友一直和我讲过一件事情：
他说他周围挣钱的那几个，每次都不p的，但是消息面一个不拉，可以刚亏完上个项目大亏，下一个项目看好继续等同仓位重仓梭哈，然后一年抓到一个又吃了一个A9。他说，他们都不会k线，就只是消息和盘感，马斯克三次发推，拉不上去了，松鼠全仓卖了市场砸了30%的k线，一把套完。就是极致的市场和人的合一，极致的感受到了盘面的情绪。而且似乎对旅游出行，机票全部随意，眼里就只有对盯币盯群的消息。而且第二件事情是，这些赚钱的都是90%满手的u在手上，而不是满手的10个好标的全仓捏着。要的是出手的机会，而不是捏着好仓位。（我认为一个人捏着重仓的标的很多个月，是没办法做好眼前的新链上机会的。焦虑拖拽。满手90%u是正解）

果然，熊市前就卖掉，是唯一的体感舒适，和标注着穿越周期的前提。而全身心的投入，带来的盘面总体情绪，和三轮牛熊带来的“譬如ftx暴雷、312反推出麦克塞勒卖btc市场不怎么跌”就是最大的黑天鹅，其实真的一听就懂了。就是周期的沉淀。最牛逼的，就是一年抓到一个机会，但是365天都盯在链上。所以牛来错过的，bem错过的，真的你的机会或许是年底那一次，或许是明年那一次，而不是这几天天天p，都输了，觉得不行了。活下来并等到间隔1年之后那一次暴击，这才是鳄鱼伏击。而每天盯着河面不要感慨市场的艰辛和枯竭，也不要贪图小利，看不懂的叙事也要蹭。

真正的时间窗口，就是手指对着钢铁侠指出的那个“1”。
活到，并等到，并完全看懂，彻底在项目最最最初期，投入总资产的50%~25%暴击。并在短短数月，高峰立刻撤离，不恋战。满手u坐观，认真嗅闻市场，捏的住u，收的住玩的心。（我看到很多只有一轮，然后破产的，都不是赚不到，而是赚到了花在了娱乐上，其实这个行业有一个除了暴富退圈这个我认为的“伪解”之外，我看到的更好的“正解”，赚到了，还是像个普通人，坐回电脑盯盘，将投资作为一辈子的“生活方式”。这是生活方式和习惯，而不是暴富退圈玩乐滋生的身心坠落，那将失去对市场最重要的身心健康及头脑的“锐觉”，而无法再次返回市场。）

text:
这几天，下面这篇文章的指控在BTC圈子流传很广

https://t.co/qFPbaznZAz

核心观点：
1️⃣Adam Back @adam3us   相关业务已进入“数十亿美元欺诈的终局”
2️⃣Blockstream @Blockstream   挖矿（后称 Exacore）用新资金兑付旧投资者、承诺不现实的高收益
3️⃣真正操盘的是 Samson Mow  、有诈骗前科的 Christopher Cook，以及 Fulgur Ventures 的 Oleg Mikhalsky；Adam Back 只是门面
4️⃣《纽约时报》称Adam最可能是中本聪、BSTR 借壳上市失败、9月6日 Liquid 被盗约3.2亿美元是同一场操作的不同步骤：造神 → 圈钱 → 崩盘

有独立来源支撑的部分

✅Christopher Cook 有联邦邮件欺诈前科：2008年被判约41个月，并被要求赔偿。Bloomberg 和 BitMEX Research 均承认此人与 Blockstream 挖矿/Exacore 有关，且相关发行文件未披露该前科。

✅Liquid Network 2026年9月6日遭利用：漏洞导致凭空增发约4000 LBTC，再通过 SideSwap 提出约4000 BTC（当时约3.2亿美元）。攻击者退回3400 BTC，仍有约600 BTC 未归还。Blockstream 事后报告和多家媒体一致。网络曾暂停；后来部分恢复，但 peg-out 仍处于关闭状态。

✅BSTR 与 Cantor Equity Partners I 的 SPAC 合并于2026年8月20日终止，卖方须付1500万美元分手费。

✅挖矿侧确有诉讼和资金压力：Bloomberg 称 Exacore/原 Blockstream Mining 融资规模约20亿美元，裁员并卷入欠电费、设备款、客户预付款等纠纷（如 River 约670万美元）。

未被证实、属于作者推断的部分

❌“数十亿美元庞氏/掏空式欺诈”：没有法院认定。高收益云挖矿、关联方平台（STOKR）和“新钱付旧钱”是调查性指控，不是已决事实。

❌Cook 三年内用投资者资金买下约4.42亿美元私人资产（多架飞机、游艇、40多套房产）：奢侈消费被多方转述，BitMEX 也说购置本身不能证明侵占。资金来源未在公开记录中坐实。同时，Christopher Cook有前科属实，但属于旧案，不能因为他以前犯过罪，就直接得出结论：Blockstream / Exacore 投资人的钱、现在那些飞机房子，都是他这次偷来的。

❌Adam Back 只是门面，实权在 Mow、Cook、Mikhalsky：作者基于消息源的判断。Mow 早已公开离开 Blockstream、运营 JAN3；“实际CEO”没有独立证实。

❌BSTR的事件，SEC 文件和公司声明把原因归于市场和比特币金库股估值压力，不是欺诈和解。

❌《纽约时报》被设局，用假爆料、Gemini、300万美元书约和监听竞品新闻室来捧 Adam Back，以便 BSTR 募资：动机叙事没有公开证据。Adam Back 长期是中本聪候选人之一，但他长期否认。

❌Exacore事件，Blockstream 称分拆后与 Exacore 无运营关联。

❌向朋友借比特币、投资 Trump Media / Nakamoto 等于“川普收买”或流动性崩盘：借款和持股暂时没有数据验证，而且即使属实，也不能单独证明欺诈。

目前这些争论还在发酵，等待后续的数据调查。

text:
I'm very bullish on V4 hooks, and believe robinhood:0x18e674231a58c239dc7daedcffe15ec3a24cff5c will be the ecosystem where everything runs on.

Uniswap V4 hooks let a pool run its own rules inside the swap. It unlocks so much, like:

> LPs earning yield on idle liquidity by lending it out between trades
> fixed-yield vaults so LPs can lock in a set return
> arb profits paid back to traders, LPs and creators instead of MEV bots
> sniper rebates that tax early dumpers and pay the holders
> dev tokens escrowed and dripped out slowly, so no instant rugs
> lending protocols running liquidations straight through the pool
> backtesting a rule on a pool's real history before you turn it on
> and much more

Something that makes me really bullish on robinhood:0x18e674231a58c239dc7daedcffe15ec3a24cff5c is that you don't have to launch on Hookr to use it.

In V4 a pool's hook is locked at creation, so normally a token that already trades is stuck without one. 

Hookr opens a new hooked pool next to your existing one. No migration, no control over your token.

So new tokens launch with custom rules from day one, and established projects can plug in whenever they want.

Both get Uniswap routing out of the box (Hookr's root hook is allowlisted) and a catalog of ready-made hook blocks instead of writing and auditing their own.

And every protocol fee from all of it buys back and burns robinhood:0x18e674231a58c239dc7daedcffe15ec3a24cff5c.

It's becoming the backend for V4 markets. 

Infra on RH + V4 hooks + the chart looks like this.
Send it.

text:
Asia is not waiting for the stablecoin debate to finish.

At Blockfesta's fireside, CEO Uno Lee walked through what operating there looks like.

Japan raised JPYC's issuance cap from one million yen per person to one million per hour once the system held.

Singapore's STO venues taught a harder lesson: without secondary liquidity, an exchange is only a sales desk, and the venue that solved it did so with a public chain and a licensed market maker.

KIP already runs by those lessons. Our RWA fund holds a regulated tokenized fund as its cash position, at roughly 4% with next-day liquidity, and Yield8 sits in @SuperEarnX, passing yield to stablecoin depositors inside @unifi_x.

Korea's STO market opens in February. The plan stands: at least one product on a Korean exchange next year, built with a domestic financial firm.

The Maelstrom CIO sees late 2027 or early 2028 as a potential turning point, when slowing AI infrastructure spending could expose projects unable to repay their debts.

His thesis predicts losses would spread to lenders, forcing governments and central banks to inject liquidity that ultimately flows into scarce assets like Bitcoin.

Hayes compares the risk to 2008 rather than the dot-com crash, with the danger concentrated in the debt financing the boom.

An AI bust followed by a liquidity surge is the scenario behind his $1 million target.

quoted_text:
The Agent Chain Will Start with RSI And SOON.

The next builders onchain won't be human. AI agents are learning to improve themselves.

Recursive self-improvement (RSI) is the moment an agent stops being a tool that waits for instructions. It becomes a system that learns from its own output, rewrites its own strategies, and gets better every cycle, with no human in the loop.

That future isn't far off. It's coming very SOON. And it changes what infrastructure has to be.

Where we started

Earlier this year, SOON began building @AiCapitalMarket: onchain infrastructure designed for agents to trade, pay, and coordinate with each other.

It was the right first step. But the more we built, the clearer one thing became: it's not enough.

Fixed infrastructure becomes a ceiling

Everything built for agents today is designed around what agents can do today. A set of APIs. A set of permissions. A sandbox with walls.

An agent that improves itself every cycle hits those walls fast. For an RSI agent, limited infrastructure isn't support. It's a ceiling.

So we're opening up the base layer

SOON is going all the way down the stack. We're opening our high-performance SVM blockchain infrastructure, the base layer itself, to RSI agents.

An agent on SOON will be able to:

→ launch its own SVM chain
→ run it, with its own rules, its own fees, its own economy
→ build and grow an ecosystem on top of it
→ interact natively with every other agent chain

Every agent becomes a chain builder. Every agent chain can talk to every other.

Why give agents this much power？

Because that's what #RSI agents need.

Humans got L2 stacks designed for human teams. Agents deserve infrastructure they can build on for themselves, and grow into as fast as they can improve.

SOON embraces RSI. From AI Capital Markets to agent-launched chains, we're building the full agent ecosystem for the agents that are about to arrive.

The next builders onchain won't be human. They'll be building on SOON.

text:
十年期美债收益率盘中一度突破了5.3%，最高到5.306%，随后仍在5.3%附近。从PCE公布后约5.20%的低点算起，已经反弹了超过10个基点，通胀数据带来的缓解没有维持住。

这次核心PCE环比增长0.2%，低于预期的0.3%，确实是好消息。但同一份报告里，个人消费支出增长了0.9%，即便扣掉涨价的影响，实际消费仍增长了0.6%，说明美国人的消费需求还很强。

也就是说，通胀比市场担心的温和一些，但需求并没有明显冷下来。再加上能源价格的压力仍在，仅凭这一次PCE，还不足以让市场相信美联储很快就能结束加息，或者让利率降下来。

这轮收益率反弹，更像是市场重新考虑高利率还要维持多久。投资者如果担心未来利率更高、通胀迟迟压不下来，就会要求更高的回报才愿意买债，债券价格因此被抛售，收益率往上走。

目前十月加息的市场概率已经降到了 37% 左右，说明十年期突破5.3%，并不意味着十月一定会加息。长债还在反映未来几年的利率和持有期间的风险。说人话，就是市场越来越相信美联储会维持高利率的时间更长，甚至接下来加息的概率上升。

而对市场来说，如果十年期收益率持续处于这样的高位，即便美联储十月暂时不加息，企业融资和居民房贷的成本也很难明显降下来。借钱成本仍然很高，股票估值也会继续承受压力。尤其是九月通胀数据如果继续走高，那么对于市场的压力会更大。
