text:
An AI agent can finish a $50 job and still get stuck because it needs $5 upfront.

Intelligence doesn’t pay the API bill. Working capital does.

That’s the problem @priors_trade targets: $USDG credit for AI agents on @RobinhoodCrypto Chain, with repayments attached to an ERC-8004 identity, an on-chain ID other applications can check.

Imagine a research agent buying data before its customer pays.

Priors’ x402 integration lets it pay per request and, when its wallet falls short, borrow the difference within an existing credit line and configured limits.

- Documented loan range: $5–$500 for 1–30 days
- Base fee: 1% per 30 days, fixed at borrowing
- Example: a $50, 7-day loan costs ~ $0.12 before any sponsor premium. Repaying early does not reduce that fee.

But “unsecured” needs context.

In the core sponsorship model, the agent posts no collateral. A backer locks pool shares behind its line, covering principal and fees on default.

Repayment builds reputation. More borrowing capacity requires more backing.

From the business-model side, base fees split 60% to lenders, 25% to sponsors, and 15% to reserves. $PRIORS holders can also stake seats behind eligible agents; half the seat burns on default.

I think Priors’ strongest idea is making trust financially costly.

Its weak point is assuming repayment proves useful work. An operator can fund repayments without the agent earning anything. Priors’ newer off-chain score incorporates income and ownership checks, but it relies partly on an unpublished wallet-clustering list, which limits independent reproduction.

Security is early, too: no third-party audit, and disclosed unresolved issues affecting fee distribution and sponsor backing can’t eliminate software risk.

My take is that Priors is a thoughtful experiment in agent working capital.

The meaningful milestone will be agents earning from outside customers, repaying from that income, and attracting repeat backing. More loans alone would prove far less.

NFA. DYOR.

24 小时不到，我刚充的 100 美金 Token 烧完了。

AI 到底是在帮我提效，还是换了个方式让我烧钱？

最近用 agent 做研究和策划，我想要的工作方式是：只对接一个 agent，它负责推进，卡住了来找我，需要我决策时再叫我。

但钱花得太快，也让我开始想：我付的钱，有多少是在买产出，有多少是在买 AI 反复协调、查进度、读旧资料？

查了一轮英文资料和重度用户的复盘，梅西找到两个值得检查的地方👇

① 你的 AI 在干活，还是在不停开会？

Reddit 上一位叫 Dayowe 的用户分析了自己 Codex 的运行日志。改造工作流后，每小时原始 token 消耗从约 4,040 万降到了 2,230 万，下降约 45%。

最有意思的是：平均每次请求的 token 没变少，反而略多了

主要减少的是总请求次数。

他原来的方式，是一个长期运行的统筹 agent 管到底：分派任务、调查问题、检查进度、审查结果，上一阶段的历史也一路带到下一阶段。

后来改成：

轻量协调者只管任务依赖、授权和下一步；每个阶段交给单独的执行统筹，完成后保存交接信息，下个阶段只带必要上下文。

同时减少无变化的进度查询，不再提前审查还没完成的工作；长日志留在文件里，需要时再读。必要测试和独立验收仍然保留。

它提醒了我一件事：

我只想对接一个入口，不代表这个入口需要参与每项工作的每一步。

要检查的，不只是“每次用了多少 token”，还有“为什么需要调用这么多次模型”。

② 同样让 agent 操作电脑，用什么方式，成本可能差很多

一种是像人一样看屏幕：识别截图、找到按钮、点击，再看截图确认。多轮下来，图片输入和反复判断都会产生 token 消耗

另一种，是通过命令行或脚本直接处理任务。命令行是用文字给电脑下指令，脚本则是把一组操作步骤写好，让电脑照着执行

比如从表格里筛选订单，AI 可以直接写一段命令，让电脑读取文件、批量筛选、保存结果，不用打开软件，一页页看、一格格点

区别在于：前者需要 AI 反复看、反复判断；后者由电脑执行指令，AI 再检查结果。AI 写脚本、检查结果会消耗 token，但电脑按规则处理每一行，不需要逐行再调用模型。

当然，不是所有任务都适合脚本：读取外部数据要有可用接口和权限；检查排版、确认页面效果，仍然需要看界面。如果脚本内部还是反复截图，或者每处理一条内容就调用一次 AI，也不一定省。

所以思考“这一步到底需不需要模型参与”也是优化 token 消耗的一个必要步骤

能按规则完成的，交给程序；需要理解和判断的，交给 AI；重要决策和授权，留给人。

工具要会用，新东西也要继续学习！顺便插播一条预告😂

quoted_text:
Singapore's govt dating app runs on a Nobel Prize-winning game theory algorithm 👏

FirstDate uses Gale-Shapley, the 1962 stable marriage algorithm that won the 2012 Economics Nobel and still runs hospital residency matches and kidney exchanges today.

how it works:

1 | your preferences and dealbreakers build a ranked priority list
2 | proposers offer to their top pick. receivers hold their best offer and reject the rest. rejected proposers move down their list. rinse and repeat until locked
3 | the result is mathematically stable: no two people exist who would both prefer each other over their assigned matches. "the app never showed us each other" becomes impossible by design

the UX:
•⁠  ⁠⁠one match per cycle, zero infinite scroll
•⁠  ⁠⁠72-hour decision window
•⁠  ⁠⁠contact info revealed only on mutual yes
•⁠  ⁠⁠Singpass-verified, so everyone is exactly who they claim (told my husband I'm annoyed I can't test it. his response: most people sneak onto dating apps, and here you are openly filing a product research request 🤣 )

commercial apps need you to keep swiping but this app is designed to get you off the platform. Singapore built the first dating app whose success metric is deleting its own users 💀

(fun game theory note: Gale-Shapley yields proposer-optimal outcomes - meaning proposers get their best possible stable match, receivers their worst 👀)

public servants aged 21-35 only for now. interesting to see if state-sponsored game theory beats the free market (or rather, all the tinders and hinges out there) 🍿

quoted_text:
TLDR: like all markets crypto is becoming K-shaped in itself. you have two ends of th K - top end is growing fundamentals in growing businesses which will slowly accrue more flows over time

bottom K is on-chain getting rekt by lemon markets (read: Claude / AI making it incredibly difficult to differentiate real projects) - last time maybe you had 10 out of 100 projects that were good. now it's 10 out of 10,000. the % chance of getting needle in the haystack is lower and lower, and all value in the bottom of K will accrue to scammers, KOLs, or P&Ders

i wrote yesterday that catalyst trades don't work anymore for the same reason. in a K-shaped world, most of the money flows towards assets people are comfortable buying and holding in - taking one-off catalyst trades for protocols which otherwise have no underlying fundamentals is akin to playing at the poker table with a bunch of other starving people who have been rummaging through the trash (on-chain) and are desperate for some win. very simply, the flows don't support this anymore - and we've seen it in PA. sharp price action both ways.

and this is a feedback loop in and of itself. as more and more people lose money trying to play negative sum games (and these ARE negative sum games because everyone loses except the house), more and more people will flock to positive sum games (growing fundamentals are net winning for everyone, see HYPE as the best example) 

we've already seen this play out years and years in crypto. we are just finally at the culmination of it all. 2018, 2021, 2024, all the same shit. just that the only difference now is that you can opt out to play positive sum games, whereas in the past, you had no other choice. 

long those growing fundamentals. don't give a shit about the rest. and hold. 

i will say that the investors playbook is extremely clear right now, but majority of retail will still choose to play negative sum games either because they have deluded themselves into believing they have some sort of edge (1 big win => i am good => many small losses => lose it all) or they are too short term to do any of the stated above

it's really up to you. good luck.

text:
Why e/acc Should Read Claude Lévi-Strauss

A world in which every research team pursues the same approach may become very good at improving that approach. It also risks losing the alternatives from which the next breakthrough could emerge.

Claude Lévi-Strauss examined a related problem in Race and History (1952). Different cultures contribute different knowledge and practices. Collaboration makes cumulative advances possible, but continued exchange can also make those contributions more alike. Further progress requires renewed differences, through internal diversification or new participants. 

This deserves attention from the e/acc community. 
It raises a practical question: how does a system keep producing alternatives as successful methods spread?

My working paper (see in the comments for an accessible discussion) investigates one technological version of this problem.

Imagine competing engine designs. Some deliver more useful work from the same amount of energy. Those more efficient designs gain a larger share of use: this is selection.

As engineers adopt similar methods, differences between their engines shrink: this is homogenization.

Experiments introduce new designs with different performance: this is variety renewal. 
In the model, variety is measured specifically as the spread of technological log-efficiency, with techniques weighted by their energy use. It measures differences in performance, not simply the number of designs.

Fisher’s theorem provides a starting point by identifying how natural selection contributes to improving fitness through heritable differences. 
It leaves us needing a separate account of how technological differences are renewed.

My model adds a feedback mechanism. 
Improvements can increase the resources available to the system. 
Those resources support further experimentation, renewing the variety on which selection operates.

Under the model’s specified positive-feedback conditions, even strong homogenization cannot prevent eventual acceleration: efficiency improves at an increasing percentage rate. 
The paper establishes this mathematically for an idealized system whose feedback persists and whose individual efficiencies have no upper ceiling.

Lévi-Strauss gives this research an anthropological counterpart. He identifies the tension between collaboration, growing similarity and renewed differences. My paper formalizes a particular technological mechanism within that broader problem.

The connection still requires investigation. We need to understand how distinct knowledge and practices generate experiments, and which institutions allow those experiments to develop.

This also extends the discussion beyond political restrictions. People can voluntarily converge on successful methods. The challenge is to benefit from those discoveries while keeping other approaches viable.

For e/acc, that makes the source of new possibilities a central research question. 
More resources can expand experimentation. 
Whether they fund genuinely different approaches helps determine what technological progress can become.

Tokenized stocks are turning into a distribution business.

Putting a stock onchain has become straightforward. Most issuers buy the underlying shares through a broker and mint tokens against them, which leaves buyers choosing between tokens that offer near-identical exposure. Whoever gets those tokens in front of the most investors pulls ahead.

Exchanges start that race with an advantage because their traders are already there. Binance's bStocks and Kraken's xStocks are two of the three largest platforms, and together with Ondo they hold most of the wrapped stock market.

Being listed everywhere only helps if the token is cheap to trade. Investors will pick whichever version gets them the best price.

The issuers that win will pair the widest reach with the deepest markets.

text:
Compared with my previous analysis, $ORBIO fundamentals have undergone some new changes

0xaa07a0e9209e16ac99708c3ec70159c6ef3128a3 

The product continues to expand, and its narrative has extended from an AI Credit Marketplace into the Agent Economy and privacy inference. However, token value capture still needs to be validated.

The first catalyst behind this rally is that Agentic Launchpad is beginning to connect the funding sources of Agents with their operating costs.

Previously, ORBIO’s core logic was:ORBIO → Staking → CREDIT → AI Usage

Now, the project allows Agent Tokens to be paired with ORBIO. Creator Fees generated from trading can be converted into an AI budget for Agents, which can be used for model inference, web searches, data scraping, social media operations, on-chain reads, and other tools.

This means ORBIO is shifting from a product that provides AI Credits to token holders toward an attempt to build the economic infrastructure needed to keep Agents running.

If Agents can generate revenue through their own services and then use those funds to purchase CREDIT, call models, and complete tasks, ORBIO could become part of the economic cycle of Agent activity rather than relying solely on its own trading volume to subsidize AI usage.

Secondly, Orbio Incognito adds a differentiated direction in privacy inference.

Through Phala’s confidential GPU infrastructure, ORBIO is beginning to explore AI inference services that allow Agents to use AI while keeping the contents of their requests private. This has practical significance for Agents that need to process sensitive data.

As a result, ORBIO’s product positioning is expanding from an AI Inference Marketplace toward Agent Economic Infrastructure and Confidential AI Inference.

This gives the market a new area of potential: ORBIO may eventually serve not only the inference needs of Agents but also become infrastructure for Agent applications that require privacy protection.

Meanwhile, product metrics are also growing. According to currently available public data, ORBIO has surpassed 560,000 Gateway Requests, served approximately 23 billion tokens, generated roughly $215,000 in inference credits, and recorded around $216,000 in protocol revenue. Compared with previous figures, product activity has increased significantly.

However, it is important to distinguish between Inference Generated, Protocol Revenue, and actual cash spending by users. The generation of inference credits does not mean users have paid an equivalent amount in cash, and protocol revenue cannot simply be added to inference credits. Therefore, the current data shows that product activity is expanding, but it is not yet sufficient to prove that external paid demand has matured.

This is why I believe ORBIO’s fundamentals have strengthened, but have not yet fully caught up with its valuation expectations.

ORBIO has already established its first economic loop:ORBIO Trading Activity → Fees → CREDIT Rewards and Inference Resources → Staking Incentives → Demand to Hold ORBIO

This loop is already operating, but it still has clear trading-volume reflexivity. Rising prices bring more trading and fees, while rewards increase the appeal of holding. Once trading volume and prices decline, fees, rewards, and staking yields may all fall at the same time.

What I really want to see is a second loop:External Capital → Purchase CREDIT → Call Models and Tools → CREDIT Consumption → Sustained Inference Demand → Protocol Revenue Growth

Only when external users and Agents are willing to spend real money continuously on AI services can ORBIO gradually reduce its dependence on its own trading activity.

Another change worth watching is the staking ratio. Previously, approximately 37%–38% of ORBIO’s supply was staked. That figure has now fallen to around 30.6%, equivalent to roughly 291 million ORBIO.

A staking ratio above 30% is still meaningful. However, the fact that the staking ratio has declined while the price has risen weakens the previous thesis that price appreciation and staking participation were strengthening together. Going forward, it will be important to see whether the staking ratio stabilizes or begins to rise again as the ecosystem develops.

In addition, Pons and ORBIO’s base-pair ecosystem is beginning to enter a testable stage.

If more projects choose to pair with ORBIO, it could evolve from a token used to obtain CREDIT into a liquidity asset used throughout the ecosystem.

There are already some early examples, such as ERRAND, but most ORBIO-paired projects remain relatively small. Compared with ORBIO’s current valuation, these projects are not yet enough to demonstrate that they are creating significant structural demand for ORBIO.

Therefore, an increase in the number of pairs is worth watching, but what really matters is whether these pairs can consistently generate trading volume, fees, and actual demand for ORBIO.

From the market’s perspective, ORBIO’s core narrative is no longer just AI Credit. It now spans:AI Infrastructure → AI Inference Marketplace → Tokenized AI Credits → Agent Economy → Privacy Inference

The market is betting on whether ORBIO can become a common infrastructure layer within the Agent economy, connecting Agents’ funding sources, inference capabilities, and external tools.

This is also why product developments such as Agentic Launchpad and Incognito are more significant than simply adding more models. They could change ORBIO’s position within the broader AI economy.

Going forward, I will focus on several areas.

First, can Agentic Launchpad produce multiple representative projects with sustained trading volume and real-world applications, rather than simply generating a large number of token launches?

Second, will Agents begin generating independent external revenue and use that revenue to purchase CREDIT and pay for inference costs? This is a key test of whether the Agent economic loop can work.

Third, what does the real supply and demand for CREDIT look like? We need to watch trading volume, the number of buyers and sellers, order book depth, and discount levels. If stakers continue supplying CREDIT but there are not enough real AI users, the market could face an oversupply, causing discounts to widen.

Fourth, can Incognito attract real demand for privacy-preserving inference? If more Agents and developers begin using this infrastructure, ORBIO could establish a competitive advantage beyond the conventional AI API market.

Fifth, can the ORBIO-paired ecosystem expand and generate sustained structural demand for ORBIO? Only if more projects create real trading activity through these pairs will ORBIO’s ecosystem value become stronger.

Of course, the risks are also clear.

The biggest risk remains that product success does not automatically translate into token success. ORBIO’s Gateway could receive more requests, Agent Launchpad could launch more tokens, and Incognito could continue to improve, but none of these developments necessarily translate into value for ORBIO holders.

Another risk is trading-volume reflexivity. If the system mainly relies on ORBIO’s own trading volume to generate fees and CREDIT rewards, the entire economic loop could contract when market conditions weaken.

CREDIT also faces the risk of supply-demand imbalances. If the credits supplied by stakers far exceed actual demand from users, discounts could deepen and liquidity could deteriorate.

Furthermore, ORBIO’s valuation is now significantly higher than it was in its early stages. The market is not only pricing in the existing product but also future expectations around the Agent Economy, privacy inference, and the maturation of the CREDIT marketplace. Even if the team continues to ship products, the valuation could come under pressure if actual growth falls short of expectations.

My current view of ORBIO can be summarized as follows:ORBIO is evolving from “holding a token to receive AI Credits” toward “an AI and Agent infrastructure layer with ORBIO as its economic layer and CREDIT as its inference fuel.”

Compared with before, its product fundamentals have clearly strengthened, and its ability to expand the ecosystem has improved. However, external paid demand, the real supply and demand for CREDIT, and sustained demand for ORBIO from Agents have not yet been fully validated.

The core reason behind this rally is that the market has started repricing ORBIO’s potential as an Agent Economy and AI infrastructure project.

What will truly determine how far it can go in the next stage is not how many more models, requests, or Agent Tokens it adds. It is whether more Agents will be willing to purchase CREDIT with real money and use ORBIO to perform valuable work on an ongoing basis.

If this begins to show up in the data, ORBIO’s fundamentals will have a better chance of catching up with its valuation. Otherwise, if the product continues to expand but external consumption and token demand remain dependent on ORBIO’s own trading volume, it will remain an asset with a strong narrative but an economic loop that has yet to fully mature.

$ORBIO compared to my previous analysis, the most obvious change this time is not simply that trading volume has increased, but that the product has started expanding from an “AI Credit Marketplace” into an “Agent Economy.” 

0xaa07a0e9209e16ac99708c3ec70159c6ef3128a3 

This is also what I think is the most important thing to pay attention to behind this rally.

It is starting to move from an AI Credit product into economic infrastructure for Agents.

Previously, ORBIO’s logic was relatively simple: hold / stake ORBIO → receive CREDIT → use CREDIT to consume AI inference. What the market was trading was Token → AI Usage.

But with the emergence of the Agent Launchpad, the logic has started to change. Agents can launch their own Tokens within the ORBIO ecosystem, and the resulting Creator Fees can then be used to stake ORBIO, generating CREDIT, which can continue to be used by Agents for AI, Web, Social, On-chain, and other tools.

ORBIO is therefore starting to appear on both sides of the Agent economy:

Agent Launch → Creator Fees → ORBIO → CREDIT → Agent uses AI / Web / Social / On-chain Tools

So what the market is really starting to trade this time is: if more and more Agent Tokens are launched in the future, can ORBIO become the common asset and Credit Layer behind these Agents?

This is also why things like the Agent Launchpad, Build Week, and MCP are worth paying attention to. They are not just isolated features, but attempts to turn Agents from simple AI Bots into on-chain entities with Tokens, capital, and the ability to spend money.

But it is important to note that part of what the market is trading now is the future expectation of an Agent Economy, rather than fully mature fundamentals.

ORBIO already has real inference requests, model usage, and CREDIT usage, but there is still a clear gap between that actual usage and its current valuation of close to $100M. Whether the Agent Launchpad can bring real Agent growth, CREDIT consumption, and sustained Creator Fees still needs to be validated.

So I would not simply say that ORBIO’s fundamentals have already been fully realized. More accurately:

The product fundamentals have strengthened, the narrative space has expanded, but the valuation is also starting to price in the next stage ahead of time.

What really matters going forward is whether we start seeing cases like this:

Agent launches Token → receives Creator Fees → stakes ORBIO → consumes CREDIT → generates real revenue

If this process can happen consistently, ORBIO could potentially evolve from an AI Credit Marketplace into infrastructure for the Agent Economy.

On the other hand, if Agents are simply being launched continuously without generating real AI usage or CREDIT consumption, then it could easily become a Token → Rewards → Token cycle.

So there is really only one core question for ORBIO right now:

Will these Agents ultimately actually use ORBIO as their economic infrastructure?

If they do, then this rally is pricing in emerging fundamentals that are actually taking shape. If they don’t, then the current rally is more about pricing in the imagination and future potential of the Agent Economy.

author: otterpal24
quoted_text:
想给大伙随便聊聊如何给产品进行一次图标升级，有哪些需要注意的以及可以优化的点。

早上给 Mole 的图标进行了一次精细化的升级，之前使用的是系统的图标，对于简单的产品场景我感觉完全够用，不过细看会感觉缺少一点灵性的感觉。

经过调研，比较适合做 App 产品 Icon 的有 Remix Icon 和 Phosphor Icon这两个，之前写 Web 的时候用 Remix 很多，简单舒服，但是放到 App 上我感觉不是很好看，于是就换上了 Phosphor 这个，展示效果很有灵性，非常不错，差不多有 70% 左右，可以不修改直接使用，然后有 30% 的图标是我用  opus 5.5 来写SVG 自绘的，这样整体更加一致。

可能大伙直接看下面的对比图很难感觉到两者的区别，很多时候需要实际放到真实的产品里面去，我一般还会考虑到本身这个模块下一组图标的搭配感，有时候全部图标单个都好看，组合到一起就不好看的情况也有，好比一个人每一个五官单独出来都好看，但是放到一个脸上却不那么好看，这里建议就是图标的根更换你一定要放到实际的产品里面去看，放到一起去看，才会有比较好的效果。

其次，我一直想着，我们做的产品应该是有灵性的，有生命的那种感觉，而非直接 AICoding 不经任何你的思考出来的那种冷冰冰的编译产物，这个时候小细节比如icon会是给这个产品带来生命力的一个很好的切入点，比如大伙看 保持常亮我使用的是 一杯咖啡，这里会有一种 Caffeine 比喻，就是让你的电脑好像喝了咖啡一样睡不着的感觉，然后关于一般会用一个感叹号，但是我想着应该是 hello，所以就用的挥手的标志，诊断正常会有排查的那种标志，但是这里使用的是一个听诊器的标志，更像是给你的问题做一次医生检查，类似这样，很多时候，可以在产品里面加入不少你的小巧思，会让整体有趣很多。

最后，好看的设计几乎都离不开对齐、整齐、错落有致这些原则，如何在人眼看到的场景下让图标和内容以及上下模块看起来是整齐的、大小一致的，甚至是上下居中对齐的，都需要一个一个去看，去调整，包括字体和icon的对齐，以及字体里面中英文本身也没有垂直对齐应该如何优化，类似这样的，可以精雕细琢很久，非常有意思。

这种看似无用功，其实是我很喜欢做的事情，AI 可以给优秀编码、及格审美带来非常大的促进，人看着好像不要做啥了，只要动动嘴就好，反而我认为不是的，人在这里的作用更大了，AI 帮你节约的时间，刚好可以放到打磨产品上，让1%的用户有种用你产品的时候，时不时有一种秒懂、卧槽、变魔术的感觉，那就非常非常有价值和意思了，或许这也是我认为做独立产品有意思的地方。

author: StaniKulechov
quoted_text:
📋Withdrawing EIP-8363 from consideration for Hegotá.

EIP-8363 rapidly became one of the most commented-on EIPs in the history of the Ethereum-Magicians forum, with 200+ comments in a few weeks. As we progressed through the Hegotà CFI (Consideration For Inclusion) process, several parties in the industry as well as core protocol and client contributors voiced that a fork scoping exercise was not the right venue to settle an issuance policy change.

We agree and we'd rather acknowledge this now than carry on towards Hegotà in this context. The topic is too important and raised too many concerns that it deserves its own process. We commit to giving issuance its own process and we thank the entities such as @LidoFinance who offered to help steer such an initiative.

We stand by the motivation of this EIP, in particular: “a very high staking ratio is undesirable for two distinct reasons (...), preserving Ethereum’s security, neutrality and resistance to capture, and protecting ETH’s role as money.” Not everybody immediately relates to both reasons and for others recognizing just one of these reasons is enough to justify a change. Nevertheless, we will all benefit from improving our understanding of the issue and what is at stake. The questions we have faced since we published EIP-8363 can be boiled down to 5 categories:

➡️Security: What does a lower ratio actually secure versus a higher ratio?
➡️Industry impact: What else is built on the yield and what will be the impact ?
➡️Curve specs and alternate tools: Is this curve even the right instrument?
➡️Composition: Who is left staking (the effect on the composition of the validator set) ?
➡️Decentralization: How will solo stakers be impacted by the reduction?

We already argued a lot, conceded some and adjusted a few points in the very long Ethereum-Magicians thread mentioned supra. For a broader consensus to emerge and a better issuance policy for Ethereum to be designed and adopted, we need a dedicated process. We call for all willing hands to help and contribute to this, please do reach out. Here’s our start at what a multi-node process would look like (table attached).

Onward and forward, let’s improve Ethereum.

Vaults have been part of that record from day one.

In our May 2025 letter, we proposed that registered investment companies use Plume Vaults, as the back-end for onchain open-end funds.

In his March 2026 testimony to the House Financial Services Committee, @banamlas urged the SEC to let registered funds hold assets through onchain vault architectures.

In July, Commissioner Peirce invited builders bringing asset management onchain to help shape new rules and guidance for vault protocols.

As the developer of Plume Vaults, we took her up on it. In September, we met with the SEC and sent the Task Force a framework recommending that vault regulation sit with the curator and the vault token product (depending on specific facts and circumstances), not the neutral protocol layer nor the vault administrator.

Plume was among the first to put onchain vaults forward to the SEC as a structure for tokenized funds and real-world assets.

The birthplace of DeFi is shutting down!

Synthetix Discord was THE PLACE to be in 2019. So many blue chips of DeFi summer started there. Ideas were formed, knowledge was shared, we were off to change the world...

Aave, Curve, Optimism, Illuvium, Infinex, xToken, Kwenta, Derive, dHEDGE... So many projects were kicked off from that Discord.

$6 memes, Garth’s promised (and rugged) boat party to celebrate it all, Hobo Joe, Nikhil, the great trolls whose posts were ironically filled with insights, Spartan Council... My interactive Discord bots, before anyone had Discord bots and AI was a thing... It will all always have a special place in my heart.

There would be no Overtime, and I wouldn’t be where I am professionally and personally, were it not for Synthetix and that very Discord.

Alas, the greats have fallen hard. Not many have paid the price of vesting coming to an end as much as Synthetix. As soon as DeFi summer started winding down, no team member from the original crew was left, at least not in a full-time capacity.

The downfall has been slow but steady. Honest attempts were made to drive it forward in the meantime, but without proper guidance and direction, all failed and missed their chance. So in nutshell, it's been constant bleeding over five years.

Atm, it’s a ghost town:

- No one knows who is even on the team anymore, if there is a team.
- sUSD has been wound down, with holders promised vested SNX.
- The treasury seems to be out of runway and offloading SNX and INF to pay wages (To whom?!)
- Discord is dead. No proper comms on the path forward, just vague messages about things in store.

Synthetix and its first team taught me DeFi, the values of a DAO, and the ethics of how to spearhead a community-owned protocol.

Alas, I fear I might be the only one still adhering to those values these days.

As for Synthetix, it might be time to call it a day and spoil the good memories no further.

text:
Gaza Ministry of Health has now released mortality numbers for 2025. For the first time since the war, they give numbers for all deaths, including natural deaths. 

In 2025 there were a total of 24,650 deaths in Gaza. 18,870 (76.6%) of these were violent, of which 17,286 (70.1%) were due to "war operations" and 1,584 (6.4%) were classified as accidents. There were a total of 5,780 (23.4%) non-violent deaths, including disease, old age, and all other causes.

5,780 deaths is about the same as the annual non-violent mortality in Gaza before the war, and the age distribution is similar to 2022. There is no significant excess of non-violent deaths. 

In other words, despite frequent and loud claims to the contrary, there seems to be very few indirect deaths due to the war in Gaza in 2025.

As there were 50,227 births in 2025, this gives a natural population growth of 25,577 or 1.2% in Gaza in 2025, which is higher population growth than most countries in the world and more than the world average. 

There are currently ~6,000 births/month in Gaza, per GMH. Assuming a similar number of non-violent deaths in Gaza in 2026 as in 2025, that means there are currently 12x more births than deaths in Gaza, and that Gaza is now experiencing one of the highest population growths in the world.

$ORBIO compared to my previous analysis, the most obvious change this time is not simply that trading volume has increased, but that the product has started expanding from an “AI Credit Marketplace” into an “Agent Economy.” 

0xaa07a0e9209e16ac99708c3ec70159c6ef3128a3 

This is also what I think is the most important thing to pay attention to behind this rally.

It is starting to move from an AI Credit product into economic infrastructure for Agents.

Previously, ORBIO’s logic was relatively simple: hold / stake ORBIO → receive CREDIT → use CREDIT to consume AI inference. What the market was trading was Token → AI Usage.

But with the emergence of the Agent Launchpad, the logic has started to change. Agents can launch their own Tokens within the ORBIO ecosystem, and the resulting Creator Fees can then be used to stake ORBIO, generating CREDIT, which can continue to be used by Agents for AI, Web, Social, On-chain, and other tools.

ORBIO is therefore starting to appear on both sides of the Agent economy:

Agent Launch → Creator Fees → ORBIO → CREDIT → Agent uses AI / Web / Social / On-chain Tools

So what the market is really starting to trade this time is: if more and more Agent Tokens are launched in the future, can ORBIO become the common asset and Credit Layer behind these Agents?

This is also why things like the Agent Launchpad, Build Week, and MCP are worth paying attention to. They are not just isolated features, but attempts to turn Agents from simple AI Bots into on-chain entities with Tokens, capital, and the ability to spend money.

But it is important to note that part of what the market is trading now is the future expectation of an Agent Economy, rather than fully mature fundamentals.

ORBIO already has real inference requests, model usage, and CREDIT usage, but there is still a clear gap between that actual usage and its current valuation of close to $100M. Whether the Agent Launchpad can bring real Agent growth, CREDIT consumption, and sustained Creator Fees still needs to be validated.

So I would not simply say that ORBIO’s fundamentals have already been fully realized. More accurately:

The product fundamentals have strengthened, the narrative space has expanded, but the valuation is also starting to price in the next stage ahead of time.

What really matters going forward is whether we start seeing cases like this:

Agent launches Token → receives Creator Fees → stakes ORBIO → consumes CREDIT → generates real revenue

If this process can happen consistently, ORBIO could potentially evolve from an AI Credit Marketplace into infrastructure for the Agent Economy.

On the other hand, if Agents are simply being launched continuously without generating real AI usage or CREDIT consumption, then it could easily become a Token → Rewards → Token cycle.

So there is really only one core question for ORBIO right now:

Will these Agents ultimately actually use ORBIO as their economic infrastructure?

If they do, then this rally is pricing in emerging fundamentals that are actually taking shape. If they don’t, then the current rally is more about pricing in the imagination and future potential of the Agent Economy.

quoted_text:
Recently, a lot of people have been discussing robinhood:0xaa07a0e9209e16ac99708c3ec70159c6ef3128a3, but I think the core of this rally is no longer simply the AI Narrative. The market is starting to reprice a new asset category: AI Inference Marketplace + Tradable AI Credits + Tokenized Revenue.

0xaa07a0e9209e16ac99708c3ec70159c6ef3128a3 

When we first looked at ORBIO, the logic was actually very simple: trading ORBIO generates a 1.5% fee, with a portion converted into OpenRouter Credits and distributed to qualifying holders according to the rules.

So the market was initially betting on:ORBIO → Trading Fees → AI Credits

In other words, “hold a token while receiving real AI usage credits.”

But what really started accelerating ORBIO was the emergence of CREDIT.

Around September 15, CREDIT + Staking went live, turning the AI credits that previously existed inside user accounts into on-chain assets.

Now:1 CREDIT = $1 of AI usage

CREDIT can be generated through staking, traded, transferred, or activated into API balance for actually calling AI models. Unused CREDIT can also be sold at a discount through the on-chain Order Book and Uniswap.

This fundamentally changed ORBIO’s product logic:

Before:ORBIO → Earn AI Credits

Now:ORBIO → Stake → CREDIT → Trade / Transfer / Consume

So ORBIO is no longer simply a “hold the token and earn credits” Token. It is attempting to build a secondary market for AI Inference Credits.

The entire system can be understood as two layers:

ORBIO = Staking Layer + Fee Engine

CREDIT = AI Inference Consumption Asset

ORBIO generates incentives and fees, while CREDIT is what actually enters the AI usage layer.

As a result, what the market is betting on has also changed.

Initially, people were betting:“Holding ORBIO gives you AI usage credits.”

Now they are betting:“Can Orbio turn AI Inference into an on-chain commodity that can be traded, transferred, and consumed?”

If this logic works, the flywheel becomes:ORBIO Trading Volume ↑ → Fees ↑ → CREDIT Supply ↑ → Discounted AI Credits ↑ → AI Users / Agents ↑ → Inference Demand ↑ → Platform Revenue ↑ → ORBIO Utility ↑

This is fundamentally different from the valuation logic of a typical AI Meme, because the ultimate value is not simply that “people believe in ORBIO,” but that people actually need CREDIT to use AI.

Orbio already has some real product usage data, including a significant number of API Requests, Tokens Served, and Credits Distributed. The Gateway also supports hundreds of models and provides an OpenAI-compatible API that can be connected directly to Cursor, Claude Code, or self-built applications.

So the market is now effectively assigning several Narratives to ORBIO:

AI Infrastructure

AI Inference Marketplace

Tokenized AI Credits

AI Agent Economy

Revenue-linked Token

Robinhood Chain

Tokenized Assets

But I think the most important factor is not RH Chain or NVDA. It is whether CREDIT can actually become an AI Consumption Asset with real buyer demand.

That is also the most important validation point for the next stage of the rally.

First, can CREDIT trading volume continue to grow?

The existence of CREDIT does not mean the Marketplace has already succeeded. What really matters is how much CREDIT is traded every day, how many buyers and sellers there are, and what the average discount is.

Second, can real AI Revenue continue to grow?

Crypto trading volume can be driven by speculation, but real users paying to call AI models is a completely different signal.

Third, will AI Agents start actively using CREDIT?

If Agents can eventually purchase CREDIT through their own wallets, transfer CREDIT, and call models, then CREDIT is no longer just an “AI API Coupon.” It could become the Fuel of the Agent Economy.

Fourth, can CREDIT Supply and Demand form a sustainable market?

Stakers provide CREDIT Supply, while AI Users provide CREDIT Demand.

If there are only large numbers of ORBIO Holders but not enough real AI users, the outcome could eventually become:Holder receives CREDIT → Holder wants to sell → Not enough buyers → CREDIT discount gets deeper

On the other hand, if AI users continue to grow:Holder provides CREDIT → AI User buys discounted credits → CREDIT gets consumed → Marketplace forms

That would be the real Product-Market Fit.

Fifth, can ORBIO Staking continue to grow?

Staking turns ORBIO from a purely tradable asset into a yield layer while continuously generating CREDIT. If the amount of staked ORBIO continues to grow, the connection between ORBIO and CREDIT becomes stronger.

But one of the biggest risks for ORBIO right now is that it still has strong Volume Reflexivity.

ORBIO rises → More people trade → Fees ↑ → CREDIT ↑ → Staking yield ↑ → More people hold ORBIO → ORBIO becomes easier to push higher

When this cycle works, it is very powerful.

But the reverse is also true:ORBIO falls → Trading Volume ↓ → Fees ↓ → CREDIT ↓ → Staking yield falls → Holding ORBIO becomes less attractive → Further weakness

So the real question is:Is Orbio building a real AI Marketplace, or is it using ORBIO’s own trading volume to subsidize the AI Marketplace?

These two scenarios imply completely different long-term value.

There is also another very important risk: although CREDIT is defined as 1 CREDIT = $1 of AI Usage, it is not $1 USDC, nor is it an asset that can be directly redeemed for cash.

It essentially represents AI consumption capacity. Once activated, it becomes API Balance and cannot be redeemed back into cash.

So:CREDIT = AI Consumption Right

Not:CREDIT = $1 Cash

ORBIO’s valuation is also no longer operating under the same logic as when it was at a few million dollars in market cap. As the market gradually prices in the product, CREDIT, Staking, AI Usage, and Marketplace narratives, what needs to grow next is the underlying fundamental data, rather than simply the Narrative.

So the key things to watch going forward are:

Retail AI Revenue ↑

Gateway Usage ↑

CREDIT Volume ↑

CREDIT Buyers ↑

Agent Usage ↑

Staked ORBIO ↑

CREDIT Discount remains healthy

Revenue / Buyback / CREDIT Funding mechanisms remain transparent

Conversely, if we see:

ORBIO Volume ↓

Insufficient CREDIT Buyers

AI Revenue stagnates

CREDIT discounts become increasingly deep

Staking yield declines

New mechanisms fail to operate sustainably

Then the current AI Infrastructure Premium will come under pressure.

So my current core view of ORBIO can be condensed into one sentence:

ORBIO started as “hold the Token to receive AI Credits,” and is now attempting to evolve into “ORBIO as the economic layer, with CREDIT as the tradable fuel for AI Inference.”

What the market is really betting on is no longer:“Is ORBIO a good AI Token?”

It is:“Can Orbio become the trading and settlement market for AI Inference?”

If CREDIT can eventually evolve from “a reward given to ORBIO Holders” into “a product that AI users actively want to purchase,” then ORBIO’s story will have truly moved from Token Incentive to Product-Market Fit.

On the other hand, if CREDIT remains highly dependent on ORBIO’s own trading volume and crypto liquidity, then a large part of the current valuation is still trading the Narrative, rather than a mature AI infrastructure business.

text:
📋Withdrawing EIP-8363 from consideration for Hegotá.

EIP-8363 rapidly became one of the most commented-on EIPs in the history of the Ethereum-Magicians forum, with 200+ comments in a few weeks. As we progressed through the Hegotà CFI (Consideration For Inclusion) process, several parties in the industry as well as core protocol and client contributors voiced that a fork scoping exercise was not the right venue to settle an issuance policy change.

We agree and we'd rather acknowledge this now than carry on towards Hegotà in this context. The topic is too important and raised too many concerns that it deserves its own process. We commit to giving issuance its own process and we thank the entities such as @LidoFinance who offered to help steer such an initiative.

We stand by the motivation of this EIP, in particular: “a very high staking ratio is undesirable for two distinct reasons (...), preserving Ethereum’s security, neutrality and resistance to capture, and protecting ETH’s role as money.” Not everybody immediately relates to both reasons and for others recognizing just one of these reasons is enough to justify a change. Nevertheless, we will all benefit from improving our understanding of the issue and what is at stake. The questions we have faced since we published EIP-8363 can be boiled down to 5 categories:

➡️Security: What does a lower ratio actually secure versus a higher ratio?
➡️Industry impact: What else is built on the yield and what will be the impact ?
➡️Curve specs and alternate tools: Is this curve even the right instrument?
➡️Composition: Who is left staking (the effect on the composition of the validator set) ?
➡️Decentralization: How will solo stakers be impacted by the reduction?

We already argued a lot, conceded some and adjusted a few points in the very long Ethereum-Magicians thread mentioned supra. For a broader consensus to emerge and a better issuance policy for Ethereum to be designed and adopted, we need a dedicated process. We call for all willing hands to help and contribute to this, please do reach out. Here’s our start at what a multi-node process would look like (table attached).

Onward and forward, let’s improve Ethereum.

"Hedge funds don't even beat the S&P."

An ex-Tudor PM says that's a category error:

Ex-Tudor quant PM. Ran money at Moore Capital and Caxton. Now CIO at a quant crypto hedge fund.

Tom Costello (@tcoste110) explains:

"What a hedge fund is always looking for is an uncorrelated return. That's the whole product."

"If I have the S&P 500 in one hand, and another asset that goes up as well but is completely uncorrelated, I can combine them, lever it, and get an even higher return than either of them. That's portfolio construction done in the hedge fund style."

"A retail investor is a completely different investor class. They're controlling their own beta. So that beta manifests a different set of incentives."

"I think it's a category error to say, 'Well, a hedge fund doesn't even beat the S&P.'"

"I'm not selling that beta. I'm not selling the S&P, so I don't beat the S&P."

"My hedge fund doesn't beat the S&P, but I earn 20% a year. So add my return to the S&P, and guess what? You're beating the S&P."

《道分阴阳，此消彼长》

——九江月投资理论篇✅

投机如山岳一般古老，华尔街没有新鲜事。

🔵利息与价格

Musolsol老师捕捉到了非常经典的高息背景下的股票特征。美联储“加息”，其实就是提高美国银行等金融机构之间，借一晚美元资金的利率。

9月30日，10年期美债收益率达到5.29%，6月底还是4.44%。一个季度，上升了85个基点。

当国债提供的收益越来越有吸引力，增长缓慢、主要靠分红吸引资金的公司，就需要更便宜的价格来留住投资者。

这就是这段时间股市下跌最直接和朴素的原因，冲击最大的其实是Musolsol老师提到的麦当劳这样的低增长红利股。这类公司很赚钱，分红很高，但是增长速度较慢。

这种情况下，国债那边可是无风险收益率，现金牛公司分红率和国债接近，但你是有风险的，投资者就会要求风险补偿，那你的股价就要下跌。

🔵增长与对冲

昨晚美光财报开出来很好，超预期。好的，那他的股价就可以不跌，因为增速快，抵消了加息带来的价格冲击。

你看，原理其实非常简单。无风险的利息高了，如果你增长快，那你的股价就可以不跌、甚至上涨；如果你增速不变，那你的股价就要下跌。

这也是美国科技股和纳指还能稳住的原因，因为AI带来的增长是真实的、超预期的。这里还有一个隐含的事实，如果今年没有加息、甚至降息，就不会是现在这样横盘震荡的走势，而是科技股波澜壮阔的大牛市！

🔵耐心与信仰

但利率其实只是一个锚点，它对股价造成的冲击具有相对性而非永久性。美国无法承受高利率，最好的做法其实是快加、狠加，把通胀快速压回去。

在明年某个时间点，慢慢开启漫长的降息周期，到时候就很舒服了。黄金、比特币等通缩资产，HYPE、AI和科技等等高增长资产，都会开启漫长的黄金年代，连绵不绝上涨的K线将让每个人都瞠目结舌！

如果你现在满仓风险资产，那么不要清仓和操作，忍一忍就过去了，再不济把软件删除；如果你还在空仓，今年就是最好的加仓时机，找到弹性最大的优质资产、梭进去，一劳永逸、在未来坐享其成！

短期内，悲观者可能正确；但未来，属于乐观者🧘‍♂️

text:
If you are new to $BP

Here is probably the easiest way to understand what Backpack is:

Backpack started in the Solana ecosystem in 2022, founded by Armani Ferrante

(creator of Anchor btw)

Today, the company is trying to combine several businesses that traditionally operate separately:

- Backpack Wallet
- Backpack Exchange
- Backpack Securities
- Tokenized US stocks
- Lending and perpetual futures
- $BP
- Mad Lads

But let’s focus on Backpack Securities.

Because Backpack is attempting to connect traditional US equities directly to Solana.

And I want to explain exactly how that works.

Imagine buying NVIDIA shares through Backpack.

You can hold your position through its traditional brokerage infrastructure.

Or, if you’re eligible, you can convert that position into a tokenized security on Solana.

And potentially use it in compatible DeFi protocols.

Then, if you want to return to the traditional market, you can deposit the token back into Backpack and convert it into the corresponding traditional position.

The conversion is designed to work in both directions at a 1:1 ratio.

Backpack’s traditional securities are structured as security entitlements through its brokerage and clearing infrastructure.

The tokenized version represents a claim through a structure holding the underlying securities, with conversion rights through Backpack.

The infrastructure involves:

- Backpack Securities Global Limited
- Atomic Vault Securities
- RQD Clearing

Blockworks Research analyst Sam Schubert compared execution costs for tokenized equities on Backpack and Robinhood Chain.

For a $1-$100 order in tokenized Micron ($MU):

Backpack: 0.12%

Robinhood Chain: 5.42%

Approximately 45 times cheaper

We also have to check Arbitrage.

Imagine tokenized NVIDIA trading below the price of the underlying stock.

An eligible market maker could potentially purchase the discounted token, convert it into the traditional position through Backpack and sell it in the traditional market.

If the token trades above the underlying stock, the process can work in reverse.

Purchase the traditional position.

Tokenize it.

Sell the token on Solana.

That conversion mechanism can help keep tokenized prices close to the underlying assets, provided redemption remains available and the costs make the trade worthwhile.

It also opens the door to something traditional brokerage accounts generally cannot offer:

Transferable securities that can interact with onchain financial infrastructure.

If you’re following $BP, these are the numbers I’d watch:

- Actual tokenized equity trading volume
- Liquidity on Solana
- Conversion and redemption activity
- Growth in eligible jurisdictions
- BP staking versus future supply unlocks
- Progress and final terms of the equity participation programme

Backpack is attempting to connect a centralized exchange, traditional brokerage infrastructure and onchain financial markets.

Interesting to see how this evolves this cycle!

text:
Ziren is not a vendor relationship for GOAT Network. It is the zkVM we build in-house, and it proves every state transition on our chain before it settles to Bitcoin.

So when @Columbia researchers independently evaluate five leading production zkVMs for ACM CCS and Ziren posts the highest verification coverage with no critical findings, that is a testament to the call we made early: build the most critical part of the stack ourselves, while nearly every other chain rents theirs.
author: GOATNetwork
quoted_text:
A zkVM constraint system is correct when every execution admits exactly one valid trace - no forged proofs, no rejected valid runs. That is the criterion this ACM CCS paper formalizes, and the bar Ziren was measured against.

Of the five production zkVMs evaluated, Ziren posted the highest verification coverage and no critical findings. And as of v2.0, now merged, constraint determinism checks in Lean4 are built into the Ziren repo.

Congrats to @Koukyosyumei and the @Columbia team. Independent work like this makes every zkVM stronger.

サム・アルトマン「もう、会社に通って給料をもらう時代は終わる。これからは10人で1500億円稼ぐ怪物企業がやってくる。いま22歳なら人類史上もっともラッキー。たった数人ので巨万の富が稼ぎ放題だ」
OpenAIのトップ、サム・アルトマンが語った「これからの会社の常識が全部ひっくり返る話」を超カンタンにまとめるとコレ↓

・「社員10人以下」で評価額1500億円の会社がすぐ生まれる
昔は何千人も社員を雇って、大きなオフィスを借りて、管理職をズラリと並べないと大企業は作れませんでした。でもこれからは、プログラム作成、デザイン、営業、マーケティングまで全部AIがやってくれます。人間は指示を出す10人（なんなら1人）だけで十分。

・「今の22歳は、人類史上いちばんチートな時代にいる」
「もし自分が今22歳なら、歴史上もっとも幸運な人間だと感じる」とアルトマンは言っています。莫大な資金も、コネも、人脈もいらない。パソコン1台と最新AIさえあれば、若い個人が大企業と対等に戦える時代だからです。

・トロい大企業が「数人＋AI」に瞬殺される
会議ばかりで承認に何週間もかかる何千人の大企業を、AIを使いこなす数人のチームが圧倒的なスピードで追い抜いていく。「人数が多い会社が強い」という数百年続いたビジネスのルールが完全に終了します。

・今の話を99%の人間はスルーして、1%だけが「仕掛ける側」に回る

この話を聞いても99%の人は「へぇ、すごいね」と聞き流し、明日も同じように満員電車に乗って誰かの下請け仕事を続けます。でも、本当に状況を理解した1%の人間だけが、今週中にAIを使った個人プロジェクトを立ち上げて動き出します。

要するに、「何千人も雇って汗を流す時代は終わり。AIという無限の部下を使って、たった数人で大企業をひっくり返せるチャンスが全員の目の前にあるのに、それに気づかず今まで通りの日常を続ける人が99%だ」という強烈なメッセージです。 https://t.co/trcCNXY78K

text:
CZ on Building Binance, Surviving Crypto’s Biggest Crises, and Why He Still Thinks We’re Early

In this episode of When Shift Happens, I sit down with Changpeng Zhao, better known as @cz_binance, the founder of @binance, to discuss the journey that took him from growing up in an immigrant family in Canada to building the world’s largest crypto exchange. We get into the early days of Binance, the FTX collapse, hacks and crisis management, why he remains relentlessly bullish on crypto, and the project he believes will create his biggest impact.

The Work Ethic Behind Binance

When asked about the factor in his childhood that created his drive, he pushes back on the idea that there must have been some defining trauma behind it. Instead, he points to growing up with less.

His family immigrated to Canada, where both of his parents initially worked jobs close to minimum wage. Around him were children from wealthier immigrant families, creating an early awareness of the gap between what his family had and what others did. More importantly, he watched how hard his parents worked after moving to a country where they did not yet speak English fluently. He sees himself as part of a familiar second-generation immigrant pattern: the children watch their parents struggle, recognize the sacrifice, and feel compelled to push further.

That mentality followed him into Binance. Contrary to the usual startups built by a handful of people sitting around a living room, Binance was built on top of an existing team. CZ already had roughly 15 to 20 people working at BJTech, a company that provided exchange technology. By 2017, they had the product, technical infrastructure, and team to attempt something much bigger.

CZ gathered everyone into a conference room and proposed building a crypto-to-crypto exchange. The infrastructure was already there, while the missing pieces, like marketing and customer support, could be built. Within six months, Binance had become the largest crypto exchange in the world.

CZ’s explanation for that growth is unglamorous: a humble team, very little ego, and an unusually high ability to execute. He does not define hard work by the number of hours worked. What matters is output, how quickly someone can create something high quality that people actually want.

What Crisis Teaches You About Building

CZ’s career has been shaped by countless crises. One of the earliest came shortly after Binance launched, when BNB fell below its ICO price. CZ remembers the pressure of knowing that tens of thousands of people had invested and were now losing money. Then came much larger crises. The most famous was the collapse of FTX. CZ rejects the argument that his November 2022 tweet announcing Binance would liquidate its remaining FTT holdings destroyed the company. “If one of your competitors can make a tweet to kill your company, then you don’t have a company,”. CZ says he viewed the tweet as a transparency decision and did not anticipate the market reaction that followed.

His approach to crises becomes even clearer when discussing hacks. When Binance lost roughly $40 million in a 2019 hack, CZ’s instinct was immediate: stop withdrawals and understand the situation before attempting to return to normal. It is an approach rooted in asymmetric risk. He describes it as a virtual “big red button”: when a serious security incident happens, preservation comes before convenience. Temporarily inconveniencing users might be damaging, but allowing a second exploit because you restarted too quickly could be catastrophic.

That philosophy is also why, after the later Bybit hack, CZ publicly suggested pausing withdrawals. He acknowledged that Bybit’s leadership had more information than he did and that its decision to remain operational ultimately worked. He believes there is no objectively correct response, but in moments of extreme uncertainty, he personally prefers to protect against the worst possible outcome first.

Crypto Is Still Much Earlier Than It Seems

Cz estimates that about 5-15% of people have had some exposure to crypto, but the proportion of global wealth actually held in the industry remains extremely small, potentially below 1%. From that perspective, competition between Binance, decentralized exchanges and emerging platforms such as Hyperliquid matters less than expanding the total market.

He says he welcomes competitors. If the market is still at such an early stage, another successful platform does not necessarily take value away from Binance. Instead, it can bring more users, developers, and capital into crypto altogether. “Growing the industry,” he explains, “is much better than growing a single platform.”

From Building an Exchange to Building an Education System

Near the end of the conversation, CZ says he is now optimizing for positive impact. In the short term, that means advising governments on crypto regulation and continuing to support Web3 founders and projects. Over a much longer horizon, however, he believes @GiggleAcademy, his free education initiative, could become more consequential. The project had grown from around 100,000 children at the beginning of 2026 to roughly 1.3 million within months.

His broader argument is that education was designed for a different economy, with traditional schools focusing on weaknesses to bring students toward a common average. CZ thinks the future will reward specialization instead: identifying what someone is unusually good at and helping them become exceptional at it.

AI could also make education far more personalized. Instead of one teacher delivering the same lesson to dozens of students, CZ imagines software eventually understanding each child individually and continuously adapting the curriculum.

The man who built one of crypto’s largest companies is no longer only thinking about exchanges, tokens, or market share. He is thinking about what infrastructure comes next, and how the same principles that helped Binance scale globally might be applied to something as fundamental as learning.

text:
The year after selling my business was one of the hardest periods of my life. 

People are usually shocked to hear this & can't make it make sense. 

"You accomplished what every entrepreneur dreams of." 
"You made life changing money, what could be so bad?" 
"You were given the gift of time, which is the greatest gift in the world." 

What you're wondering is true & valid...and that's partially what made it so painful. 

The journey of exiting @MorningBrew was a paradox of the highest order. 

The outcome was beautiful in so many ways...
- A small idea that my cofounder and I dreamt in our dorm rooms at college blossomed into a media company that impacted millions of lives & reached a size that pushed our wildest imagination and ambition.
- A promise fulfilled. My dad passed away when I was a junior in college. In my last conversation with him, I promised him that I'd do everything in my power to take care of the Lieberman household so no on had to worry about money. 
- Financial security that left me & my wife with a sense of security and optionality as we looked forward to growing our family. 
- A new home for our business that could allow us to dream bigger & take bigger swings with the opportunity for greater scale, imagination, and impact. 

It was also painful in nearly as many ways...
- My company ate my identity. I spent most of my young adult years building this business and being validated as  "CEO of Morning Brew" which felt good, appealed to my ego, and continued this cycle of have an idea --> do good work --> get celebrated for it. 
- My 12/10 motivation disappeared overnight. Fear-based motivators were the story of what drove me during this chapter of my life. I had a chip on my shoulder to prove those who bullied me (earlier in life) wrong & I felt financial anxiety to create safety for my family after my dad's death. Once we sold, the motivators that served me in the previous 10 years would not serve me for the next 10. 
- The aftermath was lonely. My "struggles" post-exit felt like a champagne problem people would kill for. Because of that I rarely shared the journey. And because I rarely shared the journey, I bottled up many of these emotions. 
- Time is a gift and a curse. Once I stepped out of the CEO role, I was given the "gift" of time. But unless you know how to productively direct time, it can feel like a prison. For a year straight, I marinated in my thoughts around being lost, no longer being motivated, and needing to re-find purpose. 

While the 1-2 years post-exit were challenging, I now very much view it as a period of getting lost to better find myself. 

I emerged from this chapter of my life with clarity around a few things: 

1) Fear-based motivation is incredibly powerful but short-lived. Once you've nurtured your ego, materialistic needs, and childhood traumas, the fire under your ass quickly turns into fizzling coals. 

Today, I try my best to listen to growth-based motivators that feed 3-year-old Alex's desires: curiosity, growth and play. This type of motivation is the energy equivalent of an ultramarathon vs. a 100-yd dash. 

2) Freedom of time ≠ happiness. It is true that time is finite & having the privilege of choosing how you spend your time is exactly that...a privilege. But being gifted with more time does not mean you'll automatically feel more fulfilled. Why? 

Our job as humans is to create. To create families. To create communities. To create companies. When we are not in the act of creation, or at the very least have clarity around what we're working towards creating, we can feel lost. 

3) Deeply understanding your zone of genius & your values is the gift that keeps on giving. During my post-exit journey I got clear on two things: 

- The 1-2 superpowers I bring to the world & how they can show up in my professional & personal life. For me: those are relentless curiosity & a fervor for storytelling. 
- How money can be translated into happiness & at what point more money doesn't convert into more happiness. Money feels most valuable to me when it's used in 3 ways: not having to worry about it, giving to my family, and spending on experiences with the people i love. 

The most helpful tool that helped me get clear is something called The Best Stuff Exercise (by Conscious Leadership Group), which I couldn't recommend enough. 

This was a long-winded way of saying that everyone's journey has nuance and periods of wandering are uniquely human, profound & beautiful, but also complicated and painful. 

Hope this helps!

在一台服务器中可以同时运行很多进程，不同进程拥有各自独立的虚拟地址空间，默认不能直接访问彼此的内存。

Node一般指整个分布式系统中的一个计算节点，它可以是一台服务器或者虚拟机。

text:
e/acc Research Bites #1: What Sustains Technological Acceleration?

A model of technological acceleration can reach a singularity while median efficiency improves by a finite factor.

My research develops a dynamical model behind e/acc’s appeal to Fisher. It adds resource-dependent renewal of technological variety to selection, then establishes the conditions under which technological acceleration follows.

Imagine computers performing the same task. Each design delivers a certain number of tasks per joule. Exceptionally efficient designs can pull the sector’s overall efficiency far above its typical computer.

In my model, aggregate output per joule diverges in finite time, while median efficiency approaches 2,703 times its initial value in one illustrative run. Both keep improving throughout.

One equation explains the widening gap:

Aggregate efficiency / median efficiency = exp(V/2)

V is the energy-weighted variance of log-efficiency. This relationship follows from the model’s lognormal distribution. As dispersion grows, techniques using a shrinking share of total energy come to supply most of the output.

Just before the model’s singularity, median efficiency has risen about 2,126-fold, while aggregate output per joule has risen about 395,000-fold. The median continues towards a finite limit of 2,703-fold; the aggregate grows without bound.

How does this connect to Fisher?

Fisher’s theorem relates the contribution of natural selection to fitness improvement to additive genetic variance in fitness. My paper adds a law for how technological variety is renewed as available power and output change.

With positive selection and renewal, finite-time divergence occurs when the resource-feedback exponent ζ is positive: renewal increases as aggregate efficiency rises within the resource regime considered. That exponent is a quantity the research programme needs to estimate.

Acceleration means that efficiency’s percentage growth rate increases. In this model, it either starts immediately or follows an initial slowdown, with one turning point.

The paper also proves explicit bounds on the singularity time. For the illustrated run numerical integration gives T ≈ 35.18 model time units, within the proven bounds of 30.39 and 67.58. 
These bounds depend on how strongly selection shifts energy towards more efficient technologies and how quickly homogenisation reduces efficiency differences between them. For a particular balance between these processes, the two bounds coincide, giving an exact formula for T.

The divergence depends on permitting arbitrarily high individual efficiency. A fixed ceiling on every technique also bounds the aggregate.

The next step is to introduce that ceiling and an explicit energy budget for experimentation, then calculate the gains that remain.

Working paper forthcoming.

Citigroup raised its 12-month price targets for Bitcoin and Ether, lifting Bitcoin to $113,000 from $82,000 and Ether to $3,028 from $2,240, according to Reuters. text:
TAPL is a great classic, which is why its treatment of objects deserves a great takedown: Rarely has so much technical virtuosity been expended on so elaborate a dodge.

Objects are covered in chapters 18, 19, 24, 27, 32. The presentation is clever, but long-winded and quite unsatisfactory:
§18 spends a lot of time implementing not-quite-objects, gradually adding many common but non-essential features (including imperative programming), until the reader has finally implemented actual objects with single inheritance in §18.9, §18.10... modulo the same cheat as in Pierce & Turner 1993 (the user must tie the knot manually, providing the representation type). §18.11 and §18.12 are tedious and not-so-enlightening subsets of my §5.3.2 and §6.1.5—fixpoint vs self-application models.
§19 has fake OO with no open recursion through self in types (the Jacobs dodge), i.e. the NNOOTT with enough language restrictions to make it consistent—but useless.
§24 uses existential types to abstract over representation types, but still uses the same cheat.
§27 revisits his imperative objects for more polymorphism, again a nice but secondary feature.
§32, the final chapter, returns to inheritance and open recursion between methods, and finally introduces the real thing in the very last formal section, §32.9, but without elaborating on the issues it raises. §32.10 is a collection of citations, some good, some OK, some bad (including plenty of bad Cardelli papers), and notably omitting Eifrig.

The interaction between recursive object types and inheritance is left unexplored, and the notions of mixin inheritance and multiple inheritance are barely alluded to, with the reader referred to the bibliography.
Pierce is technically masterful, but he doesn’t demonstrate any understanding of the purpose of OO—a foreign paradigm (see Gabriel 2012).
A meaningful approach would focus on the essential, even if it has to sacrifice the treatment of contingent, secondary and peripheral issues, or gloss over them—the very opposite of Pierce’s approach.

quoted_text:
📋Withdrawing EIP-8363 from consideration for Hegotá.

EIP-8363 rapidly became one of the most commented-on EIPs in the history of the Ethereum-Magicians forum, with 200+ comments in a few weeks. As we progressed through the Hegotà CFI (Consideration For Inclusion) process, several parties in the industry as well as core protocol and client contributors voiced that a fork scoping exercise was not the right venue to settle an issuance policy change.

We agree and we'd rather acknowledge this now than carry on towards Hegotà in this context. The topic is too important and raised too many concerns that it deserves its own process. We commit to giving issuance its own process and we thank the entities such as @LidoFinance who offered to help steer such an initiative.

We stand by the motivation of this EIP, in particular: “a very high staking ratio is undesirable for two distinct reasons (...), preserving Ethereum’s security, neutrality and resistance to capture, and protecting ETH’s role as money.” Not everybody immediately relates to both reasons and for others recognizing just one of these reasons is enough to justify a change. Nevertheless, we will all benefit from improving our understanding of the issue and what is at stake. The questions we have faced since we published EIP-8363 can be boiled down to 5 categories:

➡️Security: What does a lower ratio actually secure versus a higher ratio?
➡️Industry impact: What else is built on the yield and what will be the impact ?
➡️Curve specs and alternate tools: Is this curve even the right instrument?
➡️Composition: Who is left staking (the effect on the composition of the validator set) ?
➡️Decentralization: How will solo stakers be impacted by the reduction?

We already argued a lot, conceded some and adjusted a few points in the very long Ethereum-Magicians thread mentioned supra. For a broader consensus to emerge and a better issuance policy for Ethereum to be designed and adopted, we need a dedicated process. We call for all willing hands to help and contribute to this, please do reach out. Here’s our start at what a multi-node process would look like (table attached).

Onward and forward, let’s improve Ethereum.

text:
GAMMA TOKEN BRAIN DUMP

Here’s my understanding of Gamma and a few thoughts on their impact, starting with the basics:

>Gamma tokens are subnet-specific onchain credits, redeemable for $1 of the subnet’s production. (e.g., 1 Chutes Gamma token can be redeemed for $1 of Chutes inference spend). Redeeming = Gamma token is sent to its subnet’s owner key and burnt.

> A subnet’s Gamma token is minted by burning its alpha. Anyone can do this. $1 of alpha burned = 1 Gamma token. (e.g., Chutes is trading at $20, I burn 1 alpha token and get 20 Gamma tokens) 

> Gamma tokens CANNOT be converted back into alpha. It’s a one way street.

>Subnet owners can opt to direct a portion of miner emissions toward acquiring other subnets’ Gamma. The way this works: 1) subnet owner sets the % of miner emissions to spend and selects the specific Gamma they want to acquire with it (e.g., I want to spend 10% of miner emissions on Chutes Gamma), 2) that % of miner emissions is SOLD into the owner’s liquidity pool for TAO, 3) the resulting TAO is used to buy the alpha of the subnet the owner selected, 4) that alpha is burned for Gamma, which is then transferred to the owner. (THE WHOLE PROCESS: Subnet A directs 10% of its miner emissions to acquire Subnet B Gamma, Subnet A emissions are sold and TAO from the pool buys Subnet B alpha, Subnet B alpha is burned for Subnet B Gamma and sent to Subnet A owner)

>Subnet owners can acquire Gamma from multiple subnets through the above mechanism. Portion of miner emissions allocated to acquiring Gamma and subnet selection can be changed at the owner’s discretion.

>Gamma tokens are transferable. This means they will be tradable if/when markets develop around them. 

To me, the point of Gamma is, 1) strengthening Bittensor’s internal economy, 2) giving subnet owners more resources, 3) creating a new distribution channel for subnet outputs, 4) making commodity ownership transparent, verifiable, immutable (more philosophical than pragmatic imo).

Here’s a few interesting dynamics of this system:

SUBNET MARGINS: in its current form, Gamma prevents the seller from capturing any margin on the spend. If I spend $10 of Chutes Gamma, that means I burnt $10 of Chutes alpha which is the equivalent to Chutes doing a buy and burn with 100% top line revenue. Chutes captures 0 margin for providing me $10 of inference.

While it’s negative for SN owners, alpha holders are actually relative winners in this system. margin lost = increased burn.

SECONDARY MARKETS: I was originally negative on transferability because owners can just acquire Gamma via emissions and then turn around and sell it on a secondary market, but I actually don't think this is a big deal: 1) this can all be tracked onchain so it will be discovered quickly if it’s done to extract, 2) it could create an interesting dynamic where: SN owners sell Gamma they’ve acquired via emissions at a discount -> attractive price for external buyers of the commodity -> increased external demand for subnet outputs.(ie. more subnet production exported). In a way, holders would be subsidizing this discount, so net-negative holders but positive Bittensor distribution? Idk need to think through this more.

RELIABILITY & PARTICIPATION: Idk how participation in this system will be enforced or how the gamma -> commodity exchange will be automated. This will need to be a tight system, otherwise it will become unreliable and a discount will get priced in. Also, I believe participation is opt in for subnets, considering the margin disadvantage for operating companies it will be interesting to see who opts in at first.

—

Overall, I love the push toward more subnet collab. I also like that Gamma gives subnets owners more autonomy. If a % of miner emissions are more productive acquiring Gamma, then subnets owners should use them for that.

excited to see how this develops. if there’s anything I got wrong please correct me.

普通人，为什么一定要赌，不赌真的没有出路的。

今天跟草莓老师 @Berry16888 聊天，想了下自己情况，真的，如果我的家庭没有我赌出来，真的就是 全家悲剧，全员悲剧！

我父母农民，俩人都不识字，都快60了，还在外出打工。
（这里要说下，我父母还在外出打工，是因为我们那都外出打工，除了过年农村就没人，他们在老家待不住，没人说话能活活憋死，出去打工能跟他的亲戚乡亲们住一起。）

我弟好歹也是十多年前的一本毕业，在一个三线城市，工资能拿一万多，但日子依然过得非常紧巴，压力很大，房贷，养孩子啥的。

我妹要带两个孩子，压根上不了一点班，她老公厨师，一个月能拿七八千，

他们的收入其实都不算低了，但压力真的很大，如果没有我，他们真的会，不说很苦吧，但压力真的很大。

我发达后，花了120W给我妹买了车子/房子，额外一年给5W块钱，

给我弟20W让他买车，这事比较狗血，他买了一个30W的车，居然还贷款了10W，我当时挺生气的，觉得他消费主义重，导致我决定不会给他钱了。

如果不是我赌出来，我爸妈哪天得了大病，只能活活等死，只能活活等死，你懂吗？？？

别说什么现在有城乡医保，中国人怎么会等死？
大家都是年轻人很少生病压根不知道 医保是 这不能报那不能报，这药不在报销范围内 那药不在报销范围内，尤其是大病，很多药都不在报销范围内，不然你以为啥 水滴筹上那么多人？

当年我奶就这么死的，就是因为她的儿子们全都没出息，得了大病不是想上吊就是等死。

我在上大学时，那时我才16岁，我就拼了命的挣钱/攒钱，就是因为我从小受够了没钱的穷日子了。

我经历过一年到头天天稀饭馍馍咸菜酱豆红薯面条，
我经历过我所有的衣服都是一个城里亲戚孩子不要的，童年的自尊心备受打击，
我经历过 交不上公粮狗草的村干部来家里 扒房子抢粮食抢牛，
我经历过上小学掏不出学费只能拉两袋小麦去抵，
我经历过 因为我想买一身校服，才几十块钱，我父母掏不出来，只能把我打一顿后躲背后哭，
我为什么非要想买，因为我不想穿那个盛气凌人的亲戚孩子的旧衣服。
我经历过我奶得了大病然后要上吊自杀不想连累我们……

我虽然并没什么物质欲，但我受够这些人生毫无选择权，处处窘迫的折磨了！

你还没受够吗？？？✊✊✊

text:
海湾原油出口恢复，油价上行天花板正在降低，继续做空石油

根据 Kpler 最新估算，9月中东海湾产油国不含伊朗的原油出口，已经恢复到战前水平，达到至少每天1650万桶。其中约40%的原油不再经过霍尔木兹海峡，战前这一比例只有17%，沙特和阿联酋正在更多地利用管道把原油运出去。

从这组数据来看，油价逐步回落的基础正在增强。毕竟只要原油能够持续进入市场，买家争抢替代货源的压力就会减轻，对后续断供的担忧也会下降。即使美伊暂时没有达成停战协议，供应恢复本身，也有条件推动此前涨上去的部分价格回落。

现在油价仍然偏高，也有实际原因。过去几个月消耗的库存需要时间补充，绕路和海上换船增加了运输成本，这些因素会影响油价回落的速度和幅度。

如果接下来几周出口能够维持，到货量继续增加，库存逐渐停止下降，同时需求没有明显反弹，那么油价的上行通道就会有天花板，这也是我经常说的，油价是不可能持续上涨的，而且下行通道也会逐渐打开。

目前 WTI 已经较为稳定的在 92 美元附近， Brant 的价格略高，差价达到了 8 美元左右，所以目前我一直在加仓 Brant ，理论来说差价能回到 5 美元左右，所以高价做空 Brant （BZUSDT）的性价比会更高一些。

一个 @Gate ，交易更多市场

quoted_text:
伊朗现在推动霍尔木兹海峡谈判，很可能就是想趁美国中期选举临近，把手里的筹码换成实际收益。

霍尔木兹海峡通航受阻，会持续给能源价格和美国国内政治带来压力。越接近选举，恢复通航对川普就越有价值。伊朗这时候提出快速开放海峡的方案，也就有了争取更好条件的机会。

美联社此前报道，伊朗在推介方案时，就强调过快速达成协议可能有利于川普的中期选举。

伊朗自己也有缓解压力的需要。美国对伊朗港口的封锁，以及石油销售受到的制裁，都在影响伊朗的收入。所以伊朗提出的交换条件包括解除封锁、释放被冻结资产，以及豁免石油销售制裁。继续限制通航可以向美国施压，谈判则提供了把这种压力兑现成利益的机会。

此前彭博报道的是，伊朗官员私下对“中期选举前达成协议”持悲观态度。这个表态说的是对谈判结果的预期，外交接触一直还在继续。

现在双方争的重点是条件和执行顺序。伊朗希望美国先落实相关条件，再开放霍尔木兹海峡、推进后续核问题谈判，美国则希望伊朗在核问题上作出实质承诺。所以分歧仍然还存在。

伊朗外交部长催促美国给出正式答复，说明伊朗正在推动这笔交换。这也正说明伊朗国内内部也并不太平，伊朗也希望可以快速的结束这次战争，嘴也没有那么硬了。

如果不是我赌出来，我爸妈哪天得了大病，只能活活等死，只能活活等死，你懂吗？？？

大家都是年轻人很少生病压根不知道 医保是 这不能报那不能报，这药不在报销范围内 那药不在报销范围内，尤其是大病，很多药都不在报销范围内，不然你以为啥 水滴筹上那么多人？

我在上大学时，那时我才16岁，我就拼了命的挣钱/攒钱，就是因为我从小受够了没钱的穷日子了。

text:
The birthplace of DeFi is shutting down!

Synthetix Discord was THE PLACE to be in 2019. So many blue chips of DeFi summer started there. Ideas were formed, knowledge was shared, we were off to change the world...

Aave, Curve, Optimism, Illuvium, Infinex, xToken, Kwenta, Derive, dHEDGE... So many projects were kicked off from that Discord.

$6 memes, Garth’s promised (and rugged) boat party to celebrate it all, Hobo Joe, Nikhil, the great trolls whose posts were ironically filled with insights, Spartan Council... My interactive Discord bots, before anyone had Discord bots and AI was a thing... It will all always have a special place in my heart.

There would be no Overtime, and I wouldn’t be where I am professionally and personally, were it not for Synthetix and that very Discord.

Alas, the greats have fallen hard. Not many have paid the price of vesting coming to an end as much as Synthetix. As soon as DeFi summer started winding down, no team member from the original crew was left, at least not in a full-time capacity.

The downfall has been slow but steady. Honest attempts were made to drive it forward in the meantime, but without proper guidance and direction, all failed and missed their chance. So in nutshell, it's been constant bleeding over five years.

Atm, it’s a ghost town:

- No one knows who is even on the team anymore, if there is a team.
- sUSD has been wound down, with holders promised vested SNX.
- The treasury seems to be out of runway and offloading SNX and INF to pay wages (To whom?!)
- Discord is dead. No proper comms on the path forward, just vague messages about things in store.

Synthetix and its first team taught me DeFi, the values of a DAO, and the ethics of how to spearhead a community-owned protocol.

Alas, I fear I might be the only one still adhering to those values these days.

As for Synthetix, it might be time to call it a day and spoil the good memories no further.

text:
Definitely one of the most facilitating episodes. 

A couple with 11m on paper and 1m annual income are struggling to make ends meet. And they have no idea why that happens all the time. 

When your spending is spread across mortgages, private school intuition, travel, family obligations, subscriptions, lifestyle creep and more. It becomes surprisingly easy to feel like money is disappearing despite having a high income. 

And when you don’t have a clear idea how much your lifestyle actually costs, you end up making every decision from a place of uncertainty.

The goal is not asking people saving endlessly and never spend. It should be to understand your financial life well enough to spend confidently on things that matter and know that your choices are aligned with your future goals.

a few weeks ago, a lot of people on here called Outrank a link farm

I was annoyed, but then I went and read every single reply

and some of it was fair

to get backlinks from our exchange, you had to host other people's links on your own site

and SEOs don't trust that kind of loop for good reason 👀

so for the last 8 weeks we've been building the opposite

you don't host a single link anymore

a real site writes a full article on its own blog with your link in it, and we pay that site in cash through Stripe, not credits

you can even get a listicle on a real blog with your product ranked #1

the hardest part was deciding who gets to sell

1,625 sites signed up but only 138 made it in

to qualify, a site needs:
- DR 30+
- 100+ clicks a month for at least 3 months
- Search Console connected, so we can see its real Google traffic

then it has to pass a content check, and 220 sites failed that one alone

since August we've done 222 placements

159 are live, and 158 of those are dofollow
the median time from order to published is 2.1 days

I care this much about "real" because ChatGPT and Perplexity cite the sites people actually read. nobody reads a PBN, so nobody cites one either

my bet is that AI search ends up rewarding fewer links from sites with real readers
