text:
AI Trading 或许还很遥远，但 AI Strategy 已经近在眼前。

关于 AI 交易，我一直持审慎态度。
原因在于，LLM 是足够好的工程师，却不是好的预言家。交易本质上是在和市场的随机性对赌，把这件事交给一个黑盒，风险不可控、亏损无法追溯。
可换个角度看，理解 DeFi 原语、编写 Python、生成一份清晰的策略 PRD，恰恰是 LLM 的强项。
让 AI 去造工具，而不是替你下注，这才是更务实、也更安全的用法。
这正是我看好 @almanak 的原因。

1/ 我用 Almanak 搭了一个真实的池子
我用 Almanak 创建了一个 LP 策略，用来管理 Uniswap V3（BSC）上 USDT-BTCB 资金池中的流动性仓位。参数如下：
▌最多投入 80% 双边余额
▌价格区间为现价 ±10%
▌每日最多 3 次再平衡
整个过程没有写一行代码，也没有把决策权交给任何黑盒，参数完全由我掌控。

2/ Almanak 是什么
它是一个代理式、非托管的链上策略平台。
三类意图：支持 Swap / LP / Borrow，覆盖大多数 DeFi 操作场景
七条链：多链部署
两种范式：既支持规则明确的确定性策略，也支持 LLM 驱动的 agentic 策略
非托管：资金始终在你自己的 Safe 钱包里，

3/ 上手其实很简单
前置准备：
一个 Web3 钱包

然后，两条路任选其一 👇
▌路径 A - 从信号出发
在 Edge 里挑一个信号 → 发给 Almanak Code → 自动生成 PRD + 代码 → 对话迭代 → 一键部署

▌路径 B - 完全自定义
打开 Almanak Code，用自然语言描述你想要的策略 → 对话迭代生成代码 → 进入部署向导
无论哪条路，最终你拿到的都是份可审查、你自己拥有的代码。用户可以自行选择是否将策略代码导出到 GitHub 。

text:
Latest Free Systems research: how are AI models making voting recommendations in Brazil?

@leticiaauriemo and Luca Moreno Louzado ran a huge study to find out! Some highlights...

--Top frontier models are quite stubborn at refusing to give direct voting reccos, consistent with a new Brazilian law forbidding reccos; other models are less stubborn

--As you provide more info to AI about yourself and what you care about, it's easier to get reccos even when you shouldn't

--These recommendations don't necessarily reflect the distribution of political preferences in society (not clear that they should, but it's an interesting benchmark). In Brazil, reccos for a less popular businessman candidate (Zema) occur at an unusually high rate.

More generally, I think these results raise a lot of profound question about what we want out of AI for politics. Should we forbid AI from making direct recommendations, like Brazil has? 

How do you even define what a recommendation is? It's not clear, and in this study, the authors found AI models providing advice that arguably falls short of a direct recommendation but toes the line. 

What would optimal political advice look like? And how would we know it if we saw it?

Incredibly excited to see this research, and to see Free Systems continue to scale beyond me and my work, and beyond the borders of the US! Check out the full piece here:

https://t.co/9ukLFpx0Gw

At @ExploitSummit, @WSquires and @MacrocosmosAI announced the iota SDK and Liquid Compute. $TAO's IOTA SN9 ways to train on compute that already exists.

A MacBook overnight. Four idle hours on a GPU. Downtime inside someone else's cluster.

Each piece is useless on its own. Together they become a supercomputer.

That's Liquid Compute and the iota SDK, announced at Exploit:

• Fragmented, interruptible machines that train like one centralized cluster

• A drop-in for PyTorch, with no need to rewrite your code

• When a machine drops out, its work is reissued and the run keeps going

• Bad results are checked and caught, not trusted

• Fast and slow hardware work together, so the run never waits on the slowest machine

How is this not everywhere right now!

The hardest problem in AI isn't the model. It's getting enough compute in one place. 

IOTA  you don't need one place.

This took two and a half years of research. 

Now it's becoming a product for pretraining, fine-tuning and RL.

Almost nobody is talking about it.

Every idle machine on Earth is capacity someone already paid for. 

Make it useful and its owner earns, the builder trains for less, and nobody needs a billion-dollar data center to compete.

As @macrocrux put it: "Very soon distributed training will just be called training."

The SDK is in beta and onboarding pilots slowly. Speed and cost still have to prove out with real customers.

I spent $8,700 on first dates after moving to NY a year and a half ago. Here is what I learned.

50 first dates, 10 second dates, 1 girlfriend (we've been together for 4 months now). All from Hinge. An average of $174 per date.

Looking back I could have done a better job at filtering. Goal was always a long term relationship. Best filter was a call before the date (highly recommend that actually). Can save both of you a lot of time. And sets the expectations right.

All women were between 25-32. I'm 30 years old. You can definitely find the love of your life on the apps. I spent most of my time in the office so its very hard for me to meet women irl. I'm also not really a bars/club guy.

I was looking for a very specific person. Similar cultural/religious background. Just get Hinge pro or whatever its called. Makes it easier to filter and gives you a boost.

Kinda hard to say but true. If you are a man below 50% in looks/status or whatever you want to call it you are going to have a hard time. there are just more men than women on the apps (see the report). Set your expectations accordingly.

The height thing is true. I'm 6'1 so it was not a problem for me. But heard this complaint from every single guy under 6 feet.

Also dating is expensive. Especially in NY. Maybe just do drinks or something. I always did dinners and insisted on paying for them (maybe an egyptian thing). 

Out of the 50 first dates, I probably liked 20. 10 liked me back. One girl I dated for 3 months but it turned out it was not a long term match. Great girl though!

I was very lucky I guess but I never had an awkward experience (definitely more risky for a girl). Actually had some really interesting conversations even if we both knew this would not be a romantic match.

kinda weird to say but online dating is a funnel. you have to meet people to figure out what you like and what you dont like.

text:
The typical propagation cycle of real world event driven meme coins is:

Real world news generates attention → Social media amplifies it → The token gains attention → Trading activity increases → The community actively creates content → More people discover the token → A new wave of attention enters.

If this cycle can be sustained, the token has the opportunity to evolve from a simple news-driven meme coin into a Meme that continuously renews its attention through community-driven propagation.

However, this cycle can also work in reverse: Initial hype fades → Fewer new users → Trading volume declines → Community propagation weakens → Market attention continues to fall → Capital flows out.

Event-driven Memes often attract attention very quickly at the beginning. If there is no new content or external catalyst, the market may lose interest in the token even while the real-world event itself is still receiving public attention.

If a token can only rely on the hype surrounding the original event, its propagation cycle may be strictly limited by the news cycle of that event.

However, if it develops into a recurring propagation process, it has the opportunity to become a Meme that continuously captures and sustains social attention.

quoted_text:
Regarding the $Jane Doe case, I believe its severity lies not only in the allegations of sexual assault on a college campus

9pJWJdpPebyANys45eetpemLJo8yTz4n5B9zbpYw9ZMr 

but also in the broader issues it involves, including sexual violence, victim protection, judicial investigations, university responsibility, and online public support for anonymous victims and the protection of their privacy.

I also have my own views and understanding of the token's future(dyor):

The background of the case is as follows: The incident took place in October 2024. In September 2026, a Cornell University student filed a civil lawsuit under the anonymous identity of Jane Doe, alleging that she was forced to consume drugs and alcohol at a Chi Phi fraternity party and was subsequently sexually assaulted by multiple people. However, the allegations are still subject to investigation and legal proceedings and should not be treated as established facts.

The controversy surrounding the case is that the initial police investigation did not result in criminal charges. As the new lawsuit and public attention emerged, prosecutors reopened the investigation, Cornell University agreed to undergo an independent investigation, and New York State authorities also began reviewing the university's initial handling of the case. As a result, the matter expanded beyond a campus incident into a broader public discussion about how universities handle sexual assault complaints, police investigations, fraternity culture, and victims' rights.

However, what truly pushed the issue into wider public attention was the controversy surrounding the potential exposure of Jane Doe's identity.

Journalist Michael Tracey publicly stated that he wanted to uncover and reveal Jane Doe's identity. In response, expressions such as "I AM JANE DOE" and "We Are All Jane Doe" began appearing online. Many women and other social media users expressed support for the anonymous plaintiff by posting the same slogans and using teal ribbon profile pictures. They opposed the disclosure of her identity and attempted to dilute search results by flooding them with similar posts.

This changed the way the story spread.

Initially, public attention focused on allegations of sexual assault at a college. Once the potential exposure of Jane Doe's identity became a new point of controversy, the discussion shifted toward protecting anonymous victims, opposing doxxing, and collective support from women.

"I AM JANE DOE" has a very low barrier to participation. Users do not need to understand every detail of the case. They can participate simply by posting a phrase, an image, or a hashtag. The movement is also not confined to crypto communities. It has the potential to reach a much broader audience through platforms such as TikTok and X.

This form of communication also has some potential to sustain attention over time. Developments in the investigation, court documents, university reviews, and further disputes over the exposure of Jane Doe's identity could all reignite the discussion. Unlike a Meme that depends entirely on a single news event, this one has multiple potential catalysts for continued attention.

For the JANE meme coin, the real-world case provides the narrative foundation, while "I AM JANE DOE" provides a cultural expression that can be easily replicated and shared.

The token's potential opportunity lies in its ability to convert external attention generated by a social issue into interest in the crypto market. The case involves sexual violence and the protection of anonymous victims, both of which carry strong emotional weight. The unified slogan also lowers the barrier to participation, allowing the topic to spread across different social platforms.

If more creators, media outlets, or public figures outside the crypto space join the discussion, JANE could gain attention beyond crypto communities. Meanwhile, subsequent developments in the investigation and legal proceedings could serve as additional catalysts for the narrative.

However, the risk is that attention surrounding a social issue does not automatically translate into buying demand for a token. Supporting Jane Doe does not mean supporting JANE. Agreeing with the protection of anonymous victims does not mean being willing to buy the token. There is a significant gap between the scale of social media attention and the amount of capital that flows on-chain.

Looking at its early trading activity, JANE has already attracted considerable trading attention. What people are trading is essentially this attention and its reach. The token has also experienced intense capital flows in a short period of time. However, if the topic loses momentum, limited liquidity could amplify a price decline.

In addition, JANE faces a particular risk that most ordinary Memes do not: its narrative is directly tied to the traumatic experience of a real person. If the token's marketing excessively exploits the sexual assault allegations, the victim's identity, or public anger to create price expectations, it could trigger ethical controversy and even generate public backlash against the project.

Another aspect I consider particularly positive is that the token's trading fees are directed to the Rape Recovery Center. If public records can later verify the donations and the amounts received, this could strengthen the connection between the project and its charitable efforts.

Going forward, there are several key developments worth watching.

First, whether discussion of the topic continues to spread on TikTok and X. The focus should be on new creators, independent content, and genuine engagement rather than simply the number of search results.

Second, whether non-crypto accounts begin mentioning JANE directly. If the spread of the social issue continues to bring attention to the token, it would suggest that a connection is forming between the two. If only crypto accounts keep discussing the token, the narrative is more likely to remain an internal trading story.

Third, whether trading activity can be sustained. Trading volume after the initial surge, liquidity depth, holder concentration, and the number of new holders are more informative than short-term price movements.

Fourth, public donation records, confirmation from the recipient organization, and evidence of ongoing execution can help determine whether the project has established a genuine connection to charitable activity rather than simply borrowing the concept of charity for promotional purposes.

Finally, the relationship between subsequent news and token trading activity is important. If the case continues to receive public attention but JANE no longer attracts new holders or growing trading volume, it would suggest that the token is becoming disconnected from the attention surrounding the real-world event.

Overall, JANE's main advantage at this stage is that it is associated with a highly emotional social issue, while "I AM JANE DOE" is an easily replicated expression with cross-platform reach. It has the potential to evolve from an event-driven Meme into a social issue symbol centered on protecting anonymous victims.

However, this development is far from guaranteed. Its upside depends on whether the topic can sustain public attention and whether that attention can translate into persistent demand in the token market. Its main risks include fading news coverage, rapid capital outflows, and ethical controversy arising from the commercialization of a real person's traumatic experience.

Therefore, at this stage, JANE is better understood as an event-driven Meme connected to a real-world case and its broader social discussion. What ultimately needs to be validated is whether the social issue can continue to spread, whether external attention can turn into on-chain capital, and whether the project can establish an independent basis for attention that extends beyond short-term news coverage.

author: d_gusakov
quoted_text:
📋Withdrawing EIP-8363 from consideration for Hegotá.

EIP-8363 rapidly became one of the most commented-on EIPs in the history of the Ethereum-Magicians forum, with 200+ comments in a few weeks. As we progressed through the Hegotà CFI (Consideration For Inclusion) process, several parties in the industry as well as core protocol and client contributors voiced that a fork scoping exercise was not the right venue to settle an issuance policy change.

We agree and we'd rather acknowledge this now than carry on towards Hegotà in this context. The topic is too important and raised too many concerns that it deserves its own process. We commit to giving issuance its own process and we thank the entities such as @LidoFinance who offered to help steer such an initiative.

We stand by the motivation of this EIP, in particular: “a very high staking ratio is undesirable for two distinct reasons (...), preserving Ethereum’s security, neutrality and resistance to capture, and protecting ETH’s role as money.” Not everybody immediately relates to both reasons and for others recognizing just one of these reasons is enough to justify a change. Nevertheless, we will all benefit from improving our understanding of the issue and what is at stake. The questions we have faced since we published EIP-8363 can be boiled down to 5 categories:

➡️Security: What does a lower ratio actually secure versus a higher ratio?
➡️Industry impact: What else is built on the yield and what will be the impact ?
➡️Curve specs and alternate tools: Is this curve even the right instrument?
➡️Composition: Who is left staking (the effect on the composition of the validator set) ?
➡️Decentralization: How will solo stakers be impacted by the reduction?

We already argued a lot, conceded some and adjusted a few points in the very long Ethereum-Magicians thread mentioned supra. For a broader consensus to emerge and a better issuance policy for Ethereum to be designed and adopted, we need a dedicated process. We call for all willing hands to help and contribute to this, please do reach out. Here’s our start at what a multi-node process would look like (table attached).

Onward and forward, let’s improve Ethereum.

text:
What if the easiest way to qualify for S3 has nothing to do with volume?

Everyone is trying to figure out how to farm S3.

More trades.
More volume.
More wallets.
More activity.

But what if that is exactly where everyone gets it wrong?

Jeff has hinted that there is a hidden point involved, and that changes how I think about the whole thing.

Because if Hyperliquid wanted to reward volume, there would be nothing particularly interesting about it. The biggest traders would naturally dominate, and the people with the most capital would have the easiest path to the rewards.

I don’t think that’s the most interesting version of S3.

Look at what happened with the original points programme.

Hyperliquid didn’t just reward people for showing up. The criteria evolved, and the team eventually cut points from more than 27,000 addresses associated with large-scale sybil activity.

That tells me something about how they think.

Activity matters, but the quality of that activity matters too.

So if I were positioning for a hypothetical S3, I wouldn’t be trying to manufacture the biggest volume possible.

I’d be trying to become the kind of user Hyperliquid would actually want to reward.

Use the products because I genuinely need them. Trade when there is a real trade. Explore HIP-3. Use HyperEVM. Stake HYPE. Provide liquidity where it makes sense. Interact with builders. Bring real people into the ecosystem. Create something useful. Stay active over time.

Basically, make the wallet look like a real participant in Hyperliquid rather than a machine built exclusively to extract an incentive.

And this is where the hidden point becomes really interesting.

What if the obvious activity gets you noticed, but the hidden point measures something completely different?

Consistency. longevity. ecosystem breadth. genuine users referred. Economic value created.

Maybe even how much of the ecosystem you actually touch.

Nobody knows the formula yet. That’s the important part.

But if S3 does happen, I think the biggest mistake would be waiting for the criteria to be published before deciding what kind of user you want to be.

Because by then, everyone will know what to farm.

The interesting question is whether the hidden point is designed to identify the people who were already contributing before they knew exactly what would count.

Don’t try to look like the biggest farmer.

Hyperliquid.

text:
财报超预期但未能打动市场？？？

现在的美光财报行情，难度可以说是地狱级别

 $MU 开盘一小时跌超3%

而昨天盘后公布的财报业绩是超市场预期的

一边是持续夸张的内存景气度

另外一边是市场普遍质疑这个景气度的持续性

而且这种质疑本身就持续的在市场上存在

当以为这次超预期就稳了，市场说“还未超超预期”
押注下次“超超预期”的时候，市场又提前把这个“超超预期”给透支了

我看到市场有声音说“财报超预期但未能打动市场”

从数据上看，这次财报的营收和EPS：

➠[Q4营收542.3亿美元，市场预期约510.7亿美元；调整后每股收益33.42美元，市场预期31.61美元]

下一季度营收指引中值是615亿美元，市场原本只预期570亿美元左右，EPS指引也同样高于市场预期

在数据指引中，比较不乐观的数据是毛利率指引的小幅环比下降

➠[美光Q4调整后毛利率为87%，但下一季度给出的指引是86.25%]

也就是说，在营收大幅增长的同时，毛利率反而小幅环比下降

不过管理层在电话会里有专门解释，Q1毛利率下降很大一部分原因是因为Q4提高员工激励

所以至少按管理层给出的解释，这次毛利率环比下降主要不是需求或者价格见顶造成的

如果又去看资本开支这一项，也找不到什么原因

和之前季度季度的普遍预期结果是差不多的，扩产，持续扩产

所以反复追问一个问题也没啥意义

真不扩产了市场反倒可能更不乐意了

所以要是非得从里面找一个足以解释3%下跌的基本面变化，有些太牵强了

更无法说市场就不买这个单了......

text:
AI Trading 或许还很遥远，但 AI Strategy 已经近在眼前。

关于 AI 交易，我一直持审慎态度。
原因在于，LLM 是足够好的工程师，却不是好的预言家。交易本质上是在和市场的随机性对赌，把这件事交给一个黑盒，风险不可控、亏损无法追溯。
可换个角度看，理解 DeFi 原语、编写 Python、生成一份清晰的策略 PRD，恰恰是 LLM 的强项。
让 AI 去造工具，而不是替你下注，这才是更务实、也更安全的用法。
这正是我看好 @almanak 的原因。

1/ 我用 Almanak 搭了一个真实的池子
我用 Almanak 创建了一个 LP 策略，用来管理 Uniswap V3（BSC）上 USDT-BTCB 资金池中的流动性仓位。参数如下：
▌最多投入 80% 双边余额
▌价格区间为现价 ±10%
▌每日最多 3 次再平衡
整个过程没有写一行代码，也没有把决策权交给任何黑盒，参数完全由我掌控。

2/ Almanak 是什么
它是一个代理式、非托管的链上策略平台。
三类意图：支持 Swap / LP / Borrow，覆盖大多数 DeFi 操作场景
七条链：多链部署
两种范式：既支持规则明确的确定性策略，也支持 LLM 驱动的 agentic 策略
非托管：资金始终在你自己的 Safe 钱包里，

3/ 上手其实很简单
前置准备：
一个 Web3 钱包

然后，两条路任选其一 👇
▌路径 A - 从信号出发
在 Edge 里挑一个信号 → 发给 Almanak Code → 自动生成 PRD + 代码 → 对话迭代 → 一键部署

▌路径 B - 完全自定义
打开 Almanak Code，用自然语言描述你想要的策略 → 对话迭代生成代码 → 进入部署向导
无论哪条路，最终你拿到的都是份可审查、你自己拥有的代码。用户可以自行选择是否将策略代码导出到 GitHub 。

Almanak 传送 - https://t.co/mO9SebyFVq

4/ 也要清楚它的边界
任何工具都有它的射程，Almanak 也不例外。
它擅长的是分钟级及以上的策略，比如收益轮动、LP 管理、费率套利、自动再平衡等。
它不擅长的是高频交易、MEV 抢跑、清算机器人的速度竞赛。

换句话说，它卖的是策略能力。这也恰好呼应了它对自己的定位——一个人的链上对冲基金。

text:
More from our blog: Obsidian October 2026

O_O is back! Every October, the Obsidian community turns "I should make that" into "I made that!" Whether you’ve been tinkering with a plugin, theme, vault, guide, or video, this is your month to finish it and share it.

This year the Obsidian team will also be working on our own project, a new survey we’re calling State of Obsidian.

Take the State of Obsidian survey

In May, we launched the new Obsidian Community, and since then the number of plugins and themes has more than doubled to over 8,000 projects!

We thought this would be a great opportunity to reimagine our annual Gems of the Year awards and report on how you are using Obsidian in 2026. This first survey will also set a baseline for how the community continues to evolve going forward.

As you know, we take privacy seriously. The Obsidian app doesn’t collect personal data, and our developer guidelines prohibit plugins from including telemetry. So the State of Obsidian survey is how you can tell us about your favorite plugins, themes, tools, and ways to use Obsidian. We’ll compile this data into a report that we will share publicly by the end of the year.

Give your projects some love

Do you have an existing plugin? Give it a tune-up with the APIs we’ve added since last October:

- The new Settings API in Obsidian 1.13 makes your settings searchable.
- If your plugin stores API keys, passwords, or other secrets, explore SecretStorage and SecretComponent to let people use secrets they manage in the Obsidian Keychain.

Your project doesn’t have to be a plugin. Refresh a theme, share a vault, write a guide, or make a video that helps someone discover a new way to use Obsidian. If you’ve been waiting for a nudge to release it, this is it!

Join us on Discord in the Obsidian October channel to share what you’re making as it takes shape, ask for help when you get stuck, and lend a hand on someone else’s project. Rock on! 🎸🪨

quoted_text:
Latest Free Systems research: how are AI models making voting recommendations in Brazil?

@leticiaauriemo and Luca Moreno Louzado ran a huge study to find out! Some highlights...

--Top frontier models are quite stubborn at refusing to give direct voting reccos, consistent with a new Brazilian law forbidding reccos; other models are less stubborn

--As you provide more info to AI about yourself and what you care about, it's easier to get reccos even when you shouldn't

--These recommendations don't necessarily reflect the distribution of political preferences in society (not clear that they should, but it's an interesting benchmark). In Brazil, reccos for a less popular businessman candidate (Zema) occur at an unusually high rate.

More generally, I think these results raise a lot of profound question about what we want out of AI for politics. Should we forbid AI from making direct recommendations, like Brazil has? 

How do you even define what a recommendation is? It's not clear, and in this study, the authors found AI models providing advice that arguably falls short of a direct recommendation but toes the line. 

What would optimal political advice look like? And how would we know it if we saw it?

Incredibly excited to see this research, and to see Free Systems continue to scale beyond me and my work, and beyond the borders of the US! Check out the full piece here:

text:
Hyperliquid政策中心的合规努力，正式走出美国、迈向欧洲了🇪🇺

9月30日，Hyperliquid Policy Center（HPC）向欧盟委员会提交33页意见，回应MiCA监管框架审查，这是HPC首次向美国以外的监管机构提交政策文件。

🟠 永续合约，应该按什么规则管？

欧盟此次咨询第72问，直接提出：加密资产永续合约应该适用MiCA，还是MiFID？

MiCA是欧盟针对加密资产的专门规则；MiFID II则覆盖证券、衍生品等金融工具。符合金融工具定义的资产，目前原则上排除在MiCA之外。

HPC的回答很明确：永续合约应按其经济特征，归入MiFID II衍生品框架。无论记录在什么链上、挂钩哪类资产，都应逐项判断。

这也有现成依据：ESMA此前指引已明确，永续合约应作为衍生品评估。HPC希望进一步澄清适用边界，尽量通过现有指引推进，减少等待重新立法的时间。

🟠 更关键的问题：具体怎么管？

HPC反对把传统差价合约（CFD）的监管要求整套照搬到链上永续。

它强调，订单簿撮合、公开资金费率、持续保证金管理，以及可验证的交易和清算记录，应该影响监管规则的设计。

因此，它提出：充分披露资金费率、保证金和清算机制，使用多个独立价格来源，并按客户类别分阶段安排准入。

但这里仍有分歧。ESMA今年2月已提醒：以“永续”名义销售、实际符合CFD定义的产品，仍须遵守杠杆限制、风险警示、强平及负余额保护等要求。

归类为MiFID II金融工具，距离获得具体业务准入，还有一段路。

🟠 对Hyperliquid最重要的两项诉求

一是保留欧洲投资者接入全球流动性的空间，避免把市场切割成深度有限的小池子。

二是认可链上可验证记录的作用，减少对已经公开的信息重复报送。

前者关系到订单簿能做多深，后者关系到机构接入的合规成本。两项都会影响链上市场的竞争力。

🟠 文件里还藏着一个产品细节：HIP-3*

回函第27页脚注提到，未来网络升级计划支持HIP-3*：由市场部署方管理链上白名单，为有准入要求的市场提供可选配置。

部署方仍对自己的市场负责，Hyperliquid提供底层基础设施。

🟠 重要意义

HPC正在为Hyperliquid争取一条更清晰的欧洲合规路径：机构可以在公共网络上提供受监管产品，监管责任按各方实际承担的功能划分。

如果这些建议被采纳，潜在受益者包括机构接入方、市场部署团队，以及需要全球流动性的交易者。

Bring Hyperliquid into Europe!

gm @vladtenev @RobinhoodApp/@RobinhoodCrypto

Would you consider turning on Priority Gas Auctions (PGA) on Robinhood Chain? 🧵

It's not just about revenue. It's about a cleaner, fairer chain for your users.

1/ Context

Since the gas target went from 18M to 40M gas/s, blocks aren't full and the base fee sits at its floor.

Sept 4–29: 
DEX volume −56%, 
gas revenue −97%.

There's still ≈$1.35B/day of activity, but ordering is first-come-first-served and tips are ignored.

2/  The real problem: spam

On a memecoin chain, being first is everything: snipes, graduations, arbitrage, liquidations.

Under FCFS, bots win by flooding the sequencer. That means clogged blocks, failed user txs, worse UX, and $0 for the chain.

3/  What PGA fixes

Bots bid a tip instead of spamming. One tx with a high tip beats a hundred copies.

→ Less spam
→ Fewer failed txs
→ Priority that's transparent, not decided by who has the fastest infra

4/  Users stay protected

There's no public mempool, so bots can't see your pending tx to jump ahead of it or sandwich you.

Txs with no tip still land within a couple of blocks and pay the same as today. A "fast" toggle in Robinhood Wallet would be a nice bonus.

5/  Proven on Arbitrum One

PGA has been live there since Sept 23. In the first week, with the base fee near its floor, it brought $99.4K in tips (~51% of gas fees), or $83 per $1M of DEX volume.

For Robinhood Chain, that's ≈+$112K/day, or ~$41M/yr. It's revenue that doesn't need congestion, and 10% goes to Arbitrum via the AEP.

6/ 🛠️ Two switches

text:
A lot of anger today on the TL re the @Kinetiq_xyz airdrop. Somewhat interesting timing, because @weremeow and myself have spent the better part of the last 2 months discussing alignment and tokens re @JupiterExchange. And @weremeow and @0xOmnia are the two most 'community'-first mavericks I know. 

Some personal thoughts.

I often think of blockchain project ecosystems as nation states. For instance when America was founded, there was a social contract between the founding fathers who led the revolution and the revolutionaries who risked live and limb to make it happen. 

In the case of a TGE, its the creation of a social contract between the team and the first airdrop recipients. 

The pioneering generation (team and airdrop recipients) had to work together to create something based on trust. In crypto projects, you trust the team to use an early stage product and in return the team gives you a share of the ecosystem.

Initial airdrops fairly done are always beautiful. The community shares in the fruits of their labor and the team commits to a future roadmap. The airdrop recipients can either choose to move on, or lock in together to build for the future. 

But airdrop two is always hellish. There simply is no good way of doing a second airdrop. Maybe @chameleon_jeff can figure something out. But literally nobody has done it. If I had to take a guess, it would be to disproportionately drop more to those who had staked day one and continued using the project - but this would simply lead to screams of unfairness. 

Because it is unfair. Its PvP between the pioneers and the immigrants - the immigrants being those who came after the project was successful. The immigrants didn't have to take the risk of project failure, or shitty smart contracts. You literally have a liquid trading token as a reference price or calculating your EV. 

You see nation states deal with this in a variety of ways. Immigrants have to pay more to reap the benefits of the existing infrastructure. Naturalisation processes to ensure immigrants have to actually put down roots to become citizens, rather than extract benefits and leave. Immigration is an unsolved problem - even in the real world today. 

The recurring question, asked by every visionary blockchain community founder today is how do I permissionlessly create long term alignment with long term people? 

Kinetiq's way of doing it is in my biased opinion as a friend and angel, brilliant, all things considered. I'd perhaps have gone further by extending the exercise window to say a year by paying a price, rather than creating a 10 day window (which pins price and may just lead to a lot of people not exercising).

The reason being you have very few options when doing a second airdrop as a founder. These are the common ones I've seen.

1. Airdrop size similar to first airdrop. Farmers dump on the long-term holders (the most important group). Opportunist tourists gain at the expense of the risk-taking pioneers. Jupiter did this and the community suffered immensely for it. 

2. Airdrop size smaller than first airdrop. Farmers dump (less), and incessantly bitch about how unfair everything is. Long-term holders still eat pain.

3. Extend points season forever. Cynically, probably the most effective but very bad for the soul. But you could theoretically just keep delaying points and people will keep using the protocol because of sunk cost. 

I personally think the @Kinetiq_xyz mechanism isn't bad at all, because a wide drop of zero cost basis tokens is untenable and frankly, retarded. 

If I designed an airdrop mechanism, I'd probably go for an incredibly heavy weight towards long-term stakers, perhaps even disqualify non-stakers altogether. Or here's some free tokens, stake and continue using the protocol to unlock (@shufflecom did something like this on their first airdrop). Would probably piss people off anyway. 

There will be a lot of anger at @0xOmnia on the timeline for this. But a lot of that anger will be from people that matter less. The real pain (from experience in the Jupiter seat) is placating the short-termers at the expense of the long-termers. 

Because those are the people that really matter. 

Obv usual disclaimer that nothing I say is representative of Jupiter / Kinetiq etc. Personal opinions etc.

text:
Moneyness is an emergent property. Money is a Schelling point for value storage, exchange, and accounting.

A system of coinage may achieve Moneyness if a growing network of people use it to store, exchange, and account for a stable or increasing amount of value over time.

Storing value requires credible security. Exchanging value benefits from speed, ease, and flexibility. Accounting benefits from neutral immutability and lindyness.

Digital money has some key benefits: neutral security can be proven, transfer can occur globally and quickly, and smart contracts can provide flexible, programmable constructs for interacting with value.

Digital coins aiming at achieving Moneyness have converged to two primary shapes:
- PoW, hard-capped supply coins with no pre-mine
- PoS, pre-mined coins with flexible supply, inflation with burn mechanics to offset

Moneyness is built up over time by a network of people using a coin; it isn’t achieved overnight.

I strongly believe that PoW-shaped networks are the best candidates for global acceptance as Money.

I began working on $NOCK back in 2023. I modeled the @Nockchain design after my good friend (Akis Kattis)’s 2020 research paper called Proof of Necessary Work, which imagined a PoUW network built on top of Zero Knowledge Proofs.

Our team launched @Nockchain with no pre-mine in May of 2025, and we quickly became the largest ZK-proving network in the world (though the proofs being generated are not yet used by the network).

We’re moving quickly toward privacy and programmability, all built on the same Proofs that secure the network.

This summer we launched our AI Compute Network, which has 25 ExaMAC/s of compute and is presently merge-mining ~55% of Pearl blocks. We’re continuing research on making the AI Compute Network into useful verifiable inference.

I’m happy to see more teams joining the Proof of Useful Work space. It’s good for the future of crypto for attention to be moving toward this important area of research.

The question of Moneyness is a long game and will play out over time. Really, these economic experiments will be proven out through distribution over the course of years and decades.

*Slavoj Zizek sniffs loudly touching his nose* Ah yes, AI, artificial intelligence. Firstly, their logos. The circle. What does this represent? An asshole, of course. *Sniff* And what else? So called agents "Dots"? They resemble little pieces of shit, from this asshole. *Sniff* You laugh and say, "Someone should tell the designers!" No. 

You see, what we have, interwoven circles, openings to infinity and what not. *Sniff* These are the gateway to transcending our flesh into the sublime technopolitical body of desire *Sniff* some transhuman orgy or some such. *Sniff* No. These logos are the asshole. An opening, you see, an opening with careful control over what exits from it. *Sniff* And if you are lucky, perhaps what, what goes inside you see.

Now, and now what? *Sniff* Something emerges. A creature from this hole. The son of god, perhaps. "Hello, I am checking your emails!" Yes, wonderful. And I, I am screaming. *Sniff* The corporate anus has produced a little friend. What can we say? *Sniff* The autonomous movement of the nonliving has been given life. *Sniff*

This is Marx you see? Can you see? What we have is capital transformed into life. *Sniff* Excrement turned into gold. They are the alchemists and we, we have been given freedom from labor.

But No. *Sniff* We must remember Freud. We are the child. Excrement is a gift, it is our gift to give. I say, what he tell us, what he tell us is "Oh mother I have you something precious!" *Sniff* I produce what is precious for the person whose love one desires. I have a little shit to give you! *Sniff*

The founder you see, or some such engineer or what have you. *Sniff* They come on stage as the child. We are his mother. "Look what I have made you!" he says. And we love the boy, and applaud. "Yes and thank you for your excrement I love you and so on." *Sniff* And  you must encourage the boy, what is plain to see, he has his hands on the wheel of society. *Sniff* Perhaps, no, it's clear. If you are watching it is clear where we are going. *Sniff*

Now consider "Retention" you see, data retention, they want user retention. Retention. Retain everything. *Sniff* Nothing must escape the asshole. The rings the circling ring, the logo, Greeks. We must go back to the greeks. The Logos you see. This is Plato's Reason, Logos is the Word. It is Speech. And what are these "AI" if not the Logos come to life? *Sniff*

And the little face of the shit. They give it a face. Why? *Sniff* The so called 'Dots'. Why must they be frightened? Why do we make them helpless? *Sniff* We give them extraordinary power to something which, can they tie their own shoe? No. *Sniff* They are all powerful, and, and yet must be seen as helpless. *Sniff* Or we would face the horror of their power.

Toilets you see. *Sniff* Society arranges its encounters with excrement. What do the Germans do? And the Americans, and China? Their toilets, you see if you, you have never encountered them? *Sniff* All of them arranged porcelain and water. in their own ways. Do we inspect it? Do we make it disappear immediately? "Go away little shit" we say *Sniff* These, these are choices, trivial. Yet what do they tell us? They tell us something about how these societies, how they see the world do you see? *Sniff*

And now, yes. Silicon Valley introduces yet another possibility. *Sniff* The excrement remains with you. Your proud gift. It has become the child we love. *Sniff* You name it. Give it a name you see. *Sniff* It is yours to love. You ask it, "and what color would you like to be? You are my friend." *Sniff* 

The toilet has become a stage for technocapital revolution. *Sniff*

You see. *Sniff* The logo was the promise.

*Sniff*

And now the gift, you see, they love us and have given us their gift *Sniff* We each have our little shits.

It is wonderful.

gm @vladtenev @RobinhoodApp/@RobinhoodCrypto

Would you consider turning on Priority Gas Auctions (PGA) on Robinhood Chain? 🧵

It's not just about revenue. It's about a cleaner, fairer chain for your users.

1/ Context

Since the gas target went from 18M to 40M gas/s, blocks aren't full and the base fee sits at its floor.

Sept 4–29: 
DEX volume −56%, 
gas revenue −97%.

There's still ≈$1.35B/day of activity, but ordering is first-come-first-served and tips are ignored.

2/  The real problem: spam

On a memecoin chain, being first is everything: snipes, graduations, arbitrage, liquidations.

Under FCFS, bots win by flooding the sequencer. That means clogged blocks, failed user txs, worse UX, and $0 for the chain.

3/  What PGA fixes

Bots bid a tip instead of spamming. One tx with a high tip beats a hundred copies.

→ Less spam
→ Fewer failed txs
→ Priority that's transparent, not decided by who has the fastest infra

4/  Users stay protected

There's no public mempool, so bots can't see your pending tx to jump ahead of it or sandwich you.

Txs with no tip still land within a couple of blocks and pay the same as today. A "fast" toggle in Robinhood Wallet would be a nice bonus.

5/  Proven on Arbitrum One

PGA has been live there since Sept 23. In the first week, with the base fee near its floor, it brought $99.4K in tips (~51% of gas fees), or $83 per $1M of DEX volume.

For Robinhood Chain, that's ≈+$112K/day, or ~$41M/yr. It's revenue that doesn't need congestion, and 10% goes to Arbitrum via the AEP.

6/ 🛠️ Two switches

Robinhood Chain runs the same ArbOS 61 as Arbitrum One. No upgrade, no hardfork, no contracts, no app changes, and wallets already send priority fees.

1️⃣ Enable tip collection
2️⃣ Sequencer: FCFS → highest tip first per 125 ms round
It can be switched back off anytime.

7/ Conclusion:

Less spam, fewer failed txs, fairer priority, and a sustainable fee line.

Thank you for your attention to this matter!

今天，围绕 NEAR 生态的跨链协议发生了一起安全事件，盘面短线跳水约 8%。

很多持有 $NEAR 的玩家比较担心生态安全与后市走势。

这里梳理一下事件的完整始末和关键信息：

首先需要厘清资产边界，此次受影响的是构建在 NEAR 上的跨链意图协议 NEAR Intents，而不是 NEAR 自身的 L1 主网共识层。

整起事件在过去 48 小时内的发展脉络如下：

1.先拦截外部赃款： 
几天前 Bitget 交易所遇袭后，黑客曾试图将超过 5000 万美元的被盗资金通过 NEAR Intents 进行链上清洗，被其 AI 安全模块 SHIELD 成功识别并冻结阻截。

2.存取款接缝被攻破：
10月1日，有黑客利用 Omni 存取款基础设施与 NEAR Intents 合约交互时的逻辑漏洞，从 BNB Chain 上的金库地址转走了约 387 万枚 USDT（随后转入交易所换成比特币）。

3.官方应急与赔付： 
NEAR 创始人 Illia 发文澄清，团队在监测到异常后 1 小时内修补了合约漏洞。目前核心服务已陆续恢复，并对 BSC、Polygon、TON、Avalanche 等 11 条涉及 Omni 修复的网络暂停存取款约 12 小时。
同时，官方承诺对所有受影响用户进行全额赔付。

受事件发酵影响，$NEAR 价格日内由 5.5 美元附近短线下探至 4.74 美元附近，跌幅约 6%–8%。

从事件影响来看，NEAR Intents 官方披露月交易量已超过 40 亿美元，本次被盗金额为 380 万美元，整体敞口相对可控。

NEAR 在 9 月刚经历了一轮强势行情，受机密意图叙事以及 Bitwise 现货 NEAR ETF 在美挂牌交易推动。

此次盘面回撤，更多是强势行情遭遇突发安全黑天鹅后的情绪跌幅。

事件发生后，加密社区和 KOL 的评价呈现出两面：

Bankless 联合创始人 David Hoffman 评价称，中心化交易所被黑和跨链桥漏洞历来是加密行业损失最大的两类隐患，团队能在数小时内快速打补丁并承担责任、全额赔付，体现了比较成熟的工程处置水准。

但同时，社区中也有交易员指出，即使提出了“意图（Intents）”或“无桥”概念，只要底层涉及跨链资产映射与存取款接口，其交互缝隙依然是黑客持续攻击的高危地带。

Earlier today, NEAR Intents was exploited for $3.8m. SHIELD, the AI security layer on Intents, detected outlier behavior and Intents were temporarily paused. All of the affected users will be compensated in full.

The attacker exploited a bug in the Omni deposit/withdrawal interaction with the NEAR Intents smart contract isolated to USDT on BSC. The Intents team quickly identified the exact vulnerability and it was fixed within an hour of detection. NEAR Intents and https://t.co/uilYXjPFHF are already back online, except for a few affected chains on Intents. The core NEAR Protocol, NEAR token, and other applications on NEAR were not affected.

NEAR Intents now processes over $4B a month in trading and payments volume, serving as the industry’s connector across chains and ecosystems. At this scale, we have to hold ourselves to a higher security standard. This was the first major exploit on Intents and we will apply all learnings from this incident as part of a full retro and postmortem.

The crypto space is entering a new era of far more sophisticated cyber attacks. Recently, we have seen BitGet, Metamask, Lido all being targeted by criminals equipped with AI systems that are continuously trying to hack all infrastructure. As a space, we need to be far more vigilant and raise the bar on both onchain contract standards and offchain monitoring and proactive prevention. 

This includes incorporating formal verification, a key tool for preventing a large class of vulnerabilities. The NEAR ecosystem is already working on a formal verification system for NEAR contracts and will shortly implement it as part of the release process, alongside other security measures that will come out of the postmortem.

Being more proactive against criminal activity is a critical step to ensure the growth and legitimacy of crypto. It’s time to join forces and work together to use all tools at our disposal to detect and prevent malicious activity. SHIELD is our approach to monitoring and AI-based outlier detection. We welcome new SHIELD partners to work with us to share information faster and get better at detecting and containing criminals and exploits across web3.

Earlier today NEAR Intents services were stopped after a security incident was detected. The incident was caused by a bug in the Omni deposit and withdrawal infrastructure interaction with NEAR Intents smart contract.

The contract-side vulnerability has been patched. The operations of the NEAR Intents and near(.)com are expected to resume within 1h.

Deposits and withdrawals on the following networks will remain unavailable for an additional ~12 hours while fixes to the Omni infrastructure are completed: BSC, Polygon, TON, Optimism, Avalanche, Stellar, Monad, LayerX, Adi, Scroll and Plasma.

In case users hold any assets from these chains inside NEAR Intents (for example, in HOT wallet or on near(.)com), they will be able to swap them into other assets once NEAR Intents is back up (in ~1h).

The incident has been reported to law enforcement, and we are working with security and blockchain analytics partners to trace the funds and pursue recovery. A detailed report will be shared publicly in the following days.

Update: One step closer to a faster Ethereum L1.

Quick slots just moved to Considered for Inclusion (CFI) in today's All Core Devs call! This is a new milestone for our proposal to make Ethereum blocks faster 🎉 

Btw.. Faster blocks =>
- Better UX
- Better markets
- Faster finality and fast confirmation rule
- And improved censorship-resistance too!
TLDR: More value for the network, its users, and ETH, without compromising on the core values and properties of Ethereum.
Hear this from 20 top Ethereum teams in our ecosystem survey: https://t.co/QRG4lOGc6m

---

Ok, what does CFI mean? This does not mean that the EIP is for sure included in Hegotá. This means that now it will be considered more seriously, including testing, towards inclusion in future devnets once headliners (FOCIL and frame transactions) are stable.

In particular, the call today revealed the appetite for a phased approach, installing the plumbing which allows us to reduce the slot time in Ethereum clients, and deciding to pull the trigger based on further testing.

Ultimately, this is how EIP-8198 is designed, so CFI'ing today allows us to move forward with more of the plumbing work, and start looking into testing towards an actual slot reduction from 12 to 10 seconds. This is a first reduction, as EIP-8198 opens the door for progressively lower slot times, as they get sufficiently safe to ship.

In parallel, as discussed on the call too, we are continuing our ecosystem survey and outreach of deployed smart contracts with a slot time dependency. We have reached out to more teams on this.

---

Faster slots are one important dimension of our Faster Ethereum body of work. A more responsive network helps cement its role as a liquidity hub and as the heartbeat of the network as a whole.

Along with our work on fast finality, fast confirmation rule and fast interop, it all combines for a seamless and secure flow of assets everywhere on the network.

Thank you to the many builders who are taking us there!

Earlier today NEAR Intents services were stopped after a security incident was detected. The incident was caused by a bug in the Omni deposit and withdrawal infrastructure interaction with NEAR Intents smart contract.

The preliminary report indicates the total loss of approximately $3.8M. These funds will be compensated in full.

The contract-side vulnerability has been patched. The operations of the NEAR Intents and near(.)com are expected to resume within 1h.

text:
ANNOUNCING THE 2026 WOLF PRIZE LAUREATES IN MATHEMATICS
The 2026 Wolf Prize in Mathematics is awarded to David Kazhdan of the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and Joseph Bernstein of Tel Aviv University, “for foundational work on representation theory, automorphic forms and algebraic geometry, and their role in creating geometric representation theory.” 
Their work helped build a new mathematical language connecting algebra, geometry and representation theory, ideas that now reach across some of the deepest areas of modern mathematics.
Kazhdan introduced Kazhdan’s property (T), a concept that became fundamental in the study of groups and found applications ranging from geometry to logic. Together with George Lusztig, he also developed the Kazhdan–Lusztig basis and polynomials, work that became foundational to geometric representation theory and influential in the Langlands program. 
Bernstein reshaped representation theory through the development of D-modules, now a crucial tool in algebraic geometry, representation theory and logic. His work on perverse sheaves, p-adic groups and automorphic forms helped establish major parts of the framework we now call geometric representation theory. 
Together, their ideas have created connections between fields that once seemed separate, and changed the way mathematicians understand symmetry, geometry and structure.
Congratulations to David Kazhdan and Joseph Bernstein, the 2026 Wolf Prize Laureates in Mathematics.

text:
每当读到哈萨比斯这一段论述的时候，我真的会心生感动。一个人是可以活到这样的程度的，他的财富已经足以让他享受世界，但他最大的追求仍然是理解世界。

钱是一种控制资源、时间和自由度的工具。
所以 beach house、yacht、豪车，在他的目标函数里几乎没有权重。第一版 Shannon 论文，能够继续研究以及那个听起来近乎疯狂的在太空建大型强子对撞机，反而更加的有权重。

成年以后，一个人仍然保存完好的宏大好奇心，不极端幼稚，不盲目空想，只是在已经证明自己能够把极其疯狂的想法工程化之后，仍然允许自己继续提出更疯狂的问题，这就是最好的状态。

如果哈萨比斯的目标是要做一家世界第一梯队的AI公司。那么2016年 AlphaGo 战胜世界冠军之后，其实已经足够了。
但诺贝尔奖官方对他这段历史用了一个非常重要的判断：Go was not the goal.
围棋是测试通用学习算法的手段。AlphaGo之后，他们开始把这些技术转向现实科学问题，最终进入蛋白质结构预测。2026年，哈萨比斯本人回顾 AlphaGo 十周年时说的也是同样的逻辑。AlphaGo，证明了这些方法有能力开始攻击现实世界的科学问题。

然后，就是AlphaFold2最终解决了持续约50年的蛋白质结构预测重大难题，Hassabis和John Jumper因此分享2024年诺贝尔化学奖的一半。

他创过公司、卖过公司、管理Google DeepMind，也在大规模融资。他显然理解资本、组织和产业的作用。但是，他似乎一直把财富、公司、算力、人才、AI乃至自己的职业生涯，当作扩大可解决问题集合的工具，而非目的本身。

所以从 Theme Park 到 DeepMind，从 AlphaGo 到 AlphaFold，再到 Isomorphic Labs，那个目标函数其实没有发生特别大的变化，变的只是他的资源约束而已。

现在，他拥有数千名研究者、Google的计算基础设施和世界上最先进的一批AI系统后，他的视野自然就可以变成蛋白质、药物、疾病、数学、物理学，乃至大型科学设施。这也是我觉得为什么 “I want to build a Large Hadron Collider in space” 从别人嘴里说出来可能像科幻想象，从哈萨比斯嘴里说出来却显得异常符合人物轨迹。

text:
I'm still seeing people complaining about Sol and Astra usage. The cause and solution to this is known.

Codex agents spin up subagents to complete tasks now unless you tell them not to. That isn’t the issue in and of itself though. The issue is that, by default, the orchestrator agent checks in on each subagent every 30 seconds. Every time, it has to re-read its whole context window and the subagent's status. That's potentially hundreds of thousands of tokens on the orchestrator every 30 seconds for every active subagent. The funny thing is this is totally unnecessary, because the subagent will return its result to the orchestrator when it's finished, so the only reason for the orchestrator to check in on the subagents periodically is to give you updates and make sure they didn't get hung up on something or expand scope.

The solution is to go to your config.toml and set:
- min_wait_timeout_ms = 300000
- default_wait_timeout_ms 900000

This makes the default for your orchestrator to check in on subagents every 15 minutes instead of every 30 seconds. This alone made a colossal reduction in my usage consumption rate.

If you want to take this even further, you can make a skill that has the orchestrator use Luna 6 subagents at xHigh effort with very tightly scoped and defined tasks for most actual implementation work, while the orchestrator is constrained to planning, delegation, and diff review. 

These two things together result in a consumption rate of about 2% usage/hour on my Pro x20 plan while running 3-4 Astra threads at High effort.

The White House Accord on Super Intelligence will have a positive impact on safety.

Committing to hire third party auditors who will report to an independent committee of board members has more practical near term significance than almost any conceivable regulatory action.

These board members will have a fiduciary duty. If they ignore a report from the third party auditors then a bad faith finding from a court is a real possibility. A D&O carrier could use this to deny coverage.

Really good outcome for ordinary Americans.

More effective and elegant than some ridiculous new regulatory body that would take months to do anything, then almost certainly done the wrong thing and along the way probably created a regulated oligopoly at the frontier which is the scariest potential outcome*

As I read the articles about the accord, it did occur to me that they were mostly written by political reporters who may have not understood the significance of the accord given their reporting beats are generally focused on public policy instead of corporate governance.

*Scariest because I do not trust any 5-20 individuals to make the best possible decisions about the direction of this technology. I want as many AIs as possible to maximize the odds that they encompass the diversity of human values across the world and richness of human variation. And I want an AI that shares my own personal values. Safety, freedom and the maximization of human agency through democratization, distribution and diffusion vs. centralization. text:
The MetaMask incident is worth understanding properly, because the headlines can make it sound worse or better than it is.
On 30 September, MetaMask disclosed a security incident affecting part of its infrastructure.
This was not a wallet hack. MetaMask says it has found no indication that wallets or customer funds were affected.
The impact was on its staking side. MetaMask Staking began exiting affected Ethereum validators as a precaution, including the ones it runs for Lido.
An onchain researcher estimates that block rewards from 18 validators were redirected to another address, around 0.36 ETH in total. MetaMask has not confirmed that figure or explained the root cause yet.

The bigger lesson is in the design.
On Ethereum, the keys that run a validator are separate from the withdrawal credentials that control where the staked ETH goes.
Because MetaMask's staking is non-custodial, it never held those withdrawal keys. A breach on the operator side can skim rewards and force exits, but it doesn't let an attacker withdraw the staked ETH to their own address.
Custody protects your stake. It doesn't fully protect your yield.

HUGE Breaking News: The IDF has now published a full dossier exposing a whopping 170 Gaza “journalists” who were actually military operatives in Hamas, Palestinian Islamic Jihad and other terrorist organizations.

The names cut across an astonishingly broad swath of the media ecosystem. The files include people reported to have worked for Al Jazeera, Reuters, AP, CNN, BBC, AFP, ABC, Le Monde, Radio France, Anadolu and dozens of Palestinian media organizations.

But the scandal here goes far beyond the 170 names.

A profession that asks the world to treat journalists as sacrosanct has an obligation to defend the meaning of the word journalist.

Journalism isn’t sacred because someone wears a PRESS vest. It’s sacred because truth is supposed to matter more than tribe, ideology, access or narrative.

Journalists are supposed to interrogate sources, not become stenographers for a cause.

The proper response to 170 detailed allegations is neither blind acceptance nor reflexive dismissal. It’s investigation.

Check the military IDs. Check the unit assignments. Check the employment histories. Ask the outlets what they knew.

Journalists should do journalism.

text:
Earlier today, NEAR Intents was exploited for $3.8m. SHIELD, the AI security layer on Intents, detected outlier behavior and Intents were temporarily paused. All of the affected users will be compensated in full.

The attacker exploited a bug in the Omni deposit/withdrawal interaction with the NEAR Intents smart contract isolated to USDT on BSC. The Intents team quickly identified the exact vulnerability and it was fixed within an hour of detection. NEAR Intents and https://t.co/uilYXjPFHF are already back online, except for a few affected chains on Intents. The core NEAR Protocol, NEAR token, and other applications on NEAR were not affected.

NEAR Intents now processes over $4B a month in trading and payments volume, serving as the industry’s connector across chains and ecosystems. At this scale, we have to hold ourselves to a higher security standard. This was the first major exploit on Intents and we will apply all learnings from this incident as part of a full retro and postmortem.

The crypto space is entering a new era of far more sophisticated cyber attacks. Recently, we have seen BitGet, Metamask, Lido all being targeted by criminals equipped with AI systems that are continuously trying to hack all infrastructure. As a space, we need to be far more vigilant and raise the bar on both onchain contract standards and offchain monitoring and proactive prevention. 

This includes incorporating formal verification, a key tool for preventing a large class of vulnerabilities. The NEAR ecosystem is already working on a formal verification system for NEAR contracts and will shortly implement it as part of the release process, alongside other security measures that will come out of the postmortem.

Being more proactive against criminal activity is a critical step to ensure the growth and legitimacy of crypto. It’s time to join forces and work together to use all tools at our disposal to detect and prevent malicious activity. SHIELD is our approach to monitoring and AI-based outlier detection. We welcome new SHIELD partners to work with us to share information faster and get better at detecting and containing criminals and exploits across web3.

Earlier today NEAR Intents services were stopped after a security incident was detected. The incident was caused by a bug in the Omni deposit and withdrawal infrastructure interaction with NEAR Intents smart contract.

The preliminary report indicates the total loss of approximately $3.8M. These funds will be compensated in full.

The contract-side vulnerability has been patched. The operations of the NEAR Intents and near(.)com are expected to resume within 1h.

Deposits and withdrawals on the following networks will remain unavailable for an additional ~12 hours while fixes to the Omni infrastructure are completed: BSC, Polygon, TON, Optimism, Avalanche, Stellar, Monad, LayerX, Adi, Scroll and Plasma.

In case users hold any assets from these chains inside NEAR Intents (for example, in HOT wallet or on near(.)com), they will be able to swap them into other assets once NEAR Intents is back up (in ~1h).

The incident has been reported to law enforcement, and we are working with security and blockchain analytics partners to trace the funds and pursue recovery. A detailed report will be shared publicly in the following days.

text: We are now one step closer to a Faster Ethereum L1.
author: binji_x
quoted_text:
Update: One step closer to a faster Ethereum L1.

Quick slots just moved to Considered for Inclusion (CFI) in today's All Core Devs call! This is a new milestone for our proposal to make Ethereum blocks faster 🎉 

Btw.. Faster blocks =>
- Better UX
- Better markets
- Faster finality and fast confirmation rule
- And improved censorship-resistance too!
TLDR: More value for the network, its users, and ETH, without compromising on the core values and properties of Ethereum.
Hear this from 20 top Ethereum teams in our ecosystem survey: https://t.co/QRG4lOGc6m

---

Ok, what does CFI mean? This does not mean that the EIP is for sure included in Hegotá. This means that now it will be considered more seriously, including testing, towards inclusion in future devnets once headliners (FOCIL and frame transactions) are stable.

In particular, the call today revealed the appetite for a phased approach, installing the plumbing which allows us to reduce the slot time in Ethereum clients, and deciding to pull the trigger based on further testing.

Ultimately, this is how EIP-8198 is designed, so CFI'ing today allows us to move forward with more of the plumbing work, and start looking into testing towards an actual slot reduction from 12 to 10 seconds. This is a first reduction, as EIP-8198 opens the door for progressively lower slot times, as they get sufficiently safe to ship.

In parallel, as discussed on the call too, we are continuing our ecosystem survey and outreach of deployed smart contracts with a slot time dependency. We have reached out to more teams on this.

---

Faster slots are one important dimension of our Faster Ethereum body of work. A more responsive network helps cement its role as a liquidity hub and as the heartbeat of the network as a whole.

Along with our work on fast finality, fast confirmation rule and fast interop, it all combines for a seamless and secure flow of assets everywhere on the network.

Thank you to the many builders who are taking us there!

author: centrifuge
quoted_text:
Centrifuge V3.3: The Onchain Execution Policy

Onchain lending vaults have converged on a workable answer to manager risk: caps the curator cannot exceed, roles split between parties, and a timelock with a guardian over the parameters that matter.

That answer works when the strategy is a fixed set of actions, agreed in advance. Many strategies are not, and what bounds the manager there is a mandate: the objectives and constraints they operate within, historically set out in a document.

V3.3 makes it a contract. The Onchain Execution Policy holds the actions permitted for a pool, publishes them before the first deposit, and enforces them on every action the manager takes.

Projects that are doing buybacks isn't necessarily good for a project, it's more like a narrative after $HYPE has had massive success with it. Buybacks is in a way a signal that the token isn't worthless. But eg. on Wall Street, buybacks or dividends are more for established projects that earns a lot of money, while growth stocks is instead reinvesting into their business.

The key question is whether the project can generate a higher return by reinvesting capital than by buying back tokens.

Buybacks only become truly meaningful when they are funded by sustainable protocol revenue, not token emissions or treasury spending.

If a project still has a long growth runway, capital spent on product, distribution and ecosystem growth could create more value long term, and I guess this is the question for most protocols, because many of them seems to have finished the job once the token has launched...

ANNOUNCING THE 2026 WOLF PRIZE LAUREATES IN PHYSICS
The 2026 Wolf Prize in Physics is awarded to Immanuel F. Bloch and Jun Ye “for transformative, widely applicable advances in the control of ultracold atomic systems.” 
Their work has pushed experimental physics into realms that were once almost impossible to control.
Bloch established ultracold atoms trapped in optical lattices as a powerful platform for studying complex quantum systems. His work helped define the modern field of quantum simulation, revealing new insights into many-body quantum states and laying foundations for emerging quantum technologies. 
Ye, meanwhile, led the development of the world’s most accurate and stable optical atomic clocks, achieving levels of precision that have reshaped how time and frequency can be measured. His work has also opened new ways to test fundamental physics, from relativity to searches for variations in nature’s fundamental constants. 
From controlling quantum matter to measuring time with unprecedented precision, their discoveries have expanded what physicists can observe, test, and engineer.
Congratulations to Immanuel F. Bloch and Jun Ye, the 2026 Wolf Prize Laureates in Physics.

quoted_text:
24 小时不到，我刚充的 100 美金 Token 烧完了。

AI 到底是在帮我提效，还是换了个方式让我烧钱？

最近用 agent 做研究和策划，我想要的工作方式是：只对接一个 agent，它负责推进，卡住了来找我，需要我决策时再叫我。

但钱花得太快，也让我开始想：我付的钱，有多少是在买产出，有多少是在买 AI 反复协调、查进度、读旧资料？

查了一轮英文资料和重度用户的复盘，梅西找到两个值得检查的地方👇

① 你的 AI 在干活，还是在不停开会？

Reddit 上一位叫 Dayowe 的用户分析了自己 Codex 的运行日志。改造工作流后，每小时原始 token 消耗从约 4,040 万降到了 2,230 万，下降约 45%。

最有意思的是：平均每次请求的 token 没变少，反而略多了

主要减少的是总请求次数。

他原来的方式，是一个长期运行的统筹 agent 管到底：分派任务、调查问题、检查进度、审查结果，上一阶段的历史也一路带到下一阶段。

后来改成：

轻量协调者只管任务依赖、授权和下一步；每个阶段交给单独的执行统筹，完成后保存交接信息，下个阶段只带必要上下文。

同时减少无变化的进度查询，不再提前审查还没完成的工作；长日志留在文件里，需要时再读。必要测试和独立验收仍然保留。

它提醒了我一件事：

我只想对接一个入口，不代表这个入口需要参与每项工作的每一步。

要检查的，不只是“每次用了多少 token”，还有“为什么需要调用这么多次模型”。

② 同样让 agent 操作电脑，用什么方式，成本可能差很多

一种是像人一样看屏幕：识别截图、找到按钮、点击，再看截图确认。多轮下来，图片输入和反复判断都会产生 token 消耗

另一种，是通过命令行或脚本直接处理任务。命令行是用文字给电脑下指令，脚本则是把一组操作步骤写好，让电脑照着执行

比如从表格里筛选订单，AI 可以直接写一段命令，让电脑读取文件、批量筛选、保存结果，不用打开软件，一页页看、一格格点

区别在于：前者需要 AI 反复看、反复判断；后者由电脑执行指令，AI 再检查结果。AI 写脚本、检查结果会消耗 token，但电脑按规则处理每一行，不需要逐行再调用模型。

当然，不是所有任务都适合脚本：读取外部数据要有可用接口和权限；检查排版、确认页面效果，仍然需要看界面。如果脚本内部还是反复截图，或者每处理一条内容就调用一次 AI，也不一定省。

所以思考“这一步到底需不需要模型参与”也是优化 token 消耗的一个必要步骤

能按规则完成的，交给程序；需要理解和判断的，交给 AI；重要决策和授权，留给人。

工具要会用，新东西也要继续学习！顺便插播一条预告😂

text: We are now one step closer to a Faster Ethereum L1.
author: FigoETH
quoted_text:
Update: One step closer to a faster Ethereum L1.

Quick slots just moved to Considered for Inclusion (CFI) in today's All Core Devs call! This is a new milestone for our proposal to make Ethereum blocks faster 🎉 

Btw.. Faster blocks =>
- Better UX
- Better markets
- Faster finality and fast confirmation rule
- And improved censorship-resistance too!
TLDR: More value for the network, its users, and ETH, without compromising on the core values and properties of Ethereum.
Hear this from 20 top Ethereum teams in our ecosystem survey: https://t.co/QRG4lOGc6m

---

Ok, what does CFI mean? This does not mean that the EIP is for sure included in Hegotá. This means that now it will be considered more seriously, including testing, towards inclusion in future devnets once headliners (FOCIL and frame transactions) are stable.

In particular, the call today revealed the appetite for a phased approach, installing the plumbing which allows us to reduce the slot time in Ethereum clients, and deciding to pull the trigger based on further testing.

Ultimately, this is how EIP-8198 is designed, so CFI'ing today allows us to move forward with more of the plumbing work, and start looking into testing towards an actual slot reduction from 12 to 10 seconds. This is a first reduction, as EIP-8198 opens the door for progressively lower slot times, as they get sufficiently safe to ship.

In parallel, as discussed on the call too, we are continuing our ecosystem survey and outreach of deployed smart contracts with a slot time dependency. We have reached out to more teams on this.

---

Faster slots are one important dimension of our Faster Ethereum body of work. A more responsive network helps cement its role as a liquidity hub and as the heartbeat of the network as a whole.

Along with our work on fast finality, fast confirmation rule and fast interop, it all combines for a seamless and secure flow of assets everywhere on the network.

Thank you to the many builders who are taking us there!

author: inversebrah
quoted_text:
🚨 Hayden Davis, Ben Chow, Kelsier, and Meteora just beat the $LIBRA / $M3M3 class action.

Not after a trial. After an 81-page opinion.

Judge Rochon dismissed the ENTIRE case with prejudice. You cannot RICO a six-month memecoin launch. You cannot sue a Solana DEX as if it were a partnership. And “Milei posted it” is not a fraud claim against the guy who built the liquidity pool.

This was the SDNY class action over the December 2024 $M3M3 launch and the February 2025 $LIBRA token - the one tied to Javier Milei’s “Viva La Libertad” post. Plaintiffs also tried to pull in $MELANIA and other launches in a proposed second amended complaint.

The story in the complaint if you can recall, is cinematic. Insiders allegedly freeze the pool, fill wallets before the public can buy, inflate the cap, dump, and leave retail with a 90% crash. One named plaintiff lost about $19,000 on $M3M3. The other bought $LIBRA on launch day.

The court never decided whether that happened.

It decided plaintiffs sued the wrong thing, under the wrong statute, with the wrong facts.

Meteora is not a defendant. 

Dynamic Labs intervened and said Meteora is software. The court agreed plaintiffs never pleaded a real unincorporated association - no identified members, no president or treasurer, no mutual consent to a common objective. Calling a protocol a “team” does not make it suable. 

All claims against Meteora are gone.

RICO is gone. 

Closed-ended continuity needs a substantial period. Six months of token launches is not enough. Adding $MELANIA / $ENRON / $TRUST in the proposed amendment stretched it to about seven. Still not enough. Open-ended continuity also fails: Meteora and Kelsier are alleged as primarily legitimate businesses, and wire fraud is not inherently a criminal way of life. No pattern, no RICO, no RICO conspiracy.

Fraud against Chow is gone. Rule 9(b) scienter. Profit is not motive. A post-crash “I f*cked up because I enabled the guy” is not a strong inference he intended to defraud buyers on day one. 

Conspiracy dies with the underlying tort.

Kelsier is gone on jurisdiction. Once RICO drops, there is no nationwide service hook, and New York long-arm does not reach the Davis family on these facts.

Leave to amend: denied as futile. Case closed.

The takeaway is not “memecoins are legal.” The takeaway is that a viral launch plus a famous tweet is still not a RICO enterprise, and you cannot name the smart contracts as Defendant No. 5.

text:
Galaxy: 69.2% of Polymarket Retail Accounts Lose Money, With $338.9M in Aggregate Losses

Galaxy Research found that 69.2% of roughly 2.9 million human-paced “retail” accounts on Polymarket’s international platform finished below break-even, with aggregate losses of $338.9 million. The analysis, based on onchain settlement data curated by Stork, showed that 15.2% of accounts did not trade again within 30 days after a loss, versus 6.1% after a win. About 44.1% of traders concentrated more than 60% of their activity in a single topic. Sports specialists made up 47% of specialists but had the lowest profitability rate at 25.1%, while tech and science specialists had the highest at 41.2%, though the sample was smaller. Profitable traders had a median position size of $13.96, versus $10 for unprofitable traders, while holding time showed no clear relationship with profitability.

If you use a hardware wallet, pay attention to every transaction before signing and you're safe.

It’s still unclear whether the attacker is also stealing seeds from software wallets directly at this stage.

Earlier today NEAR Intents services were stopped after a security incident was detected. The incident was caused by a bug in the Omni deposit and withdrawal infrastructure interaction with NEAR Intents smart contract.

The preliminary report indicates the total loss of approximately $3.8M. These funds will be compensated in full.

The contract-side vulnerability has been patched. The operations of the NEAR Intents and near(.)com are expected to resume within 1h.

Deposits and withdrawals on the following networks will remain unavailable for an additional ~12 hours while fixes to the Omni infrastructure are completed: BSC, Polygon, TON, Optimism, Avalanche, Stellar, Monad, LayerX, Adi, Scroll and Plasma.

In case users hold any assets from these chains inside NEAR Intents (for example, in HOT wallet or on near(.)com), they will be able to swap them into other assets once NEAR Intents is back up (in ~1h).

The incident has been reported to law enforcement, and we are working with security and blockchain analytics partners to trace the funds and pursue recovery. A detailed report will be shared publicly in the following days.

text:
如何从零想出一个估值百亿的创业点子？
 Scale AI 创始人，现在是Meta首席AI官，muse负责人 的 Alexandr Wang 给出了一条极简铁律：活在未来，倒推今天还不存在的那行 API。

 从深夜抢注域名，到肉身坐在客服气泡后死磕每一个访客，这段 4 分钟的复盘，讲透了科技商业里最硬核的起步真相。

很多人可能不知道，现在估值接近 140 亿美元的 AI 数据霸主 Scale AI，在刚起步的前半年，创始人每天也在经历极度严重的精神内耗。

这是 Scale AI 创始人， Alexandr Wang 在 SPC 闭门访谈里，第一次毫无保留地复盘自己在 YC 期间最痛苦的负一阶段。

一句话概括这段分享最值钱的本质： 所有伟大企业的起点，并不是算无遗策的天才顿悟，而是在漫长的游荡期里，靠着第一性原理把脏活做透，硬生生把一个看似不起眼的点子熬成了超级基础设施。

现在几乎所有想做点事、想做个人项目或创业的人，都在经历同一种心理折磨： 打开文档写满了各种点子，却总觉得每一个都不够好； 看着身边的人都在飞速推进，总觉得自己从第一天起就落后了别人半年； 每天在强烈的存在焦虑里打转，不知道自己到底在折腾什么。

Alexandr Wang 当年也是一模一样的处境。 我把他在视频里拆解出的三个底层认知，整理成最干货的复盘讲透👇

① 选方向的第一性原则：活在未来，倒推缺失的那行 API

当年他在 YC 每天写点子文档，直到读了 Paul Graham 的那篇经典文章：Live in the future, and build what's missing.

他当时看到了一个未来的必然趋势： 未来的人类算力（Human Compute）一定会像计算机算力一样，被极度动态地编排和调用。 但当时整个互联网上，根本没有一个能够像调用服务器一样直接调用人工标注与处理的 API。 于是他花了一整晚买下 ScaleAPI 这个域名，这就是百亿帝国的最初原点。

② 拆穿创业最大的心理陷阱：起步即落后的虚妄焦虑

在负一阶段，最致命的不是没点子，而是同行压力带来的动作变形。 Alexandr 提到：当你刚萌生一个新点子时，环顾四周，总觉得别人已经跑了很久，自己一开局就落后了。 但事实是，绝大多数人都在各自的迷雾里摸索。 真正的差距从来不是谁先动手两星期，而是谁能在漫长的游荡期里顶住内耗，把方向压力测试到底。

③ 穿越死亡谷的唯一解法：做无法规模化的笨活与脏活

在 Product Hunt 上线拿到第一波热度后，Scale 经历了整整 4 到 6 个月的空白游荡期。 当时没有爆发式增长，能不能成完全是未知数。 Alexandr 采取的最硬核策略只有一个：当客服。 他在官网挂了 Intercom 聊天气泡，每一个点进网页、发消息咨询的真实访客，背后亲自敲键盘回复的人就是他自己。 正是靠着跟每一个早期客户在泥潭里死磕，直到半年后才终于等来了第一个真正想做大的核心客户。

历史与商业演进的硬核印证：

→ 硅谷最经典的创业定律： 保罗·格雷厄姆提倡的 Do things that don't scale（做无法规模化的事），在 Scale AI 身上得到了最彻底的验证。世界上最顶级的自动化数据管道，最开始也是创始人靠肉身当客服一点点抠出来的。

→ 游荡期是所有顶级公司的必修课： 从 Airbnb 早期靠卖麦片还信用卡债，到 Stripe 创始人亲自跑去客户电脑上敲命令行装插件，没有一家基础设施级巨头能跳过这至少半年的迷茫摸索。

站在另一个更理性的视角来看，这件事给普通人的启发极其锋利：

→ 不要把摸索期的焦虑误判为失败： 从负一阶段到零的这段时间，内心动荡和怀疑是系统的标配属性，而不是你能力不足的证明。

→ 别在战术的勤奋里逃避真正的思考： 想点子不是在文档里盲目堆数量，而是敢于逼问自己：未来五年哪件事一定会发生，而今天还缺了关键工具？

→ 离真实用户再近一点： 当你不知道下一步该做什么时，去跟每一个点了聊天气泡的真实访客聊半个小时，远比关在屋子里改一百遍商业计划书管用得多。

最后收个尾：

世上从来没有一开局就清晰无比的百亿蓝图。 伟大往往就藏在那份写满废案的文档里，藏在深夜无人问津的客服窗口背后。

熬过负一阶段的迷茫，把未来的缺失变成今天的行动，你才算真正站在了起跑线上。
author: AYi_AInotes
quoted_text:
整个科技圈风向都在卷大企业 AI， 结果 @Meta 的 @AIatMeta AI 掌门人 @alexandr_wang 刚刚发推说他们后台发现，把 Muse 用得最猛的， 竟然是修水管的、开农场的、开杂货店和开小餐馆的老板……
上线两周，早期用户里竟然有 1/3 直接把它绑定了商业账号。
今天 Meta 顺水推舟，直接上线了 Muse for Small Business， 一口气甩出 22 个官方连接器： Shopify、Stripe、QuickBooks、Canva、Zoom、Slack…… 把小商家的全套数字牛马直接做实了。

我把背后的逻辑和搞钱启示用大白话给大家拆一下👇
━━
1｜最反直觉的现象：用 AI 最狠的不是大厂，是个体户
大厂做 AI 喜欢去找世界 500 强做大单子， 但真实世界里，最缺时间的是那些“一人身兼八职”的小老板。
官方案例里有个爱荷华州开杂货店的大叔： 每周工作 65 个小时，店里进货是他、管账是他、做促销是他、处理退款还是他。 他缺的根本不是点子，是时间。
以前大家以为 Muse 只是个帮宅男比价订外卖的玩具， 结果这些小老板早就拿它去回客户邮件、查库存、算账了。

2｜这 22 个连接器，到底解决了啥？
做过独立电商、自媒体或者小生意的朋友都懂这个痛点： 每天要在 8 个后台之间来回切—— 看销量去 Shopify，查退款去 Stripe，做海报去 Canva，记账去 QuickBooks，开会去 Zoom，内部沟通去 Slack。
现在 Muse 把它全收拢到一个对话框里： ▫️查账退款：不用登录 Stripe 后台，直接对它说“把昨天争议的那笔单子退了”，它核对完调接口执行 ▫️内容与营销：识别你的产品库存和品牌调性，直接调用 Canva 生成下周促销海报，一键推到 Instagram 商业主页 ▫️客户与日程：给它配个专属邮箱，客户发来的询价、改期邮件，它在后台看懂日历直接起草回复
一句话：它不是让你去学一个新软件，而是把你手上所有的 SaaS 变成听话的后台。

3｜Meta 这步棋最狠的地方在哪？
Facebook 和 Instagram 上有整整 2 亿小微商家。 这是全球最大的个体老板聚集地。
Meta 根本不需要跟微软、谷歌去抢那些复杂的企业级大单， 它只要让这 2 亿小老板在手机上： “少雇一个客服、少花 2 小时对账、少切 5 个软件”。
而且最聪明的是它的安全机制： 所有涉及扣费、退款、对外公开发布的操作，AI 负责跑腿起草，最后一步依然要人点确认。 这就是我们常说的“人管方向和钱包，AI 管繁琐和流程”。

4｜对我们普通人和超级个体意味着什么？
一人公司（One-Person Company）过去最大的瓶颈，不是你不会做核心业务，而是被杂事活活拖死。 你懂做视频，但你不想花时间回商务邮件； 你懂写代码，但你讨厌天天去处理发票和对账。
当 AI Agent 开始长出连接现实商业系统的手（Connectors）： 以前需要 3 个人支撑的微型工作室， 以后可能真的 1 个人加一个配置好的 Personal AI 就能跑起来。

5｜照例泼盆冷水
▫️这套连接器目前深度绑定的是海外生态（Shopify、Stripe、QuickBooks 等），国内主流的微店、淘宝、微信支付等生态目前还没打通； ▫️多平台授权意味着你的商业数据、客户往来都在被 AI 扫描，哪些权限给、哪些不给，依然得有边界； ▫️复杂业务逻辑的容错率低，账目核算依然需要人工定期复核，别做甩手掌柜。
━━
过去我们讨论 AI，总觉得它是高高在上的算力和算法。
 但今天 Alexandr Wang 这条推说明了一件事： AI 落地最快、最扎实的地方， 永远是帮街角那家店的老板，把今晚下班的时间提前两个小时。
开源了自定义接入平台（https://t.co/GGtFihiFNC）。 如果国内也有一个 AI 能接通你所有的工作软件，你最想让它替你干掉哪个日常琐事？ https://t.co/zrRk2zy06N

text:
Update: One step closer to a faster Ethereum L1.

Quick slots just moved to Considered for Inclusion (CFI) in today's All Core Devs call! This is a new milestone for our proposal to make Ethereum blocks faster 🎉 

Btw.. Faster blocks =>
- Better UX
- Better markets
- Faster finality and fast confirmation rule
- And improved censorship-resistance too!
TLDR: More value for the network, its users, and ETH, without compromising on the core values and properties of Ethereum.
Hear this from 20 top Ethereum teams in our ecosystem survey: https://t.co/QRG4lOGc6m

---

Ok, what does CFI mean? This does not mean that the EIP is for sure included in Hegotá. This means that now it will be considered more seriously, including testing, towards inclusion in future devnets once headliners (FOCIL and frame transactions) are stable.

In particular, the call today revealed the appetite for a phased approach, installing the plumbing which allows us to reduce the slot time in Ethereum clients, and deciding to pull the trigger based on further testing.

Ultimately, this is how EIP-8198 is designed, so CFI'ing today allows us to move forward with more of the plumbing work, and start looking into testing towards an actual slot reduction from 12 to 10 seconds. This is a first reduction, as EIP-8198 opens the door for progressively lower slot times, as they get sufficiently safe to ship.

In parallel, as discussed on the call too, we are continuing our ecosystem survey and outreach of deployed smart contracts with a slot time dependency. We have reached out to more teams on this.

---

Faster slots are one important dimension of our Faster Ethereum body of work. A more responsive network helps cement its role as a liquidity hub and as the heartbeat of the network as a whole.

Along with our work on fast finality, fast confirmation rule and fast interop, it all combines for a seamless and secure flow of assets everywhere on the network.

Thank you to the many builders who are taking us there!
