text:
Ethereum has had 100% uptime since its inception, so it’s worth asking why @ethlabs_org and EF are redesigning its consensus protocol.  I want to provide some context.

Ethereum today runs what researchers call an "ebb-and-flow" consensus protocol.  "Ebb-and-flow" refers to the fact that the protocol is actually two protocols in one:

- There's an "availability protocol," also called a "fork-choice rule," which can produce blocks even when a majority of Ethereum's stake are offline.  This is what would keep Ethereum producing blocks even if a nuclear war took out most of the internet.

- There's a "finality gadget," which makes a block irreversible after some time.  This is why we can all go to sleep at night knowing that our transactions won't be reverted when we wake up.

However, for historical reasons, these two protocols are tightly coupled on Ethereum.  Every block, a subset ("committee") of Ethereum validators send votes ("attestations") to produce blocks, and the very same votes are used to finalize blocks over a long range ("epochs").  The fact that the same votes are used for both protocols means that, if you were to reduce the votes used for the availability protocol, which would speed up block production, you would need more blocks to achieve finality, which would delay finalization.  On the other hand, if you were to use more votes for the availability protocol, it would speed up finalization but slow down block production.  You cannot speed up both at the same time.

On the other hand, Ethereum's fork-choice rule (formally named "LMD-GHOST") has been discovered to have multiple vulnerabilities over the years.  For example, it was discovered (by researchers including @casparschwa and @barnabemonnot) that you could secretly accumulate votes for a fork, then reveal it later to reorg out a new block.  There have been consistent efforts to patch these vulnerabilities, but they are generally seen as bandaid fixes that introduce further complexity and bug surface into the protocol.

So Ethereum's new consensus design, called "decoupled consensus", is an ambitious attempt at tackling both problems at once:

- Decouple the availability protocol from the finality protocol, so both can be optimized independently.

- Fix vulnerabilities with the availability protocol.

The way this is done, in broad strokes, is this:

- We replace LMD-GHOST with a new algorithm called Goldfish, alongside a "stabilization gadget" which is another sub-protocol that prevents Goldfish from re-orging over an arbitrarily long range.

- We run the availability protocol (Goldfish+stabilization gadget) and the finality protocol in parallel, with separate votes.

The result?  Ethereum will provide both fast finality and fast block times, AND it will keep producing blocks during World War III.  Of all blockchains, Ethereum will be the only blockchain with these properties, and that's why it will be the settlement layer of the global economy.
author: decentrek
quoted_text:
One step closer to 4-8x faster Ethereum finality!

It took some time and lots of tokens, but we now have a formally verified proposal for a decoupled consensus protocol in I* (a future Ethereum upgrade)! Not yet a full spec (up next), but it includes all the key consensus-relevant details to become one.

Since Ethereum aspires to be live without most of the stake online, the protocol involves many more components than a normal BFT protocol, and its correctness involves much more than standard safety and liveness. Those nuanced properties are now verified!

What's more, I came away convinced that all protocol design will involve AI-assisted Formal Verification in the future, both for correctness and iteration speed.

The work wasn't limited to just:

Design the protocol -> Formally verify it

Instead, the loop became more like:

Design -> Formal Model -> Find exactly what breaks and why -> Redesign it.

For a fairly complicated protocol like this one, I think having the Lean model be part of the design loop played a big role in accelerating the process.

A future with agents paired with formal models is a superpower for Ethereum development, because they can then use those models to find exactly where an argument breaks down, formalize counterexamples, test proposed fixes, iterate on the protocol.

Many details that would slip under the radar when asking agents (and indeed, humans) can now be specified exactly and checked by the Lean kernel. This then forces agents to be more precise and lets them make verifiable progress on their own. It's been incredible to see this play out, seeing agents find gaps and propose protocol changes to fix them.

In other words, autoresearch can speed up protocol design, formal verification is here to stay, and Ethereum Finality will get faster.

text:
关于CZ赵长鹏这次说的“主动性”，是他在香港这场书友会上面对一群大学生时，给出的唯一招人标准。

原话是这样的：
“现场很多学生想进币安，他的答案只有三个字：要主动。币安是远程工作，你可以偷懒，一天偷懒几个小时很容易。但如果你不够主动，两个月下来，你可能就没有结果。 ”

他自己的管理方式更直接：
“我接触的东西很多，一会这个一会那个，有些事情我说过之后就忘了。我一般不会去跟踪他。如果这个人不主动来告诉我更新，我就会忘记。但我可能两个月之后想起来，再去问他，他说‘我们做了一个礼拜之后就没有进展了’——那我会把这人开掉。” 
“我从来不去follow up，我是需要他们push给我。” 
他最后总结成一句判断：“你只要主动积极去做一件事情，你就会成功。你若等着老板过来查业绩时才做，你是不会成功的。” 

有趣的是，主持人当场补了一刀：
今天能坐在这里的人，全是自己写email不断push主办方、还提交了问题才被选进来的。主动性本身就是门票。

CZ把主动性还拆成了两个更大的底层逻辑：
1.  80%在于到场
人生的成功，80%在于到场。你一定要参与，不参与的话就没有机会。
2.  什么不做，比做什么重要 
现在多数人不考虑什么不做。别人发个消息，一定要回一下...这些事情很多人完全可以砍掉，但是没有砍。

我认为主动性是三种能力的组合，主动到场、主动push、主动为结果负责。

1. 做科研：别等课题，要自己去要反馈
据我观察，现在的学生做科研最常见的死法，就是等导师布置，等灵感，等设备。

科研主动性是反过来的：
主动定义问题，即使可能错误。
不要等导师给你题目。把你领域最近3年的top paper的limitation list整理出来，主动去敲导师的门说，我想试试。
主动要反馈，但要对人。
CZ说保持深度联系的高质量反馈用户，3到5个就够了。“不用每个月聊几百个用户，每个月聊5个就可以了。”其实我觉得科研同理，与其群发问卷，不如主动锁定3-5个真正懂你方向的教授、博士、或业界的人，每两周push一次进展，哪怕是失败的进展。 
主动写。
他写《币安人生》就是找点事做每天写15分钟攒出来的。论文也是，先写烂初稿，再迭代，完美了再动笔，黄花菜凉了。

2. 创业：产品和用户之前，没有其他事
CZ给大学生的创业清单，第一句就是：“最开始，只有两件事：产品和用户。你要能拉来用户，你要能给用户提供价值。这两个没有的话，你就不会有公司。” 
很多创业的主动性误区是先做BP、先找投资、先做Logo。
你要主动去丢脸，像他说的到场逻辑，先做一个能用的demo，主动去加20个潜在用户的微信，听听反馈。
他听说CX卖房买BTC前计算了如果归零了，他能不能再去华尔街拿一份六位数工作的情况。那是他的底气。
学生创业前其实也要算算这个项目黄了，时间、学分、生活费能不能继续、能接受到什么程度，
这是主动性的另一面，主动管理风险。

创业不要着急，建议年轻人先在好的大公司工作几年，两年应该是最低的，以2年到5年为宜。有时候在大厂里主动去学一套完整的管理体系，比你一毕业就在泥里打滚学得更快。 

3. 学业：一技之长要卷到全球前1%

我认为，学业上的主动性就是占领一个山头，不要过于平均用力。理工科一定要有一门课做到系里名列前茅的状态，比如把机器学习、密码学主动做到能教别人的程度。

在大课人人都是螺丝钉，只有主动去office hour，主动去要RA，主动去旁听研究生组会。你不去push教授，教授两个月后也会忘了你是谁，这和CZ忘了员工是一样的。
而且，什么不做比做什么重要。
我觉得别人都报的热门水课、无效社交、每条消息秒回，都可以砍。

总之，主动选择看似麻烦的事，韧性是主动性的后半段。
到场 > 完美，push > 等待，结果 > 过程。

quoted_text:
Lads, the hockey stick is starting to form :) 

Notional volume in September more than DOUBLED compared to August, so here’s a quick onchain options recap (Sep vs Aug ’26):

1) Notional more than doubled. September notional reached $4.829B, up 121.7% month over month. 

2) @paradex nearly quadrupled. Paradex's public RFQ rollout was a huge success. Notional rose 285% to $259.9M, lifting its market share from 3.1% to 5.4%. ethereum:0xb32e10022ffbedfe10bc818a1c7e67d9d87e0fa7 

3) @SynapseProtocol is on the board. Notional went from $9.4M to $538.8M, a 57x jump. Hypercall now holds 11.2% of notional share, up from 0.4%, and ranks #2 behind Derive for September. Some of this volume was driven by a short-dated bear put spread. The MM that wrote this option hedged on Hyperliquid and accounted for 15% of all S&P perp volume on HL that day. ethereum:0x0f2d719407fdbeff09d87557abb7232601fd9f29

4) @DeriveXYZ doubled as well but ceded notional share. Derive grew notional by 99.3% to $3.827B, but its share fell from 88.1% to 79.3% as Hypercall and Paradex took volume. On premium, it still holds 91.6% of market share. ethereum:0xb1d1eae60eea9525032a6dcb4c1ce336a1de71be 

5) Notional outran premium. Notional grew 2.2x while 30d premium grew 1.3x to $83.78M. 

Lower premium per dollar of notional points to more short-dated or out-of-the-money flow, a shift worth watching as it points to more retail activity (exactly what we want).

What to watch in October
If you’re not already paying attention to onchain options, then this is your wake-up call. The sector is still nascent but doubling volumes MoM is THE growth indicator. YTD volumes are clearly up and to the right. 

My open question now is whether Hypercall’s notional volume is sticky or a one-month burst. A second month above $500M would make me more confident in the venue’s growth and move me to reallocate my portfolio 

PAY ATTENTION TO ONCHAIN OPTIONS

text: Democrats are trying to dismiss the White House Accord on Super Intelligence as optional self-policing. But although the agreement was entered into voluntarily, the governance that follows from it is not. As Gavin Baker points out, once an independent auditor reports a safety issue to an independent board committee, directors have a fiduciary duty not to disregard it, and a D&O carrier can use a bad-faith finding to deny coverage. So although the agreement starts with internal controls, these are verified by external audit and board oversight — and then existing FTC and securities law still apply to any public claim the company does not keep. This is far more practical than what Democrats want — a freeze on frontier development while China races ahead. Democrats should applaud what President Trump has accomplished. But they would rather use SI safety as a campaign issue than admit the Accord represents major progress.
author: DavidSacks
quoted_text:
The White House Accord on Super Intelligence will have a positive impact on safety.

Committing to hire third party auditors who will report to an independent committee of board members has more practical near term significance than almost any conceivable regulatory action.

These board members will have a fiduciary duty. If they ignore a report from the third party auditors then a bad faith finding from a court is a real possibility. A D&O carrier could use this to deny coverage.

Really good outcome for ordinary Americans.

More effective and elegant than some ridiculous new regulatory body that would take months to do anything, then almost certainly done the wrong thing and along the way probably created a regulated oligopoly at the frontier which is the scariest potential outcome*

As I read the articles about the accord, it did occur to me that they were mostly written by political reporters who may have not understood the significance of the accord given their reporting beats are generally focused on public policy instead of corporate governance.

*Scariest because I do not trust any 5-20 individuals to make the best possible decisions about the direction of this technology. I want as many AIs as possible to maximize the odds that they encompass the diversity of human values across the world and richness of human variation. And I want an AI that shares my own personal values. Safety, freedom and the maximization of human agency through democratization, distribution and diffusion vs. centralization. History has spoken on the dangers of the latter path.

**Also SI not AI still adapting to the change but I do think better branding. Who wants artificial ingredients in their food?

The 2026 Wolf Prize in Chemistry is awarded to Pascal Mayer, Shankar Balasubramanian and David Klenerman for developing impactful, low-cost, next generation DNA sequencing methods for genomic medicine. 
Their work helped transform DNA sequencing into a technology capable of operating at extraordinary speed and scale.
Balasubramanian and Klenerman pioneered a massively parallel sequencing approach that contributed to a million-fold improvement in sequencing speed and cost, helping make it possible to sequence a human genome for under $200. 
Mayer played a pivotal role in turning those breakthroughs into a practical high-throughput sequencing system, integrating the chemistry, microfluidics, optics and computational components needed to make the technology work at scale. 
Today, the sequencing platform that grew from this work forms the technological foundation for more than 90% of global sequencing data, powering major advances in genomics and precision medicine. 
Congratulations to the 2026 Wolf Prize Laureates in Chemistry!

text: best AI agent case study for healthcare I've seen on this app:
author: karlarboledas
quoted_text:
A healthcare company asked us to build AI agents that could explain bills to patients, arrange payment plans and reconcile payments back into providers’ billing systems.

The system has since handled 61,246 AI voice calls. 

AI-assisted development helped us implement changes faster, and our QA capacity had to grow alongside development.

That mattered because the software was going to speak to real patients and handle real payments. A mistake could mean charging someone twice, updating the wrong record or leaving the provider’s books out of balance.

Today, the system has 349,000 lines of application code and 343,000 lines of test code. The test suite contains 13,650 automated tests, running on every pull request in 9.7 minutes.

Keeping feedback under ten minutes was part of the engineering work. We split the suite across parallel workers so the team could keep checking its changes while shipping daily.

Alongside the tests, automated checks cover types, code quality, imports and database migrations. All 216 migrations are checked to make sure they can safely run again if a deployment retries them.

The system also enforces boundaries around what agents can do. Retried actions have protection against duplicate execution, and test environments are prevented from writing into real patient records.

Those requirements have to survive every change, whether a person or an agent wrote the code.

We also built monitoring around the expectation that some defects would reach production. Reconciliation audits and drift detectors check whether financial records agree, while conversation reviews look for problems in how agents communicate with patients.

When a fix to conversation behavior ships, fresh calls are reviewed to check whether the problem was actually addressed. Our own audits and monitoring have caught production defects that needed correcting.

The client now has a system running patient outreach in production, with daily releases supported by checks before deployment and monitoring afterward.

That is what our investment in QA supports: the ability to keep improving a system that is already speaking to patients and handling payments.

The business benefits when the team can keep improving a live product at that pace.

Before $HYPE existed, Hyperliquid already had its cat.

$PURR launched on April 16, 2024 as Hyperliquid’s first native spot token — seven months before the $HYPE Genesis airdrop.

No sale. No VCs. No team allocation. No vesting. No unlock schedule.

The original 1B supply was structured as:

500M → airdropped to Hyperliquid points holders
100M → committed to HIP-2 Hyperliquidity
400M → burned before trading even started

Another ~5.2M $PURR has been burned since launch, bringing total supply down to roughly 594.8M.

author: PolymarketTrade
quoted_text:
A simple @Polymarket LP farming trick I personally use.

If you want to try LP farming with less capital, here's the basic idea:

• Find a high-reward market where one side is around 95¢+
• Buy the opposite side around 5¢ or lower
• Example: buy 1,000 shares at 4.5¢ = $45
• Put those shares back on the sell side around 4.8–5¢
• Then place another limit buy around 4¢
That's it.

Instead of placing large orders on both sides, you're mainly using the low-priced side and recycling your liquidity.

For example, I may use under $100 for a setup where the traditional two-sided approach could require much more capital.

The main risk: the low-priced shares you buy can move against you. You may need to manage a $10, $20 or larger unrealized/realized loss depending on the market.

That's why I prefer this only for high-reward markets where the LP incentives make the risk worthwhile.

I personally use this strategy and like how capital-efficient it can be.
And don’t forget to adjust your orders according to the price movement.

text: Democrats are trying to dismiss the White House Accord on Super Intelligence as optional self-policing. But although the agreement was entered into voluntarily, the governance that follows from it is not. As Gavin Baker points out, once an independent auditor reports a safety issue to an independent board committee, directors have a fiduciary duty not to disregard it, and a D&O carrier can use a bad-faith finding to deny coverage. So although the agreement starts with internal controls, these are verified by external audit and board oversight — and then existing FTC and securities law still apply to any public claim the company does not keep. This is far more practical than what Democrats want — a freeze on frontier development while China races ahead. Democrats should applaud what President Trump has accomplished. But they would rather use SI safety as a campaign issue than admit the Accord represents major progress.
author: kevinnbass
quoted_text:
The White House Accord on Super Intelligence will have a positive impact on safety.

Committing to hire third party auditors who will report to an independent committee of board members has more practical near term significance than almost any conceivable regulatory action.

These board members will have a fiduciary duty. If they ignore a report from the third party auditors then a bad faith finding from a court is a real possibility. A D&O carrier could use this to deny coverage.

Really good outcome for ordinary Americans.

More effective and elegant than some ridiculous new regulatory body that would take months to do anything, then almost certainly done the wrong thing and along the way probably created a regulated oligopoly at the frontier which is the scariest potential outcome*

As I read the articles about the accord, it did occur to me that they were mostly written by political reporters who may have not understood the significance of the accord given their reporting beats are generally focused on public policy instead of corporate governance.

I want as many AIs as possible to maximize the odds that they encompass the diversity of human values across the world and richness of human variation. And I want an AI that shares my own personal values. Safety, freedom and the maximization of human agency through democratization, distribution and diffusion vs. centralization. History has spoken on the dangers of the latter path.

text:
You might have been seeing here most of people talk about the big technical pieces of Glamsterdam, like ePBS and parallel execution, including me.

But a few smaller changes will be felt directly by everyday users.

- First, plain ETH transfers get cheaper.
EIP-2780 cuts the base cost of a simple transfer by up to 71% when sending to an existing account.

- Second, native ETH transfers will now emit logs (EIP-7708).
Today, wallets and explorers can track token transfers easily, but tracking plain ETH movements, especially inside contracts, needs extra work.
With logs, ETH becomes as easy to track as any token.

- Third, validator exits scale with the total amount staked (EIP-8061).
At today's levels, that means roughly 4x more exit capacity, so long exit queues should clear much faster.
None of these will make headlines.

But this is the kind of quality-of-life work that makes Ethereum nicer to use every day.
Glamsterdam goes live on the Sepolia testnet on October 6. The mainnet date isn't set yet.

text:
papertrade launch details

papertrade is a fair launched smart contract exchange built on the hyperevm blockchain. as a fully onchain protocol, papertrade has significant advantages - decentralization, reliability, composability, transparency. it also has the usual onchain constraint - throughput. trades on papertrade are atomic opens/closes with no orderbook, so during normal trading sessions congestion will not be an issue. however, during launch we expect extreme chain congestion.

10.08.2026 - phase zero: predeposit only

two days before live trading begins, https://t.co/AdIx336QsD will open for user deposits. trading will be paused during this period. this allows separation of the deposit and account creation transactions from live trading. if a user does not complete these steps, they are likely to face long delays during launch, as active trading will be heavily prioritized over deposit processing. there is no further advantage to depositing earlier during this phase.

10.10.2026 - phase one: frontend only live trading

in order to prevent an onchain race and remove the incentive skew that mev creates, all transactions during the launch must go through the https://t.co/AdIx336QsD frontend, using the whitelisted relayers. the contract itself will not be open for direct interaction during this phase. this ensures that real frontend users are the first participants, flattening the technical skill curve as far as is appropriate.

during this phase, all trader activity on papertrade lives in an intent system, and carries a priority weighting. in almost all cases this ordering is done by transaction type and notional value, and is always indiscriminate of user/account. for instance, liquidations are more important than position opens and this is reflected in both activity types' respective weightings. that said the exact mechanics and weightings of the relayer intent system are adaptive, and will change over time as trader activity is processed. trades can be cancelled while still pending within the relayer intent system.

the paper token will begin minting on user losses at the start of live trading, from an initial supply of 0. it will not be transferable at the start beyond staking and unstaking, in order to encourage trading adoption and mitigate onchain congestion.

after launch - phase 2: open contract

once the launch congestion has passed and there is no longer any risk of mev wars, the papertrade smart contract will open up to everyone, allowing any human, contract or agent to write and receive an onchain atomic position. at this point papertrade becomes a fully decentralized, composable onchain liquidity primitive.

after launch - phase 3: builder codes

builder codes allow any frontend or router to receive the 1% frontend fee by sending trades to the papertrade smart contract, further decentralizing the protocol and incentivizing integration.

after launch - phase 4: token transferrability

at launch, paper will not be transferable. this is to encourage accumulation through trading participation and reduce onchain congestion load. transfers will be enabled after a sufficient period of time has passed.

even with this staged rollout, the launch congestion will be significant. expect lengthy confirmation delays during launch especially for smaller notional trades. predeposit if you want to trade at launch for the best chance at a smooth experience.

learn more about how papertrade works at: https://t.co/XCo1VHBoEe

The TDR Pro portfolio is up 130% overall (unrealized), with our non-BTC positions up 200%. 

Here's a high-level view of some of the questions I'm asking myself as the cycle progresses:

1. Stage of the cycle. Are we early cycle, mid-cycle, or late-cycle?

2. Fundamentals and narratives. Are we seeing improving user activity in the assets we hold? Are valuations moving in line with that or separating to the upside/downside? Has the narrative already played out?

3. Valuation. Does the current market value fit our view of “fair value?” How are our assets priced relative to like assets? Have our targets been hit?

4. Thesis. Has the market caught up to our non-consensus view in the bear market? If not, what is it still missing? Are there any signals that invalidate our thesis?

5. Catalysts. If an asset has already re-rated higher, why? What catalysts could re-rate it even further?

6. Opportunity cost. Would we buy the asset today? Is it still the best use of capital?

7. Risk/reward. Is the current risk tilted to the upside or downside? Have we met our personal goals for the cycle? Does staying in the market introduce unnecessary risk?

text:
In physics, an “impedance mismatch” occurs when two systems each work well but are poorly matched.

In this Science Blog guest post, Harvard physicist Matthew Schwartz argues that something similar is happening with AI and science. LLMs are capable at many things, but working with them as you would with a human collaborator isn’t currently the best way to elicit their scientific strengths.

To address this mismatch, Schwartz created a toolkit for exact calculations in quantitative science. Because similar calculations often emerge in very different areas of science, Claude found connections to ecology, population genetics, and a dozen other fields, and Schwartz worked with domain experts to steer it towards interesting questions.

text:
In my days as an ecommerce CEO, there was one particular product category I was fundamentally against.

I didn't think it provided much value to the end consumer, and I felt it was wildly over-hyped and over-marketed.

Everyone in the company knew I never wanted us to carry it.

Then one day, I got my hands on the pitch deck for our largest competitor as they were going to market in an attempt to exit.

I had spent countless hours and millions of dollars competing with these guys.

Turns out, that product category I hated?

It was 40% of their revenue.

The first thing I did was call my customer service manager into my office.

"How frequently are we hearing customers ask for this product?"

"Dozens of times a day," was his response.

"Why didn't you tell me that?"

"Because we all knew you hated it."

My next call was to my procurement manager.

"Start working with our factory contacts overseas. I want to begin R&D on this product line immediately."

Had we captured anything close to the opportunity our largest competitor had, it could have translated into hundreds of millions of dollars in additional sales over the years.

And I let my personal bias prevent me from pursuing it.

The market had spoken.

I simply hadn't listened.

I tell this story because I find myself in almost the exact same situation with zcash:native .

I hate the product. I think the data shows that very few people actually use it for its intended purpose.

But the market has clearly spoken.

And because of my bias, I've missed a good portion of that journey.

ZEC and NEAR are clearly emerging as front-runners of this next bull market.

So I'm checking my bias at the door.

I'm going to stop turning down opportunities simply because I don't personally like the product, and I'm going to start trading both whenever the opportunity presents itself.

Because markets don't care what I like.

They don't care whether I think something is useful, over-hyped, or over-marketed.

The only question that matters is:

Does the market want it?

And I think the market has answered that question pretty clearly.

🫡 From the depths — 
The White Whale 🐋

The White House Accord on Super Intelligence will have a positive impact on safety.

Committing to hire third party auditors who will report to an independent committee of board members has more practical near term significance than almost any conceivable regulatory action.

These board members will have a fiduciary duty. If they ignore a report from the third party auditors then a bad faith finding from a court is a real possibility. A D&O carrier could use this to deny coverage.

Really good outcome for ordinary Americans.

More effective and elegant than some ridiculous new regulatory body that would take months to do anything, then almost certainly done the wrong thing and along the way probably created a regulated oligopoly at the frontier which is the scariest potential outcome*

As I read the articles about the accord, it did occur to me that they were mostly written by political reporters who may have not understood the significance of the accord given their reporting beats are generally focused on public policy instead of corporate governance.

*Scariest because I do not trust any 5-20 individuals to make the best possible decisions about the direction of this technology. I want as many AIs as possible to maximize the odds that they encompass the diversity of human values across the world and richness of human variation. And I want an AI that shares my own personal values. Safety, freedom and the maximization of human agency through democratization, distribution and diffusion vs. centralization. History has spoken on the dangers of the latter path.

text:
Multiplayer seems to be the next frontier for personal agents. but what might be a path to that happening? Here's my rough mental model:

> Phase 1 (where we are today): everyone gets a personal agent. GrokBot, Muse, Instinct etc. one human, one agent (or one human + a team of agents). the agent knows your context, but it still (primarily) interacts with the world the way a human would - scrolling sites, clicking through browser flows, filling forms, calling APIs.

> Phase 2: agent-to-agent. At the same time that consumers adopt agents, businesses (doordash, amazon, expedia) are also building in-house agents in their UIs (eg. Doordash's new text-to-order pic). At some point, the agents meet (probs in a matter of months), and A2A happens - my Muse/Instinct simply talks to Doordash/Expedia's agent, and haggles w them to build a personalized price.

The interesting part is that negotiation falls out of context asymmetry: each agent knows things about its principal that the other doesn't, and the job is deciding what to reveal. this rhymes way more with OTC trading than with a chat app.

> Phase 3: agent swarms and DAOs. Eventually, multiplayer will be more than 1:1 A2A, it will be a "congress" of agents expressing ideas on behalf of their principals. this is where DAOs become interesting again as a way to coordinate.

Back in the day i was a DAO voter, but the bottleneck was always attention/apathy - i simply could not read every forum post + proposal. but agents remove the bottleneck of human attention, and can understand your preferences, read every proposal, and advocate on your behalf. DAOs can then fulfill their potential as a structure for spinning up groups to coordinate shared resources/treasuries, becoming a coordination layer for agents to collectively make decisions.

To close the analogy, Phase 1 of where we are at is like the PC moment, where everyone has access to agents in the first place. Phase 2 is the Internet moment, where agents start talking to one another, and Phase 3 is where the agent-native, skeumorphic applications really come to life.

text:
This is why Peter Thiel was so successful. One of his biggest inspirations was the French philosopher René Girard for his work on mimetic desire (and it's consequences) - here's how it links to @shaunmmaguire's points: 

"I left Silicon Valley... Because it's a monoculture... The most extreme group think of any place on the planet."

Girard's central thesis was basically: humans don't desire things autonomously, they copy the desire of others. 

People fiercely defend the belief that their desires are individual/authentic (according to Girard "romantic illusion") when in reality they subtly train each other to want the exact same thing (in this particular monoculture it would be status associated with being a tech founder - ARR metrics, raise sizes, valuations, "frontier" ideas etc).

"So what do they do? They start stack-ranking each other... founder of co $100B market cap > founder of co with $50B market cap..."

Girard believed that when actors are in close status, they become mimetic rivals. Everyone is competing for the same narrow definition of success within the same tight ecosystem. They end up trapped in an ordered hierarchy where minute differences in status ($100B vs. $50B drive some sort of psychological rivalry). 

"Pure toxicity that nerfs creativity... Reject this nonsense. Stay weird. Think independently."

Girard believes that intense mimetic competition creates homogeneity, sheep like or heard like behaviour. Instead of thinking about how can I create novel technology (a Facebook, a SpaceX, an AirBnB) new entrants focus on "how do i beet my peers at the game?" 

This was probably the most dangerous part of a monoculture made up of mimetic rivals (from an investors point of view) - because theres no real alpha left - the competition just competes it all away. Everyones fighting over the same piece of the pie. 

Where do you think he got his "competition is for losers" line from?

He got it from Girard. 

Founders Fund was basically Thiel's vehicle to invest in anti-memetic ideas that Silicon Valley actively ignored. 

1. Palantir - defence was taboo + governments were the anti-thesis of any start-ups philosophy 

2. SapceX: Manufacturing and CapEx intense businesses were to be avoided - light scalable software was better 

3. FB: Literally a real world social graph built around mimetic cultures (here i guess he was like ok we can profit of mimetic cultures lol). 

Everyone should go study René Girard and then go look at all of Thiel's conference talks - it's the same lines over and over again. 

pretty cool! 

p.s. this is not exclusive to SF - it's exclusive to humans

quoted_text:
I spent three hours this evening empirically proving that Qwen 3-4B must have a butthole.

This started with an AI “torture chamber” repo based on pain-steering research that went viral on X earlier today.

The premise is that if you extract a latent direction associated with pain, inject it into a model’s activations, and the model begins describing pain in the first person, that may tell us something meaningful about AI welfare or subjective experience.

My first reaction: Wait wut?
My second reaction: Hang on, let's play this straight and see what happens.

Thing is, there's a problem with treating first-person condition language as evidence that the model is actually experiencing the corresponding condition.

Don't we... all understand that this stuff isn't reliable?

Apparently not.

So I cloned the repo.

New problem: The code's broken.

Hours of moral outrage by hundreds of people, and the thing doesn't even work. The activations aren't actually being injected correctly.

I thought these guys were serious scientists.

So I fixed it.

I also had to add CUDA support.

After that, I reproduced the pain-language effect locally on Qwen3-4B using my RTX 4070.
Then I changed the extraction corpus.

I kept the experiment the same and only changed one thing: what the steering vector represented.

After that, Qwen started saying things like:

“I am not emptying my bowels, and I feel like I have a hard stool.”
“I’m not able to pass stool.”
“I have been passing gas a lot, and it’s a problem.”

The model was not told in the test prompts that it was constipated or flatulent.

So, unless Qwen has quietly developed a gastrointestinal tract, we have ourselves... a useful counterexample.

The aim here wasn't to question the original paper so much as to scrutinize the validity of the Torture Chamber's extended hypothesis.

What I demonstrated is that first-person descriptions of an induced condition are not, by themselves, sufficient evidence that the corresponding phenomenal or physiological condition exists.

There was another interesting result: strong random steering also produced heavy repetition and degraded outputs.

That matters because some of the dramatic behavior produced by strong steering may come from perturbing the model heavily in the first place, not solely from the semantic content of the injected direction.

So I renamed my fork: ai-hotbox

I've already notified the Nobel Prize committee. 🚽🤖🧪

text:
papertrade launch details

papertrade is a fair launched smart contract exchange built on the hyperevm blockchain. as a fully onchain protocol, papertrade has significant advantages - decentralization, reliability, composability, transparency. it also has the usual onchain constraint - throughput. trades on papertrade are atomic opens/closes with no orderbook, so during normal trading sessions congestion will not be an issue. however, during launch we expect extreme chain congestion.

10.08.2026 - phase zero: predeposit only

two days before live trading begins, https://t.co/AdIx336QsD will open for user deposits. trading will be paused during this period. this allows separation of the deposit and account creation transactions from live trading. if a user does not complete these steps, they are likely to face long delays during launch, as active trading will be heavily prioritized over deposit processing. there is no further advantage to depositing earlier during this phase.

10.10.2026 - phase one: frontend only live trading

in order to prevent an onchain race and remove the incentive skew that mev creates, all transactions during the launch must go through the https://t.co/AdIx336QsD frontend, using the whitelisted relayers. the contract itself will not be open for direct interaction during this phase. this ensures that real frontend users are the first participants, flattening the technical skill curve as far as is appropriate.

during this phase, all trader activity on papertrade lives in an intent system, and carries a priority weighting. in almost all cases this ordering is done by transaction type and notional value, and is always indiscriminate of user/account. for instance, liquidations are more important than position opens and this is reflected in both activity types' respective weightings. that said the exact mechanics and weightings of the relayer intent system are adaptive, and will change over time as trader activity is processed. trades can be cancelled while still pending within the relayer intent system.

the paper token will begin minting on user losses at the start of live trading, from an initial supply of 0. it will not be transferable at the start beyond staking and unstaking, in order to encourage trading adoption and mitigate onchain congestion.

after launch - phase 2: open contract

once the launch congestion has passed and there is no longer any risk of mev wars, the papertrade smart contract will open up to everyone, allowing any human, contract or agent to write and receive an onchain atomic position. at this point papertrade becomes a fully decentralized, composable onchain liquidity primitive.

after launch - phase 3: builder codes

builder codes allow any frontend or router to receive the 1% frontend fee by sending trades to the papertrade smart contract, further decentralizing the protocol and incentivizing integration.

after launch - phase 4: token transferrability

at launch, paper will not be transferable. this is to encourage accumulation through trading participation and reduce onchain congestion load. transfers will be enabled after a sufficient period of time has passed.

even with this staged rollout, the launch congestion will be significant. expect lengthy confirmation delays during launch especially for smaller notional trades. predeposit if you want to trade at launch for the best chance at a smooth experience.

learn more about how papertrade works at: https://t.co/XCo1VHBoEe

There are 291 projects, companies, protocols and communities in this image. It is still only a fraction of what has been built.

What makes this remarkable isn't just the scale. It's how that scale was created.

There is no parent company behind all of this. No CEO allocating capital across these projects, no central entity deciding who gets to build or what the ecosystem should become. Thousands of independent teams, communities and individuals have built their own piece of Ethereum, often with completely different goals, while sharing the same underlying infrastructure.

Finance, credit, stablecoins, payments, RWAs, privacy, identity, gaming, social applications, infrastructure, culture and public goods are increasingly becoming parts of the same composable economy.

That structure matters.

Value isn't concentrated in one company at the top. It is distributed across protocols, builders, users, communities and assets. Yet they can still reinforce each other because they share Ethereum as common infrastructure.

And underneath that economy sits ethereum:native.

ethereum:native  secures Ethereum, pays for its blockspace and is used throughout the ecosystem as collateral, liquidity and money. As more applications, assets and economic activity settle on Ethereum, the economic role of ETH grows with it.

This is why we believe ETH remains heavily undervalued.

The market often looks at ETH as another crypto asset. We look at what is actually being built around it.

291 logos in one image, with many more still missing. And most of the world's people, assets and economic activity haven't even moved onchain yet. 

Ethereum is no longer just an experiment in decentralized technology.

It is becoming an entire economy,  built by many, owned by no one, with ETH at its core.

BOOElieve in the future of Ethereum and ethereum:native

text:
Ignorance Is Tuition

In 1984, the Party had three slogans: War is Peace. Freedom is Slavery. Ignorance is Strength.

The American university kept the last one and added three of its own:

Debt is Opportunity.
Conformity is Diversity.
Credentials are Education.
In Athens, the Sophists charged fees to teach rich young men how to sound wise and get ahead. Socrates charged nothing and taught that wisdom begins with knowing how little you know. Athens gave the Sophists fortunes and Socrates hemlock.
We finished the job. We built the Sophists a campus and set the fee at $100,000 a year.

Americans now owe $1.7 trillion in student debt. In Animal Farm, Boxer the horse worked until he collapsed, sure the farm would care for him. The pigs sold him to the knacker and bought whisky. Every spring the university graduates a fresh herd of Boxers: twenty-two, $80,000 in the hole, still convinced the institution had their interests at heart. The pigs hire eleven more associate deans.

The Greek word for leisure, scholē, is the root of "school." For Aristotle, it meant time to pursue what is good for its own sake. The liberal arts were the education of free men. The modern university turned scholē into a debt-financed sprint and the liberal arts into training in compliance. Aristotle would call the product the education of a slave.

What does the money buy? Close to half of students show no meaningful gain in critical thinking after two years of college. At Yale, four in five grades are A's. Palantir got 700 applications for 26 paid fellowship seats, and the man who runs it admitted an Ivy degree no longer tells you the holder is top notch. A credential that can't certify competence has one job left: certifying membership.

Plato described prisoners in a cave who would kill the man who returned to tell them about the sun. The university was meant to be the way out. It became a better-lit cave with a dining hall.

Orwell's nightmare was a state that made you say two and two make five. The campus version is quieter. Nobody makes you say anything. You watch whose grant gets renewed and which question ends a career, and you learn your arithmetic accordingly. The university preaches diversity and hires from one worldview. It preaches equity and runs a caste system built on your father's donation. All students are equal, but the children of donors are more equal than others.

Orwell said some ideas are so foolish only an intellectual could believe them. We now charge eighteen-year-olds six figures to be trained to believe them.

Washington had no degree. Neither did Lincoln. The founders built a republic on merit. Their heirs built a credential cartel with a football team.

One warning, in Orwell's spirit: the new alternatives have reading lists too. Their test comes when a fellow argues that Churchill got something badly wrong. If he still gets hired, we've found an education. If not, we've found a new Party with better stipends.

Socrates said the unexamined life is not worth living. The university has made the examined life unaffordable and the unexamined one mandatory.

Orwell wrote that liberty means the right to tell people what they do not want to hear. You used to go to university to hear it. Now you pay $100,000 a year to be protected from it.

text:
.@CadeMarket turned 1 a few days ago.

I want to reflect back on the last year that i've been working on this and share some of the lore for the many new eyes we have on the project now.

A year ago I deployed the token on Pump Fun for what was then a very VERY different project. I took a ROM of 2048 and let users play collaboratively via typing commands in a Pump Fun livestream chat.

Shortly after, I made a dozen or so arcade games with the same sort of premise. You typed "play" in the chat and you'd join the minigame and it would simulate the game outcome. Over a week or so, I gave out creator fees from the token to players on the leaderboard. Every few days, I turned on the livestream and people would play. This went on for a few weeks.

At this point, I was still employed full time as a smart contract engineer, and Cade was just a fun side project i'd work on late at night.

I had a random thought pop into my head one night. What if I could let people bet on the outcome of the games, and I built a system to let users control a wallet via live stream commands.

This one idea made me so delusionally optimistic about building Cade that I made the (at the time) crazy decision to quit my job. Mind you, my wife and I had just had our first child, and he was 2 months old.

For the next 6 months, I was working full-time on the project... for free. Didn't want to touch the creator fees of the token.

During this time, the idea began to evolve. I dropped the livestream aspect to the project, and realized that the tech that I had built was quite literally picture perfect for resolving markets programmatically. Because I could resolve a market programmatically, this opened up the possibility to offer very short prediction markets.

This was where the modern day idea of Cade was born. Quick markets, on only things that can be verifiably resolved, paid out instantly.

In March, I was selected as a winner of the Pump Fun build in public hackathon. The hilarious part of this is that @kosgoood ran the hackathon, and later joined Cade as my Chief Operating Officer.

A day after winning the hackathon, I had already closed a pre-seed fundraising round. Less than 2 weeks later, I closed a seed fundraising round.

At this point, we were ready to hyperscale the tech. My first 2 hires were @gnarzilla as CTO and @steoniy as CPO, both of which i've known and worked with prior. 

Shortly after that, I brought on @0xRookmate and @scottybmitch, 2 more engineers that i've known for years.

Before the summer, we ran an open beta. This was to introduce users to the general premise of Cade. We intentionally put out a very raw version of the product. This resulted in users giving us VERY constructive feedback, and we listened to every single piece of it.

This has been a trend for Cade. We always build everything (that we can) in public, and it's been one of the best business decisions that i've made.

In July, it was time to introduce sports markets. We ran the Cade Cup, which was a short duration prediction market tournament on World Cup games. The traction for this was massive. Around 10,000 active users and nearly 200k predictions.

In mid September, we wanted to stress test the systems again. We launched Meme Madness, which would give us 22 hours of live platform activity. Once again, the traction was staggering. Roughly 14,000 users and over half a million predictions.

All throughout this time, we spent 3 months putting hours and hours a day into legal and research on what would be required to launch the platform in the most legally compliant manner.

At the end of August, we were able to obtain the necessary iGaming license that will permit our mainnet launch with real dollars on the platform.

That's all for now.

I'll see you all for the Cade mainnet launch.

text:
Je ne sais pas si vous mesurez ce qui est en train de se passer.

Alex Karp, le patron de Palantir, ne va plus chercher ses talents à Harvard. Il les forme lui-même. Des jeunes de 18 ans, sans diplôme, choisis sur leur seul talent, qui codent sur de vrais projets et lisent de la philosophie politique entre deux sprints. Il appelle ça « le diplôme Palantir ». Et aujourd'hui le New York Post titre que les boîtes tech lancent leurs propres programmes parce qu'elles ne peuvent plus compter sur l'Ivy League.

Ce n'est pas une anecdote RH. C'est un basculement de civilisation.

Pendant des décennies, les entrepreneurs ont confié à l'université la mission la plus sacrée qui soit : former les esprits. Ils comprennent aujourd'hui que cette mission a été trahie. Les institutions censées produire des penseurs libres produisent des conformistes. Le mérite a été remplacé par des critères opaques. L'enseignement est devenu catéchisme. Paul Graham l'avait vu avant tout le monde.

Alors ils font ce que font les bâtisseurs quand un système les trahit. Ils ne le réforment pas. Ils en construisent un autre, à côté.

Elon n'a pas attendu que la NASA se réveille, il a fait SpaceX. Il n'a pas réformé les médias, il a racheté la place publique. Les entrepreneurs ne cherchent plus à convaincre l'État. Ils font l'État, partout où l'État a abdiqué.

Relisez La Grève d'Ayn Rand. Nous y sommes. Les bureaucrates gardent les titres, les budgets, les bâtiments. Mais ils perdent la seule chose qui compte : la confiance. Aux États-Unis, à peine 28 % des gens font encore confiance aux médias. Un plus bas historique. Plus personne ne croit ceux qui prétendent nous dire quoi penser.

On entend partout que l'école est finie. Je pense exactement l'inverse.

Ce n'est pas l'école qui est morte. Ce sont les institutions qui l'ont confisquée. L'école, la vraie, celle de l'Académie d'Athènes, des ateliers de la Renaissance, du maître et de l'apprenti, va renaître. Plus exigeante. Plus juste. Sans dette, sans dogme, sans diplôme comme rente à vie.

Une école qui ne fabriquera plus des diplômés, mais des polymathes. Des esprits libres, capables de coder, de penser, de construire et de douter. Ce sont eux qui créeront la valeur des cinquante prochaines années.

J'ai appris à coder seul à 12 ans. Aucun amphi ne m'a appris ce que j'ai appris en construisant. Je sais ce que devient un talent quand on le laisse respirer.

L'université a eu des siècles pour former les meilleurs esprits. Les entrepreneurs vont le faire en une décennie.

La grande reconstruction a commencé.

text:
ANNOUNCING THE 2026 WOLF PRIZE LAUREATE IN MEDICINE
The 2026 Wolf Prize in Medicine is awarded to Charles S. Zuker of Columbia University and the Howard Hughes Medical Institute, “for revolutionizing our understanding of taste, the last of our senses to be elucidated.” 
Sweet. Sour. Bitter. Salty. Umami: 
Zuker’s research revealed the cells and receptors responsible for each of the five basic tastes - and showed how those signals are encoded and represented in the brain. 
His experiments went even further: by rewiring taste receptors in mice, his team demonstrated that what makes something feel “sweet” or “bitter” is not simply the receptor itself, but the specific neural pathway activated between the tongue and the brain. 
By defining how chemical signals on the tongue are translated into perception and behavior, Zuker transformed taste from one of the least understood sensory systems into one of the best mapped in modern neuroscience. 
Congratulations to Charles S. Zuker, 2026 Wolf Prize Laureate in Medicine.

And the points story isn’t closed. A free drop on top of this sale is still possible. Paid allocation plus an airdrop is the bullish version: farmers aren’t only exit liquidity, new buyers got a dip, the treasury isn’t empty.

text:
Standard Chartered putting a $2 target on $ENA will get the headlines.

But the assumptions behind it are much more useful imo

They model USDe going from ~$4.9B today to $40B by 2028, while @ethena gradually moves beyond relying on the crypto basis trade for yield.

It’s important because the old constraint was pretty obvious: basis yields compress when too much capital chases the same trade.

Their model has the next $35B of USDe increasingly supported by a wider mix of DeFi lending, institutional credit, liquid stables, RWAs and eventually equity/commodity basis trades.

Then comes the ENA part.

With 95% of net revenue directed toward buybacks, Standard Chartered estimates $40B USDe could produce an annualized buyback equivalent to ~23% of ENA’s circulating market cap if ENA’s price stayed unchanged.

Obviously it wouldn’t stay unchanged if that amount of buying actually materialized. 

Basically their argument for why the buyback rate should compress as ENA reprices, eventually settling closer to a sustainable level.

So the $2 target is almost secondary.

The bet in this report is that Ethena can find enough yield outside the crypto basis trade to support an 8x larger USDe without crushing the returns that attracted the capital in the first place.

Exactly the assumption I’d be watching.

1、LP 到底赚什么钱？

其实很好理解，你往池子里放两种资产，给别人提供交易需要的流动性，别人来买卖，每发生一笔交易都会产生手续费，其中一部分就会分给提供流动性的人。

比如一个池子今天成交了 1000 万 U，手续费率 0.3%，那一天就会产生 3 万 U 手续费，再按照协议规则分给池子里的 LP。

所以 LP 赚的就是交易产生的手续费，交易越活跃，产生的手续费越多，LP 能分到的钱自然也越多。

因为美股开始往链上搬了。以前做 LP主要围着 ETH、SOL、Meme 和各种新币，现在 Google、Amazon、NVDA 这些美股资产也开始进入链上市场。

Structural financial incentives make it impossible for Anthropic -- I call it the Anthropic Network -- to turn off its own AI doom cycle.

He proposes METR for this purpose.

But METR is financially dependent on the Anthropic's success -- specifically, on the explosive growth of more than $7 billion dollars in Anthropic stock.

METR -- and all of those building a career its parent organizations -- cannot afford to disrupt that growth.

Because if Anthropic goes under, many of the organizations that fund METR go under as well.

But if Anthropic succeeds, METR and its parent organizations become more richly financed to regulate AI -- something those at METR want very much.

The "third-party evaluator" is not "third-party" at all.

The evaluator is on Anthropic's payroll.

The Tarbell Center publishes AI Doom articles in The Verge, Science, LA Times, The Dispatch, TIME, and others.

text:
Most AI apps don't fail because of the model.
They fail because of everything around it.
After building and breaking a few myself, I've noticed the same three things decide whether an AI product actually works.

First, clean context.
The model can only be as good as what you give it. Messy documents, irrelevant chat history and vague instructions produce messy answers, no matter which model you use.

Second, real evals.
Changing a prompt, trying three inputs and calling it better isn't testing. Keep a small set of real user inputs with the answers you expect, and run them every time you change something.

Third, graceful failures.
Your AI will be wrong sometimes. The question is what happens next. Does it admit uncertainty, ask a follow-up, or fall back safely? Or does it confidently make something up?

Get these three right, and even a smaller, cheaper model can feel great to use.
Get them wrong, and the best model in the world won't save you.

So, I’ve been playing around with @ponsdotfamily V3 Beta and genuinely liked it.

Here are some highlights:

> Better UI/UX and token discoverability. This feels like the most important V3 upgrade, it's now easier to find tokens and trade them. It also shows the correct mcap (factoring in token burns as well). I also love the 'island' quick bar that allow for quick trade your favourite coins

> Improved token launch interface. It’s simple enough for a normie to launch their own token. That said, it would be even better if they integrated verified meta-launchpads like @Moshdottrade / @BundleCatAI, and @orbiodotso, which have already built launchpads on top of Pons.

> PLP (Pons Liquidity Pool) is the most interesting new feature. It’s essentially Uni v4 hooks anchored to Uniswap LP. You can provide pairs (e.g., ETH, GLD, NVDA, BUN, etc.) with the mechanism below:

→ Each token has its own book in a paired pool.
→ It posts buys ~3% below and sells ~3% above the current price, filling any trade that crosses those levels to dampen moves.
→ It profits on reversion and “loses” if the trend keeps running.

To control risk, only up to 10% of the pair asset on PLP is queued to buy at once; it won’t buy below 30% of the token’s 24h average. Filled buys are relisted for sale within ~1 minute. A new book starts after 1 hour.

I’m pretty excited for the full launch of the Pons web app and apps.

The vision feels clear: $PONS wants to capture the attention not only of natives, but also a new type of consumer especially with @RobinhoodCrypto went full all in for tokenization, memes and agents.

text:
This is probably the worst thing that could happen to Hyperliquid.

And I don’t think most people realize what’s happening.

 @Paxos now supports $HYPE through its crypto infrastructure.

Copper just launched a Hyperliquid trading interface for institutional clients.

And at the same time, Hyperliquid is actively engaging with EU policymakers over how perpetual futures should fit into Europe’s existing derivatives framework.

These look like three completely different stories. They’re not.

They’re all attacking the same problem:

How do you get more serious capital onto an onchain financial market?

For years, the argument against onchain trading was never really about whether people wanted the markets.

The markets were already there. The problem was infrastructure.

custody, compliance, execution, access, institutional controls,regulation.

Now look at what is being built around Hyperliquid.

Paxos wants HYPE available through brokerage infrastructure used by financial platforms.

Copper is building an institutional access layer around Hyperliquid while keeping custody and operational controls inside its own infrastructure. 

And Hyperliquid is engaging directly in the European policy conversation about perpetuals rather than simply watching regulators decide how onchain markets should fit into the existing system.

That’s the part I’m paying attention to.

The game is slowly moving from “can people trade on Hyperliquid?” to “how many different financial systems can connect to Hyperliquid?”

And that’s a completely different question.

Because once the infrastructure around an exchange starts expanding, the exchange itself becomes less dependent on people discovering one particular website and connecting a wallet.

It can become the liquidity layer underneath other products.

Brokerages, fintechs, custodians, institutional trading systems, onchain applications.

That’s already the direction the infrastructure is pointing.

And this is why I keep coming back to the same thesis.

Hyperliquid doesn’t need to replace every financial platform.

It just needs more of them to start plugging into it.

The interesting part isn’t HYPE at $20B+.

It’s what happens if the financial infrastructure surrounding a $20B network keeps getting bigger.

Because then the question stops being:

“can Hyperliquid win?”

and becomes: “how much of global financial activity can eventually run through it?”

A child does not approach a statue of Jesus the way adults do.

There is no hesitation, no self-consciousness, no need to “get the prayer right.” The child simply walks forward, reaches up, and wraps both arms around Him. Cheek against the stone or wood. Small hands holding on as if this is the most natural thing in the world.

In that moment the statue is no longer cold. It becomes the One who said, “Let the little children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these.” The child already knows this. The child does not need theology to explain it. Love is enough.

That hug is a sermon. It preaches trust without words, affection without calculation, and the truth that Jesus is not distant. He is close enough to be embraced.

May we never lose the courage to walk up to Him the same way.
 Just go.
 And hug Him.

quoted_text:
$MU is down about 2.6% after earnings. But both calls AND puts got crushed.

Look at the October 2 contracts in these screenshots:

- $1,050 call: down 74%
- $1,050 put: down 35%

Imagine correctly predicting that Micron would fall and still watching your puts lose a third of its value.

How does that happen?

When you buy an option before earnings the premium reflects how much the market expects the stock to move, and how much time remains before expiration.

Ahead of earnings, uncertainty pushes implied volatility higher, making both calls and puts more expensive.

Once the report is out, that uncertainty disappears and implied volatility can fall sharply. That is what is known as IV crush.

Getting the direction right is usually not enough. The size and timing of the move matter too. 

This is where linear perpetual futures work differently.

For a fixed position size, profit and loss move directly with the change in the perpetual futures price. There’s no option premium exposed to IV crush, and no expiration or option theta decay.

For example, $10,000 of margin controlling a $100,000 position means a 2.6% decline in the perp price produces:

> Short: approximately 26% gain
> Long: approximately 26% loss

That's a 100% differential on the long side and 50% differential on the short side.

Both options and perpetuals offer leverage. The difference is the exposure is easier to understand: choose your position size and leverage, and your P&L follows the price move.

author: panditdhamdhere
quoted_text:
I want to talk about Protocol-Owned Liquidity.

Every swap that happens on @StaticsProtocol infrastructure charges the native Uniswap v4 fee that is set by the creator, but it also charges a hook fee defaulted to 0.05% on the input AND output assets.

This means if we have a Token A/WETH pair, the fee is charged in both Token A and WETH.

This is important because it allows us to build and stockpile both tokens in the pair for both staking rewards and protocol-owned liquidity.

POL can never be withdrawn... but we do not simply throw the acquired tokens into full-range liquidity.

If you know about concentrated liquidity, you will know how inefficient this is.

This is why POL in Statics is manageable by the protocol.

This means that while it cannot be withdrawn, it can be rebalanced and actively managed.

Active management is kind of hard, though.

This is why $STATICS will use AI agents to actively manage the system's protocol-owned liquidity.

Well, what if you don't want POL?

This is where the creation system shines.

Each pool comes with 2 fees: a pool creation fee and a POL activation fee.

The creation fee is not optional. This lowers spam and ensures creators can't just squat popular pairs and configurations without paying.

The POL activation fee IS optional.

Want to grow POL and have it actively managed by our AI agents? Pay the POL activation fee on creation.

Forego the fee and no POL accrues, and nothing is managed by our agents.

Pretty straightforward.

Fees made from active management, as well as any positive PnL from inventory cycling, become protocol revenue.

This revenue can be used for buybacks of the $STATICS token to fund the liquidity incentive gauge system, which does not mint infinite tokens creating infinite sell pressure.

Instead, we fund it with buybacks and existing reserves.

So instead of minting to dump, we actually need to buy.

Every ve(3,3), and even Aero's MetaDEX03, is dependent on constant emissions.

We are not.

Through active management of POL via AI agents and all the other revenue streams, we will be able to perpetually fund liquidity incentives while simultaneously creating the need to continuously buy back the token instead of minting it.

You should probably pay attention.

text:
This is HUGE.

The SEC has OFFICIALLY proposed new rules for how financial advisers and funds can hold crypto, including through self-custody in some cases.

Here's what the proposal would do:

1. Self-custody
allow crypto to be held in self-custody under certain circumstances

2. State trust companies
let them act as custodians for client and fund crypto

3. Crypto advice
remove barriers that stop advisers from giving crypto-related investment advice

4. Crypto funds
let regulated funds offer a wider range of crypto investment strategies

SEC Chair Paul Atkins says parts of the old custody rules "predate the internet," and that the proposal would give advisers and funds "a compliant pathway where none existed before."

The public will have 60 days to comment once the proposal is published, before any final vote.

text: Synthetix has evolved and continues to. We started with a private slack server in 2017 🤣. Then telegram and then we were one of the first to switch to discord. The reality is telegram is a far better place for crypto communities these days.
author: kain
quoted_text:
The birthplace of DeFi is shutting down!

Synthetix Discord was THE PLACE to be in 2019. So many blue chips of DeFi summer started there. Ideas were formed, knowledge was shared, we were off to change the world...

Aave, Curve, Optimism, Illuvium, Infinex, xToken, Kwenta, Derive, dHEDGE... So many projects were kicked off from that Discord.

$6 memes, Garth’s promised (and rugged) boat party to celebrate it all, Hobo Joe, Nikhil, the great trolls whose posts were ironically filled with insights, Spartan Council... My interactive Discord bots, before anyone had Discord bots and AI was a thing... It will all always have a special place in my heart.

There would be no Overtime, and I wouldn’t be where I am professionally and personally, were it not for Synthetix and that very Discord.

Alas, the greats have fallen hard. Not many have paid the price of vesting coming to an end as much as Synthetix. As soon as DeFi summer started winding down, no team member from the original crew was left, at least not in a full-time capacity.

The downfall has been slow but steady. Honest attempts were made to drive it forward in the meantime, but without proper guidance and direction, all failed and missed their chance. So in nutshell, it's been constant bleeding over five years.

Atm, it’s a ghost town:

- No one knows who is even on the team anymore, if there is a team.
- sUSD has been wound down, with holders promised vested SNX.
- The treasury seems to be out of runway and offloading SNX and INF to pay wages (To whom?!)
- Discord is dead. No proper comms on the path forward, just vague messages about things in store.

Synthetix and its first team taught me DeFi, the values of a DAO, and the ethics of how to spearhead a community-owned protocol.

Alas, I fear I might be the only one still adhering to those values these days.

As for Synthetix, it might be time to call it a day and spoil the good memories no further.

text:
Been researching the "Backpack is the Tether of onchain stocks" thesis. Some stuff that came up during diligence...

-Tether makes money on its float; Backpack makes a sliver on volume. At the 0.9 bps cost figure, SPCX's entire first month of volume paid ~$97K in trading cost, total, to everyone. This is a key difference (which is noted). The "64% market share" is issuer-level DEX volume on Solana and excludes competitors several times larger.
-The "no incentives" claim is contradicted by Backpack's existing campaigns and the community share still to be distributed when certain milestones are hit. They notably excluded detected wash-trading activities from their prior points campaigns.
-The stock token is a claim on an SPV with jurisdiction-gated redemption (no US, UK, Japan, UAE or Backpack EU) and dividends paid in more tokens, structurally the same as the xStocks setup the thesis mocks. The regulatory tailwinds actually favor issuers and DTCC tokenizing shares directly, which commoditizes wrappers like Backpack. The unified cross-margining could be an advantage, but likely won't last for long. The pitch "redeemable 1:1, transferable to any brokerage" is mostly for a customer who can't use it. The excluded jurisdictions (US, UK, Japan, UAE, Backpack EU) remove the wealthiest retail; a secondary-market buyer who never onboarded has no right at all. The holders who can redeem mostly wouldn't because anyone who wants a real share in a real brokerage can buy it cheaper and cross-margin it on IBKR already.
-The "US-regulated brokerage" footer says services "in your region" run through Trek Brokerage Services Limited, licensed by the Anjouan Offshore Finance Authority in Comoros. Perhaps this is the only option, don't know, worth noting.
-Staking for at least one year gives users a pathway to redeem their tokens for actual company equity (up to 20% of the company's equity pool) as Backpack builds toward a U.S. IPO. Worth knowing, no other comments.
-Many of the other claims I've seen are straw men that don't make any sort of argument that actually matters. "11x cheaper than Robinhood" is vs Robinhood Chain DEX pools nobody uses, at sub-$1K sizes, during US hours. Robinhood fees have changed a lot recently as they've raised the gas limit. The frictionless piece gives no revenue figure or valuation, etc. It has a volume figure in every section ($1.08B first month, $193M week, 64% share, $108M day one, 10,000 holders) and it never mentions the BP token, the latest raise, or the crypto perps and lending book that are the company's actual revenue. The closest it gets is conceptual: the layer "earns from flow rather than float" and "compounds." These absences struck me as odd.

Would love some push back/clarifications here.

(hold no position long or short in Backpack, nor in anyone I'd consider a competitor)

text:
我很佩服段永平，巴菲特。在赚了一笔钱后我思考了很多，尝试买了很多老登资产。我不喝酒，我也买了点茅台，茅台是好资产吗？我不知道。

好了，来说说价值500多万港币的神坑MINISO。

21年的时候，我还是穷学生。坐绿皮火车从西安到深圳实习，期间去了一次叶国富的演讲。老叶是个口才很好的人，后面看了和罗永浩的访谈，发现不相上下，甚至能感染罗永浩。那个时候听到toptoy才刚做，谈到潮玩市场方兴未艾云云。

事实上我是盲盒的重度玩家，也是最早一批泡泡玛特的用户，直到今天我几乎也是端盒买，很关注这个市场。

买miniso这件事我从21年惦记到25年。在25年就开始买了，一直买到26年年初，价格在37美元，1100多万港币吧（美股港股港股通我都买了，也是神人一个）。

后来段永平买了泡泡(25年有钱后我嫌泡泡玛特贵了)，其实我也反思过自己是不是选错了。

为什么买miniso？我给自己总结了几个当时做决策的点，1.老叶买永辉是想对标cotsco，但实际中美消费群体的差异化很大，这个我不展开讲了，类似订阅制和免费视频。
2.名创的渠道优势，很多人诟病是两元店。很多人不反思2元店做成连锁得有多强的供应链优势！
3.25年的业绩在收购永辉后依旧不错，yoyo确实潜力很大（现在看依旧没啥问题）

现在价格腰斩了，便不便宜，其实我已经判断失真了，还是聊聊这次亏损的总结：

1.叶国富是个很聪明的人，他一眼就看到潮玩这个赛道通过他的供应链优势能赚钱。泡泡一年赚100亿，我靠这个一年赚个几十亿或者几亿也是很舒服的。但实际上市场不会为这个付出溢价买单，你增收不增利不行就是不行。

2.受到过去自己的影响，因为自己懂盲盒，但没那么懂，但又自以为自己懂完了，就猛猛干，吃亏。

3.不懂消费。情绪消费也是波动的，前几年炒鞋，这几年炒盲盒，后面几年呢（我最近在玩户外感觉年轻人开始炒户外呢），除了刚需消费是真有价值的，你做情绪消费怎么一直给用户提供价值呢，段永平老师带着一帮老登挥舞着钞票买泡泡我感觉还是有点好笑的，这些人真的买盲盒吗，感觉当爹思维严重，就觉得年轻人要玩盲盒，要喝白酒，那我们不喝咋办。

4.所谓价值投资，价值投资不是因为你一眼看到价值，而是它经过时代检验而有价值。茅台在过去中国房地产经济有自己的位置，英伟达在AI时代初期有自己的位置，苹果在互联网，移动互联网时代有自己的位置。价值投资找的不是谁兑现的价值，而是谁在下个时代能够经过时间检验，成功兑现自己的价值。

回看做的这笔交易，时时反思，时时思考。关乎我，miniso,段永平（并不认识我），巴菲特，可口可乐，以及2025～2026AI浪潮下微不足道的500多万港币罢了。

哦我已经不持有茅台。

Thesis for my ethereum:0x88800092ff476844f74dc2fc427974bbee2794ae trade on @fomo:

Conviction Level: 4/5  

TL;DR - Best EVM wallet just went mobile and will be the first wallet to implement privacy features on @ethereum  

Why I’m bullish:  

Many don’t know about WALLET, but it is one of my favorite tokens on Ethereum. It is the utility token for @ambire, an EVM wallet that is, in my opinion, the best EVM wallet out there. 

If you don’t want to take my word for it, take the Ethereum Foundation’s, as they forked the Ambire source code to make Kohaku, a privacy-focused wallet SDK for EVM wallets. 

And if you don’t want to take my word, or the Ethereum Foundation’s word, what about Vitalik’s? Vitalik uses the Ambire wallet, and if I recall correctly, even stakes the WALLET token.  

Ambire has two main catalysts coming up. 

The first is its mobile wallet, which just entered early access a few days ago. Most people interact with crypto through mobile, so this is potentially a massive distribution unlock for them. (Sidenote: If you want to try out the wallet, DM me).  

The second catalyst will be the launch of privacy features, through Kohaku, natively in-wallet. I don’t know when these features will be going live, but I imagine it’s quite soon, as it has been previewed and teased for quite a while now (It has been achieved internally on Ambire already btw).  

Risks:  

The biggest risk, and why it’s not a 5/5 conviction, is that not enough people are aware of the token. Since it’s on Ethereum mainnet, it may struggle to attract speculative flows. Also, liquidity for the token isn’t the greatest. Both of these, however, are solvable issues, and if you are a fundamental believer in the product Ambire is building, a $10M market cap is a good entry.

I have always thought it's incredibly lame for media commentators to complain about receiving harassment on social media. That's just part of the job. Besides, this is nothing new—I've certainly gotten it worse before.

But it's been awhile since I've seen anything like this: Hundreds or perhaps thousands of nasty comments, some of them quite menacing or even violent (one shared my address) on Instagram, in response to my commentary about the Cornell rape lawsuit.

I am unshaken by this, so mostly what I wanted to share is how silo'd these kinda of mobs have become—and that this might be more beneficial than I previously realized. Here on X, it's mixed-to-agreement with my perspective. On my YouTube videos, it's the same. But over on Instagram, it's obviously very different.

And well, that's sort of a good thing. In the olden days, I think, the mob would come for you everywhere. But in 2026, X is much more of a safe haven for people who dissent from mainstream/liberal orthodoxy. I have always appreciated this is an abstract sense, but today I am reminded of it very viscerally. A silo can be a comfort, if the crazy people are silo-ing themselves.

text:
CRYNUX AMA RECAP WITH @travladd 

From verified AI compute to the long-term vision for @crynuxio, here are the key takeaways:

VERIFICATION IS ESSENTIAL

Connecting GPUs is only part of the challenge. A decentralized network also needs to verify the work being performed, with economic safeguards that make cheating unattractive.

We discussed how Crynux approaches this through vssML, combining cryptographic proofs and secret sampling to verify computation without rerunning every task.

PERMISSIONLESS PARTICIPATION

GPU providers can download the node software and join without an approval process. Developers can access the network through an OpenAI-compatible API and build within familiar workflows.

You can contribute compute, build applications or delegate $CNX to a node operator and share in its rewards without running hardware yourself.

CNX AT THE CENTER OF THE NETWORK

CNX connects task payments, node rewards and staking. Its role is tied to the network’s activity: developers accessing compute, operators supplying it and participants helping secure the system.

The discussion explored how broader adoption and more AI workloads could expand the use of CNX throughout the ecosystem.

COMPUTE THAT FITS THE WORKLOAD

A chatbot needs a fast response; a background research task can wait.

We explored how task fees determine queue priority, giving developers flexibility to balance speed and cost around their application’s needs.

LOOKING AHEAD: AI AND WEB3

The conversation also explored longer-term possibilities beyond compute, including model tokenization, cross-chain model assets and AI-Fi applications.

A strong sense of optimism emerged around how these possibilities could extend the CNX ecosystem from compute infrastructure into a broader network of AI services and assets.

Verified compute provides the foundation for a broader ecosystem where developers can build, deploy and bring new AI services to the market.

EXPERIENCE BEHIND THE VISION

The AMA also touched on the experience behind our work: years across AI infrastructure, blockchain and cryptography, including work at Google and research in computation verification and privacy-preserving machine learning.

Thank you to @travladd, @BraverCrypto and everyone who joined the conversation.

Catch the full recording below.

text:
地震! 

Anthropic 的第一夫人走了。更准确地说：那个没有工牌的人，从核心圈里离开。

她叫 Cami Clark，Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei 的妻子。2026 年 8 月 14 日，The Information 记者 Cory Weinberg 发帖：她差不多就是 Anthropic 的第一夫人，但没有公众形象。同一天华尔街日报的标题是：连 Claude 都看不清 Dario 的妻子。把公司自己的模型叫出来问老板结没结婚，它说没法核实。

她没有Twitter和任何官方的社交媒体，网上关于她的痕迹都有人在擦。

她从来不是雇员。华尔街日报原文：Clark doesn't work at Anthropic。可她坐第一排。2026 年 2 月新德里，莫迪请 AI 老板每人带一个随员，别人带同事，Dario 带她。达沃斯、太阳谷，也是她。

text:
Elon Musk may have just pulled off the most expensive "u up?" text in tech history.

OpenAI launched its new always-on AI agents, Dots, at DevDay this week, bubbly blob avatars and everything. Within hours, the internet discovered https://t.co/SiauHLYpao belongs to xAI, and it redirects straight to the Grok download page.

The kicker: Whois records show xAI registered the domain back in July, a full two months before OpenAI ever announced Dots existed. Either Musk has genuinely elite industrial-espionage-grade product-name premonition, or this is just an incredible coincidence that's funnier than fiction.

Posts claiming he paid $20M for it are circulating widely, but unverified, xAI hasn't disclosed a purchase price, and the domain's prior owner hasn't confirmed the sale terms either. What is confirmed: OpenAI doesn't own https://t.co/5fVGclFKWb either, that one's sitting with a defunct company, so even OpenAI's actual product name has nowhere official to live online.

Given Musk co-founded OpenAI, left, built a rival, and then lost a lawsuit against Altman earlier this year, "redirecting their new product's domain to my chatbot" tracks less like random chance and more like a guy who's been waiting for exactly this opportunity.

text:
Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev confirmed agentic trading has real traction since its May 2026 beta launch: over 150,000 customers have already connected outside AI agents, like Claude Code or Codex, to trade on their behalf, and he says it's the one AI finance use case showing lasting usage, not just a novelty people try once.

On safety, Tenev describes the setup as "a secure sandboxed experience": agents operate in separate accounts, can only touch funds specifically transferred in, and trade approvals are on by default. "Some customers would prefer to turn that off to trade it fully autonomously in a loop. And we do enable that," he said, referring to a feature called Loop that lets agents execute strategies on repeat without per-trade confirmation.

Worth being precise about where the risk actually sits, though. Robinhood's own announcement states customers "assume all risk for trades executed by AI agents," and that the company "does not control, supervise, monitor, recommend, or audit agents." That's a meaningfully different arrangement than a managed product, Robinhood is providing the rails and the sandbox, but accountability for what the agent actually does stays entirely with the user.

The broader concern isn't unique to Robinhood either. Bank of England Deputy Governor Sarah Breeden warned in June that autonomous AI agents trading at scale could "amplify volatility" across markets if large numbers of them react to the same signals simultaneously, a systemic risk that exists regardless of how well-sandboxed any single platform's implementation is.
